column6: Zhōumò wǒmen qù le bówùguǎn.
column7: We went to the museum on the weekend.
column9: Counted with 座 or 家: 一座博物館, 參觀博物館. The Palace Museum is 故宮博物院, which uses 院. 博 is "wide", also in 博士 and 博覽會.

column3: A quiet room to read in on the spot, not to borrow from: 图书馆的阅览室, 报刊阅览室. The general word for reading is 阅读. 室 is a room, as in 办公室, 教室 and 卧室.
column6: Yuèlǎnshì lǐ hěn ānjìng.
column7: The reading room is very quiet.
column9: A quiet room to read in on the spot, not to borrow from: 圖書館的閱覽室, 報刊閱覽室. The general word for reading is 閱讀. 室 is a room, as in 辦公室, 教室 and 臥室.

column3: A loanword from "club", also meaning the premises: 足球俱乐部 a soccer club, 健身俱乐部 a gym, 加入俱乐部 to join. Here 乐 is read lè, "happy", not yuè, "music".
column4: 他加入了一个足球俱乐部。
column5: 他加入了一個足球俱樂部。
column6: Tā jiārù le yī gè zúqiú jùlèbù.
column7: He joined a soccer club.
column9: A loanword from "club", also meaning the premises: 足球俱樂部 a soccer club, 健身俱樂部 a gym, 加入俱樂部 to join. Here 樂 is read lè, "happy", not yuè, "music".

column3: The narrow alleys of old Beijing; 胡同儿 is how Beijingers say 胡同, and 逛胡同 is a typical outing. 同 is read tòng only in 胡同, and 儿 here is the suffix r, not "child".
column4: 老北京的胡同儿很有特色。
column5: 老北京的胡同兒很有特色。
column6: Lǎo Běijīng de hútòngr hěn yǒu tèsè.
column7: The hutongs of old Beijing have a special character.
column9: The narrow alleys of old Beijing; 胡同兒 is how Beijingers say 胡同, and 逛胡同 is a typical outing. 同 is read tòng only in 胡同, and 兒 here is the suffix r, not "child".

column3: In the city or town, as against the countryside: 城里人, 进城, 住在城里. The noun "a city" is 城市. The opposite is 乡下. 城 first meant city walls, which were made of stamped earth.
column4: 他每天从郊区到城里上班。
column5: 他每天從郊區到城裡上班。
column6: Tā měitiān cóng jiāoqū dào chénglǐ shàngbān.
column7: Every day he goes from the suburbs into the city to work.
column9: In the city or town, as against the countryside: 城裡人, 進城, 住在城裡. The noun "a city" is 城市. The opposite is 鄉下. 城 first meant city walls, which were made of stamped earth.

column3: Research institute on the mainland, and in Taiwan, "graduate school": 考研究所 "take the entrance exam for graduate school", 研究所毕业. In the mainland sense it is an institute, such as 语言研究所. 研 "to grind" and 究 "to look into" make 研究 "to research"; 所 is "place, institute".
column6: Tā xiǎng kǎo yánjiūsuǒ.
column7: He wants to take the graduate school entrance exam.
column9: Research institute on the mainland, and in Taiwan, "graduate school": 考研究所 "take the entrance exam for graduate school", 研究所畢業. In the mainland sense it is an institute, such as 語言研究所. 研 "to grind" and 究 "to look into" make 研究 "to research"; 所 is "place, institute".

column3: A base for military, research, production or training, usually with a modifier: 军事基地, 生产基地, 培训基地. 基 is a foundation, as in 基础 and 基本. 基 is earth 土 under 其: a foundation of earth.
column4: 这个城市有一个大型科研基地。
column5: 這個城市有一個大型科研基地。
column6: Zhège chéngshì yǒu yī gè dàxíng kēyán jīdì.
column7: This city has a large scientific research base.
column9: A base for military, research, production or training, usually with a modifier: 軍事基地, 生產基地, 培訓基地. 基 is a foundation, as in 基礎 and 基本. 基 is earth 土 under 其: a foundation of earth.

column3: Often shortened to 泳池. Measure word 个. 游 also means "to roam" (游玩, 旅游), but 泳 only appears in swimming words. 池 is a pool or pond, also in 电池 battery.
column6: Jiǔdiàn lǐ yǒu yī gè yóuyǒngchí.
column7: The hotel has a swimming pool.
column9: Often shortened to 泳池. Measure word 個. 游 also means "to roam" (遊玩, 旅遊), but 泳 only appears in swimming words. 池 is a pool or pond, also in 電池 battery.

column3: The area around a city: 住在郊区, 市区和郊区. 市中心 is the city center. 郊 is also in 郊游 an outing to the countryside and 近郊 the near outskirts.
column6: Tā zhù zài chéngshì de jiāoqū.
column7: He lives in the suburbs of the city.
column9: The area around a city: 住在郊區, 市區和郊區. 市中心 is the city center. 郊 is also in 郊遊 an outing to the countryside and 近郊 the near outskirts.

column3: Mostly bound: 家乡 hometown, 乡下 countryside, 乡镇 towns and townships, 同乡 someone from the same place. Alone it is a township, an administrative unit below the county.
column6: Zhège xiāng yǒu shí jǐ gè cūnzi.
column7: This township has a dozen or so villages.
column9: Mostly bound: 家鄉 hometown, 鄉下 countryside, 鄉鎮 towns and townships, 同鄉 someone from the same place. Alone it is a township, an administrative unit below the county.

column3: Neutral and a little written, set against 城市: 乡村生活, 乡村旅游 rural tourism, 乡村医生. 乡下 is the spoken "countryside", and 农村 stresses farming villages.
column6: Xiāngcūn de kōngqì bǐ chéngshì hǎo.
column7: The air in the countryside is better than in the city.
column9: Neutral and a little written, set against 城市: 鄉村生活, 鄉村旅遊 rural tourism, 鄉村醫生. 鄉下 is the spoken "countryside", and 農村 stresses farming villages.

column3: The classical Chinese garden with rocks, ponds and pavilions, as in 苏州园林; also 园林设计 and 园林绿化 landscaping. An ordinary garden is 花园. 林 is a tree 木 doubled, to give the idea of many trees.
column6: Sūzhōu de yuánlín hěn yǒumíng.
column7: The gardens of Suzhou are famous.
column9: The classical Chinese garden with rocks, ponds and pavilions, as in 蘇州園林; also 園林設計 and 園林綠化 landscaping. An ordinary garden is 花園. 林 is a tree 木 doubled, to give the idea of many trees.

column3: An expo or trade fair: 世界博览会, 汽车博览会 auto show, with 世博会 as the short form for the World Expo. Typical: 举办博览会 to hold an expo. 会 ends many event words: 运动会, 晚会.
column4: 这个城市举办过国际博览会。
column5: 這個城市舉辦過國際博覽會。
column6: Zhège chéngshì jǔbàn guo guójì bólǎnhuì.
column7: This city has held an international exposition.
column9: An expo or trade fair: 世界博覽會, 汽車博覽會 auto show, with 世博會 as the short form for the World Expo. Typical: 舉辦博覽會 to hold an expo. 會 ends many event words: 運動會, 晚會.

column3: Bound, found at the end of words for places that store things: 仓库 warehouse, 车库 garage, 水库 reservoir, 数据库 database; 入库 is to put into storage. One scholar links 库 to 车, a carriage: a storehouse for carriages.
column6: Huòwù yǐjīng rù kù le.
column7: The goods have already been put into storage.
column9: Bound, found at the end of words for places that store things: 倉庫 warehouse, 車庫 garage, 水庫 reservoir, 數據庫 database; 入庫 is to put into storage. One scholar links 庫 to 車, a carriage: a storehouse for carriages.

column3: A written word for "to ride", with a vehicle as object: 乘飞机, 乘船, 乘车; 坐 is the spoken one. Also "to take advantage of": 乘机, and in math "times": 三乘四. 乘 pictures a person 大 climbing a tree 木, with the feet visible.
column6: Wǒmen chéng fēijī qù Shànghǎi.
column7: We are going to Shanghai by plane.
column9: A written word for "to ride", with a vehicle as object: 乘飛機, 乘船, 乘車; 坐 is the spoken one. Also "to take advantage of": 乘機, and in math "times": 三乘四. 乘 pictures a person 大 climbing a tree 木, with the feet visible.

column3: Sounds more official than 坐车 and shows up on signs and in announcements: 乘车须知 riding rules, 乘车码 ride code, 买票乘车. Swap 车 for other vehicles: 乘船, 乘机.
column6: Xiǎohái chéngchē yào jì ānquándài.
column7: Children must wear a seat belt when riding in a car.
column9: Sounds more official than 坐車 and shows up on signs and in announcements: 乘車須知 riding rules, 乘車碼 ride code, 買票乘車. Swap 車 for other vehicles: 乘船, 乘機.

column3: Someone riding a particular bus, train, plane or ship: 全体乘客 all passengers, 各位乘客 in announcements. 旅客 is a traveler in general. 客 also ends 游客 tourist and 顾客 customer. 客 is a guest under a roof 宀.
column6: Měi wèi chéngkè dōu yǒu zuòwèi.
column7: Every passenger has a seat.
column9: Someone riding a particular bus, train, plane or ship: 全體乘客 all passengers, 各位乘客 in announcements. 旅客 is a traveler in general. 客 also ends 遊客 tourist and 顧客 customer. 客 is a guest under a roof 宀.

column3: Formal, for notices and announcements: 乘坐飞机, 乘坐地铁, 乘坐本次航班. In conversation 坐 alone is natural, and only 坐 works for sitting on a chair.
column6: Huānyíng chéngzuò běn cì hángbān.
column7: Welcome aboard this flight.
column9: Formal, for notices and announcements: 乘坐飛機, 乘坐地鐵, 乘坐本次航班. In conversation 坐 alone is natural, and only 坐 works for sitting on a chair.

column3: To drive or pilot a car, ship or aircraft, more formal than 开车: 驾驶汽车, 驾驶飞机. 驾驶员 is a driver or pilot, and 驾驶证 is the official license. Both characters have the horse 马 as their meaning part.
column6: Tā jiàshǐ zhe yī liàng xīn chē.
column7: He is driving a new car.
column9: To drive or pilot a car, ship or aircraft, more formal than 開車: 駕駛汽車, 駕駛飛機. 駕駛員 is a driver or pilot, and 駕駛證 is the official license. Both characters have the horse 馬 as their meaning part.

column3: Spoken short form of 驾驶执照 (the official name in Taiwan; on the mainland the card is 驾驶证): 考驾照 to take the driving test, 拿驾照, 驾照到期. 照 is a permit too in 执照 and 护照 passport, and a photo in 照片. 照 has fire 灬 under it and means to shine or illuminate.
column6: Tā gāng kǎodào jiàzhào.
column7: He has just got his driver's license.
column9: Spoken short form of 駕駛執照 (the official name in Taiwan; on the mainland the card is 駕駛證): 考駕照 to take the driving test, 拿駕照, 駕照到期. 照 is a permit too in 執照 and 護照 passport, and a photo in 照片. 照 has fire 灬 under it and means to shine or illuminate.

column3: The subject is a vehicle (a train, a car, a ship), never a person: people 走 or 开. It usually comes with a road or a speed, as in 在高速公路上行驶, and shows up on signs such as 禁止行驶.
column6: Huǒchē zhèngzài píngwěn de xíngshǐ.
column7: The train is running smoothly.
column9: The subject is a vehicle (a train, a car, a ship), never a person: people 走 or 開. It usually comes with a road or a speed, as in 在高速公路上行駛, and shows up on signs such as 禁止行駛.

column3: Motorbike, a loanword from "motor", short for 摩托车: 骑摩托 "ride a motorbike", 摩托头盔. Only the first two syllables of 摩托车 are used when speaking casually. In Taiwan a scooter is 机车, an ordinary motorcycle 摩托车, and a big, powerful one 重机 (重型机车). 托 has the hand 扌 and 乇 as sound (tuō), "to support".
column6: Tā qí mótuō shàngbān.
column7: He rides a motorbike to work.
column9: Motorbike, a loanword from "motor", short for 摩托車: 騎摩托 "ride a motorbike", 摩托頭盔. Only the first two syllables of 摩托車 are used when speaking casually. In Taiwan a scooter is 機車, an ordinary motorcycle 摩托車, and a big, powerful one 重機 (重型機車). 托 has the hand 扌 and 乇 as sound (tuō), "to support".

column3: Heard in notices and forms: 车主请注意. The same 主 names the owner in other words, such as 房主 (a house) and 店主 (a shop). A driver who does not own the car is just 司机.
column6: Chēzhǔ qǐng bǎ chē kāi zǒu.
column7: Car owners, please move your cars.
column9: Heard in notices and forms: 車主請注意. The same 主 names the owner in other words, such as 房主 (a house) and 店主 (a shop). A driver who does not own the car is just 司機.

column3: Someone who leads you along a route, such as a local hired for a hike or an expedition: 请向导, 当地向导. A 导游 is the tour guide who also explains the sights. Also the word for a setup wizard in software.
column4: 我们请了一位当地人做向导。
column5: 我們請了一位當地人做嚮導。
column6: Wǒmen qǐng le yī wèi dāngdìrén zuò xiàngdǎo.
column7: We hired a local person as our guide.
column9: Someone who leads you along a route, such as a local hired for a hike or an expedition: 請嚮導, 當地嚮導. A 導遊 is the tour guide who also explains the sights. Also the word for a setup wizard in software.

column3: More formal than the spoken 回来 and 回去. The place follows directly: 返回北京, 返回原处. Also the label on a screen or button for going back: 返回首页, 返回上一页.
column6: Tāmen míngtiān jiù fǎnhuí Běijīng.
column7: They return to Beijing tomorrow.
column9: More formal than the spoken 回來 and 回去. The place follows directly: 返回北京, 返回原處. Also the label on a screen or button for going back: 返回首頁, 返回上一頁.

column3: Before a verb, it says something went on the whole way: 一路说笑, 一路走来. The wishes 一路平安 and 一路顺风 are set farewells for a trip.
column4: 我们一路说说笑笑地回了家。
column5: 我們一路說說笑笑地回了家。
column6: Wǒmen yīlù shuōshuo xiàoxiào de huí le jiā.
column7: We chatted and laughed all the way home.
column9: Before a verb, it says something went on the whole way: 一路說笑, 一路走來. The wishes 一路平安 and 一路順風 are set farewells for a trip.

column3: Money you leave and get back: 交押金, 退押金. Typical for rented bikes, apartments and hotel rooms. A 定金 is different: a down payment toward something you are buying.
column4: 租自行车要交一百块押金。
column5: 租自行車要交一百塊押金。
column6: Zū zìxíngchē yào jiāo yībǎi kuài yājīn.
column7: You have to pay a deposit of one hundred yuan to rent a bike.
column9: Money you leave and get back: 交押金, 退押金. Typical for rented bikes, apartments and hotel rooms. A 定金 is different: a down payment toward something you are buying.

column3: What you say to the server when you cannot finish your meal: 请帮我打包. It is also used for packing goods to ship and, on a computer, for bundling files into one archive. 打 here is the light verb that forms many set phrases, as in 打电话.
column4: 菜太多了，请帮我们打包。
column5: 菜太多了，請幫我們打包。
column6: Cài tài duō le, qǐng bāng wǒmen dǎbāo.
column7: There is too much food. Please pack the rest for us.
column9: What you say to the server when you cannot finish your meal: 請幫我打包. It is also used for packing goods to ship and, on a computer, for bundling files into one archive. 打 here is the light verb that forms many set phrases, as in 打電話.

column3: A verb-object word, so the count goes in the middle: 出了一趟差, 出差回来. It is for work trips only; a vacation trip is 旅行.
column6: Tā xià zhōu yào qù Shànghǎi chūchāi.
column7: He is going on a business trip to Shanghai next week.
column9: A verb-object word, so the count goes in the middle: 出了一趟差, 出差回來. It is for work trips only; a vacation trip is 旅行.

column3: As a verb it takes the goods or a destination: 运货, 运到北京. Most uses are in compounds, such as 运气, 好运, 命运 and 运动.
column6: Zhèxiē shuǐguǒ yào yùn dào Běijīng.
column7: These fruits are going to be shipped to Beijing.
column9: As a verb it takes the goods or a destination: 運貨, 運到北京. Most uses are in compounds, such as 運氣, 好運, 命運 and 運動.

column3: The measure word for volumes of one work: 第二册, 这套书有三册. A single book is 一本书. It also ends words for small books, such as 手册 (handbook) and 相册 (photo album). It began as a picture of bamboo slips tied together.
column6: Zhè tào shū yīgòng yǒu sān cè.
column7: This set of books has three volumes in all.
column9: The measure word for volumes of one work: 第二冊, 這套書有三冊. A single book is 一本書. It also ends words for small books, such as 手冊 (handbook) and 相冊 (photo album). It began as a picture of bamboo slips tied together.

column3: Counts flowers and things shaped like them, especially clouds: 一朵花, 一朵云. A whole plant or tree takes 棵. Also in 耳朵 (ear).
column6: Tiānshàng yǒu jǐ duǒ báiyún.
column7: There are a few white clouds in the sky.
column9: Counts flowers and things shaped like them, especially clouds: 一朵花, 一朵雲. A whole plant or tree takes 棵. Also in 耳朵 (ear).

column3: Measure word for small round things: 一颗星星 "a star", 一颗糖 "a candy", 一颗心 "a heart", 一颗牙, 一颗珍珠 "a pearl", also satellites. It stands before the noun like 个 but only for small, grain-like objects. The word 页 on the right is the "head" radical, referring to something round like a head.
column6: Tā chī le yī kē táng.
column7: She ate a candy.
column9: Measure word for small round things: 一顆星星 "a star", 一顆糖 "a candy", 一顆心 "a heart", 一顆牙, 一顆珍珠 "a pearl", also satellites. It stands before the noun like 個 but only for small, grain-like objects. The word 頁 on the right is the "head" radical, referring to something round like a head.

column3: Counts horses and mules (一匹马) and bolts of cloth (一匹布); other animals take 只 or 头. It also means to match, as in 匹配.
column6: Cǎoyuán shàng yǒu jǐ pǐ mǎ.
column7: There are a few horses on the grassland.
column9: Counts horses and mules (一匹馬) and bolts of cloth (一匹布); other animals take 隻 or 頭. It also means to match, as in 匹配.

column3: Counts flat things hung up or spread out: 一幅画, 一幅地图, 一幅照片. As a noun it is a width, hence 篇幅 (the length of an article) and 幅度 (the range of a change).
column6: Qiáng shàng guà zhe yī fú shānshuǐ huà.
column7: A landscape painting hangs on the wall.
column9: Counts flat things hung up or spread out: 一幅畫, 一幅地圖, 一幅照片. As a noun it is a width, hence 篇幅 (the length of an article) and 幅度 (the range of a change).

column3: As a measure word it is loose and casual, 'a heap of': 一堆书, 一堆问题, and for people 一堆人 (a crowd). As a verb it is 堆在一起, 堆满 (piled full).
column6: Zhuōzi shàng yǒu yī duī shū.
column7: There is a pile of books on the table.
column9: As a measure word it is loose and casual, 'a heap of': 一堆書, 一堆問題, and for people 一堆人 (a crowd). As a verb it is 堆在一起, 堆滿 (piled full).

column3: Counts editions of a recurring event, after 第 and a number: 第三十二届奥运会. 本届 is this one and 历届 all earlier ones; 应届毕业生 are this year's graduates.
column4: 这是第三十二届奥运会。
column5: 這是第三十二屆奧運會。
column6: Zhè shì dì sānshí'èr jiè Àoyùnhuì.
column7: This is the thirty-second Olympic Games.
column9: Counts editions of a recurring event, after 第 and a number: 第三十二屆奧運會. 本屆 is this one and 歷屆 all earlier ones; 應屆畢業生 are this year's graduates.

column3: Chatty speech for a person's height or build (个儿高, 个儿矮) and for the size of things: 大个儿的苹果. In more careful speech use 个子 or 身高.
column4: 他个儿很高，打篮球很合适。
column5: 他個兒很高，打籃球很合適。
column6: Tā gèr hěn gāo, dǎ lánqiú hěn héshì.
column7: He is tall and well suited to basketball.
column9: Chatty speech for a person's height or build (個兒高, 個兒矮) and for the size of things: 大個兒的蘋果. In more careful speech use 個子 or 身高.

column3: It is followed by whatever covers the body: 一身汗, 一身泥, 出了一身汗. With a clothing verb it means a whole outfit: 穿一身黑. Also 一身轻松, 'feeling free of a burden'.
column6: Tā chū le yīshēn hàn.
column7: He broke out in a sweat all over.
column9: It is followed by whatever covers the body: 一身汗, 一身泥, 出了一身汗. With a clothing verb it means a whole outfit: 穿一身黑. Also 一身輕鬆, 'feeling free of a burden'.

column3: Before a verb it means doing something in one go: 一口气跑到山顶, 一口气说完. As an object it is a breath: 松了一口气 'breathed a sigh of relief'. 口 here counts mouthfuls, as in 一口水.
column6: Tā yīkǒuqì pǎo dào le shāndǐng.
column7: He ran to the top of the hill without stopping.
column9: Before a verb it means doing something in one go: 一口氣跑到山頂, 一口氣說完. As an object it is a breath: 鬆了一口氣 'breathed a sigh of relief'. 口 here counts mouthfuls, as in 一口水.

column3: Before the verb it says the change was sudden or all at once: 一下子就明白了, 一下子全忘了. After a verb, 一下 is a different thing: it softens a request, as in 看一下.
column6: Tā yīxiàzi zhàn le qǐlái.
column7: He stood up all of a sudden.
column9: Before the verb it says the change was sudden or all at once: 一下子就明白了, 一下子全忘了. After a verb, 一下 is a different thing: it softens a request, as in 看一下.

column3: As an opener it cuts to the decision: 一句话，你去不去? The same words can be literal, 'one sentence'. 一句话的事 means it is a matter of a single word, no trouble at all.
column6: Yījùhuà, nǐ dàodǐ qù bu qù?
column7: In a word, are you going or not?
column9: As an opener it cuts to the decision: 一句話，你去不去? The same words can be literal, 'one sentence'. 一句話的事 means it is a matter of a single word, no trouble at all.

column3: Follows the number directly: 五吨, 三吨水. 吨位 is the carrying capacity of a ship or truck.
column6: Zhè liàng kǎchē néng zhuāng wǔ dūn huò.
column7: This truck can carry five tons of goods.
column9: Follows the number directly: 五噸, 三噸水. 噸位 is the carrying capacity of a ship or truck.

column3: The old Chinese inch is about 3.3 cm, but photo and screen sizes use 寸 for the inch: 五寸照片. 尺寸 means the size of something. An old dictionary took it to mark the spot on the forearm where the pulse is felt, and the unit is said to come from the distance between the wrist and that spot.
column6: Zhè zhāng zhàopiàn shì wǔ cùn de.
column7: This photo is five inches.
column9: The old Chinese inch is about 3.3 cm, but photo and screen sizes use 寸 for the inch: 五寸照片. 尺寸 means the size of something. An old dictionary took it to mark the spot on the forearm where the pulse is felt, and the unit is said to come from the distance between the wrist and that spot.

column3: After a number: 十秒, or with 钟, 十秒钟. 秒表 is a stopwatch. In online slang it means instantly: 秒回 (reply right away), 秒杀 (a flash sale, or to crush someone).
column4: 他用十秒跑完了一百米。
column5: 他用十秒跑完了一百米。
column6: Tā yòng shí miǎo pǎo wán le yībǎi mǐ.
column7: He ran one hundred meters in ten seconds.
column9: After a number: 十秒, or with 鐘, 十秒鐘. 秒表 is a stopwatch. In online slang it means instantly: 秒回 (reply right away), 秒殺 (a flash sale, or to crush someone).

column3: January 1, a short public holiday. The Lunar New Year is a different day, called 春节. Greetings: 元旦快乐; the night before is often spent counting down, 跨年.
column4: 元旦那天，我们一起吃饭。
column5: 元旦那天，我們一起吃飯。
column6: Yuándàn nà tiān, wǒmen yīqǐ chīfàn.
column7: On New Year's Day we eat together.
column9: January 1, a short public holiday. The Lunar New Year is a different day, called 春節. Greetings: 元旦快樂; the night before is often spent counting down, 跨年.

column3: The night before the Spring Festival, centered on the family reunion dinner 年夜饭; many stay up late, 守岁. It is the eve of the lunar year, not of January 1, whose eve is 跨年.
column4: 除夕晚上全家人一起吃年夜饭。
column5: 除夕晚上全家人一起吃年夜飯。
column6: Chúxī wǎnshang quánjiārén yīqǐ chī niányèfàn.
column7: On New Year's Eve the whole family eats the reunion dinner together.
column9: The night before the Spring Festival, centered on the family reunion dinner 年夜飯; many stay up late, 守歲. It is the eve of the lunar year, not of January 1, whose eve is 跨年.

column3: The moon festival, when families get together and eat mooncakes 月饼 under a full moon. Often shortened to 中秋; say 过中秋节 for celebrating it and 中秋节快乐 as the greeting.
column4: 中秋节是家人团聚的日子。
column5: 中秋節是家人團聚的日子。
column6: Zhōngqiūjié shì jiārén tuánjù de rìzi.
column7: The Mid-Autumn Festival is a day for families to get together.
column9: The moon festival, when families get together and eat mooncakes 月餅 under a full moon. Often shortened to 中秋; say 過中秋節 for celebrating it and 中秋節快樂 as the greeting.

column3: Week and "Sunday" in speech, in southern China and in Taiwan, where 星期 is just as usual: 下个礼拜 "next week", 礼拜一 "Monday", 礼拜天 "Sunday". The mainland also writes 周. Its first meaning is "religious service", 做礼拜 "attend worship". 拜 is two hands 手 together in respect: "to bow, to pay respects".
column6: Xià ge lǐbài wǒmen qù lǚxíng.
column7: Next week we are going on a trip.
column9: Week and "Sunday" in speech, in southern China and in Taiwan, where 星期 is just as usual: 下個禮拜 "next week", 禮拜一 "Monday", 禮拜天 "Sunday". The mainland also writes 週. Its first meaning is "religious service", 做禮拜 "attend worship". 拜 is two hands 手 together in respect: "to bow, to pay respects".

column3: Weekday as opposed to the weekend 周末 and holidays. Common in rules and notices: 三个工作日内 (within three business days), 工作日不送货. In chat people say 平时 or 周一到周五.
column4: 工作日我早上七点起床。
column5: 工作日我早上七點起床。
column6: Gōngzuòrì wǒ zǎoshang qī diǎn qǐchuáng.
column7: On weekdays I get up at seven.
column9: Weekday as opposed to the weekend 週末 and holidays. Common in rules and notices: 三個工作日內 (within three business days), 工作日不送貨. In chat people say 平時 or 週一到週五.

column3: The written form of 今天, found in headlines, signs and announcements: 今日新闻, 今日有雨, 今日头条. In ordinary speech, say 今天.
column6: Jīnrì yǒu yǔ, qǐng dài sǎn.
column7: There will be rain today, please bring an umbrella.
column9: The written form of 今天, found in headlines, signs and announcements: 今日新聞, 今日有雨, 今日頭條. In ordinary speech, say 今天.

column3: A written, pleasant word for the first hours after dawn: 清晨的空气. The everyday word is 早上, and 凌晨 is the small hours after midnight.
column6: Qīngchén de kōngqì tèbié xīnxiān.
column7: The air is especially fresh in the early morning.
column9: A written, pleasant word for the first hours after dawn: 清晨的空氣. The everyday word is 早上, and 凌晨 is the small hours after midnight.

column3: A formal time word for rules and services: 夜间行驶, 夜间门诊 (night clinic), 夜间部 (evening classes). The opposite is 日间 or 白天; in speech people say 晚上 or 夜里.
column6: Yèjiān qǐng bùyào dàshēng shuōhuà.
column7: Please don't talk loudly at night.
column9: A formal time word for rules and services: 夜間行駛, 夜間門診 (night clinic), 夜間部 (evening classes). The opposite is 日間 or 白天; in speech people say 晚上 or 夜裡.

column3: A year as a unit of work, school or accounts: 年度总结, 年度报告, 财政年度, 年度最佳. To count ordinary years use 年, as in 三年, never 年度.
column6: Gōngsī yào xiě niándù zǒngjié.
column7: The company has to write an annual review.
column9: A year as a unit of work, school or accounts: 年度總結, 年度報告, 財政年度, 年度最佳. To count ordinary years use 年, as in 三年, never 年度.

column3: Before the new year: the weeks before the Spring Festival, short for 过年前 in speech: 年前把工作做完 "finish the work before New Year", 年前年后 "before and after New Year". Note that in 三年前 "three years ago" the 年 belongs to the count 三年, so that is not this word. 前 shows a foot moving forward on a boat.
column4: 年前我们要把工作做完。
column5: 年前我們要把工作做完。
column6: Niánqián wǒmen yào bǎ gōngzuò zuò wán.
column7: Before the New Year we have to finish the work.
column9: Before the new year: the weeks before the Spring Festival, short for 過年前 in speech: 年前把工作做完 "finish the work before New Year", 年前年後 "before and after New Year". Note that in 三年前 "three years ago" the 年 belongs to the count 三年, so that is not this word. 前 shows a foot moving forward on a boat.

column3: Looks back to a time that is now over: 当年他还是个学生, and 想当年 'when I think back'. It can also mean the prime of life: 当年的小伙子.
column6: Dāngnián tā hái shì ge xuésheng.
column7: Back then he was still a student.
column9: Looks back to a time that is now over: 當年他還是個學生, and 想當年 'when I think back'. It can also mean the prime of life: 當年的小夥子.

column3: The time one full round takes, for a plant, the moon, an economy or a product: 生长周期, 经济周期. 周期性 means periodic, and 周期表 is the periodic table.
column4: 这种植物的生长周期很短。
column5: 這種植物的生長週期很短。
column6: Zhè zhǒng zhíwù de shēngzhǎng zhōuqī hěn duǎn.
column7: This plant has a very short growth cycle.
column9: The time one full round takes, for a plant, the moon, an economy or a product: 生長週期, 經濟週期. 週期性 means periodic, and 週期表 is the periodic table.

column3: A literary, feeling-laden word for years passing over a long stretch of life: 岁月流逝, 艰苦的岁月, 岁月如梭. It turns up in songs and essays more than in plain talk.
column6: Suìyuè guò de zhēn kuài.
column7: Time passes so fast.
column9: A literary, feeling-laden word for years passing over a long stretch of life: 歲月流逝, 艱苦的歲月, 歲月如梭. It turns up in songs and essays more than in plain talk.

column3: Time as something we live through, usually pleasant and shorter than 岁月: 美好的时光, 时光飞逝. Written and warm; for plain time as a quantity, use 时间.
column4: 我们度过了一段美好的时光。
column5: 我們度過了一段美好的時光。
column6: Wǒmen dùguò le yī duàn měihǎo de shíguāng.
column7: We spent a wonderful time together.
column9: Time as something we live through, usually pleasant and shorter than 歲月: 美好的時光, 時光飛逝. Written and warm; for plain time as a quantity, use 時間.

column3: Said of the head: 他回头看了一眼. In chatty speech it also means 'later, when I get to it', without a time: 回头见, 回头再说, 回头给你打电话. 浪子回头 is a prodigal changing his ways.
column4: 我现在有事，回头再给你打电话。
column5: 我現在有事，回頭再給你打電話。
column6: Wǒ xiànzài yǒu shì, huítóu zài gěi nǐ dǎ diànhuà.
column7: I'm busy now, I'll call you later.
column9: Said of the head: 他回頭看了一眼. In chatty speech it also means 'later, when I get to it', without a time: 回頭見, 回頭再說, 回頭給你打電話. 浪子回頭 is a prodigal changing his ways.

column3: Both a noun (封建迷信) and a verb that takes an object: 迷信风水, 迷信权威. It is always critical, for belief with no evidence. Believing a person or fact is just 相信.
column6: Nǐ bùyào tài míxìn guǎnggào.
column7: Don't put too much blind faith in ads.
column9: Both a noun (封建迷信) and a verb that takes an object: 迷信風水, 迷信權威. It is always critical, for belief with no evidence. Believing a person or fact is just 相信.

column3: Gods and spirits: 拜神, 神仙, 神话. Colloquially it is also 'amazing, uncanny': 太神了! Elsewhere it means mind or look, as in 精神 and 眼神.
column4: 他们每年都去庙里拜神。
column5: 他們每年都去廟裡拜神。
column6: Tāmen měi nián dōu qù miào lǐ bài shén.
column7: Every year they go to the temple to worship the gods.
column9: Gods and spirits: 拜神, 神仙, 神話. Colloquially it is also 'amazing, uncanny': 太神了! Elsewhere it means mind or look, as in 精神 and 眼神.

column3: Beyond the ghost, it is a suffix for people with a vice: 酒鬼 (drunk), 懒鬼 (lazybones), and 小鬼 for a cheeky kid. 见鬼 is 'damn it', and 鬼点子 a sly idea.
column6: Xiǎoháizi dōu pà guǐ.
column7: All children are afraid of ghosts.
column9: Beyond the ghost, it is a suffix for people with a vice: 酒鬼 (drunk), 懶鬼 (lazybones), and 小鬼 for a cheeky kid. 見鬼 is 'damn it', and 鬼點子 a sly idea.

column3: A formal word of speeches and news, mostly before a noun: 当前形势, 当前的任务. Ordinary speech says 目前 or 现在.
column6: Dāngqián zuì zhòngyào de shì ānquán.
column7: What matters most at present is safety.
column9: A formal word of speeches and news, mostly before a noun: 當前形勢, 當前的任務. Ordinary speech says 目前 or 現在.

column3: The present age, contemporary: 当代文学, 当代艺术, 当代大学生. It points to the era we live in, whereas 现代 is "modern times" in a longer sense, since about 1919. 代 has a person 亻 and 弋 for the sound, and means "generation, era".
column6: Tā xǐhuan dāngdài yìshù.
column7: He likes contemporary art.
column9: The present age, contemporary: 當代文學, 當代藝術, 當代大學生. It points to the era we live in, whereas 現代 is "modern times" in a longer sense, since about 1919. 代 has a person 亻 and 弋 for the sound, and means "generation, era".

column3: A written, often emotional 'right now', usually opening a sentence: 此刻，我心里充满了感谢. 此时此刻 stresses it. Compare 此时, which is a time in a story, past or present.
column4: 此刻，我心里充满了感谢。
column5: 此刻，我心裡充滿了感謝。
column6: Cǐkè, wǒ xīnli chōngmǎn le gǎnxiè.
column7: At this moment I am full of gratitude.
column9: A written, often emotional 'right now', usually opening a sentence: 此刻，我心裡充滿了感謝. 此時此刻 stresses it. Compare 此時, which is a time in a story, past or present.

column3: Written style, placed before the main clause, for the time under discussion, which can be past ('by then') or present: 此时天已经黑了. 此刻 leans toward the feeling of right now.
column6: Cǐshí tiān yǐjīng hēi le.
column7: By then it was already dark.
column9: Written style, placed before the main clause, for the time under discussion, which can be past ('by then') or present: 此時天已經黑了. 此刻 leans toward the feeling of right now.

column3: Stands at the start of a sentence or before the verb, for the last few days or weeks up to now: 近来天气变化很大, 近来好吗? A bit more formal than 最近.
column6: Jìnlái tiānqì biànhuà hěn dà.
column7: The weather has changed a lot lately.
column9: Stands at the start of a sentence or before the verb, for the last few days or weeks up to now: 近來天氣變化很大, 近來好嗎? A bit more formal than 最近.

column3: Only before a noun, with or without 的: 现有的条件, 现有资源, 利用现有设备. It is what is at hand now; 原有 is what was there before.
column4: 我们要充分利用现有的资源。
column5: 我們要充分利用現有的資源。
column6: Wǒmen yào chōngfèn lìyòng xiànyǒu de zīyuán.
column7: We should make full use of the resources we have.
column9: Only before a noun, with or without 的: 現有的條件, 現有資源, 利用現有設備. It is what is at hand now; 原有 is what was there before.

column3: The standard word in news and reports for how things stand: 了解现状, 改变现状, 维持现状 (keep the status quo), 现状不容乐观 (the situation is not encouraging).
column4: 他对自己的现状很不满意。
column5: 他對自己的現狀很不滿意。
column6: Tā duì zìjǐ de xiànzhuàng hěn bù mǎnyì.
column7: He is very dissatisfied with his present situation.
column9: The standard word in news and reports for how things stand: 了解現狀, 改變現狀, 維持現狀 (keep the status quo), 現狀不容樂觀 (the situation is not encouraging).

column3: Works before 的 (暂时的困难) and before a verb (暂时不去). It only says it is not final, and is not 临时, which means makeshift or arranged on the spot, as in 临时工 (temp worker).
column6: Zhè zhǐ shì zànshí de kùnnan.
column7: This is only a temporary difficulty.
column9: Works before 的 (暫時的困難) and before a verb (暫時不去). It only says it is not final, and is not 臨時, which means makeshift or arranged on the spot, as in 臨時工 (temp worker).

column3: A slightly formal 'earlier', looking back from a later point in the story: 比先前瘦了, 先前的计划, 先前提到过. The everyday word is 以前.
column6: Tā bǐ xiānqián shòu le hěn duō.
column7: He is much thinner than before.
column9: A slightly formal 'earlier', looking back from a later point in the story: 比先前瘦了, 先前的計劃, 先前提到過. The everyday word is 以前.

column3: Sets how things first were against a change since: 原先他住在乡下，现在搬到了城里. Works as an adverb (原先以为) or before a noun with 的 (原先的计划).
column6: Yuánxiān de jìhuà gǎibiàn le.
column7: The original plan has changed.
column9: Sets how things first were against a change since: 原先他住在鄉下，現在搬到了城裡. Works as an adverb (原先以為) or before a noun with 的 (原先的計劃).

column3: Only a modifier before a noun, and it implies something has been added or changed since: 原有的设施, 保持原有风格. 现有 is what exists now.
column4: 他们保留了房子原有的样子。
column5: 他們保留了房子原有的樣子。
column6: Tāmen bǎoliú le fángzi yuányǒu de yàngzi.
column7: They kept the house's original look.
column9: Only a modifier before a noun, and it implies something has been added or changed since: 原有的設施, 保持原有風格. 現有 is what exists now.

column3: Sets the present against the long past, as a noun, modifier or adverb: 与以往不同, 比以往更好, 以往的经验. It sounds more formal than 以前 and 过去.
column4: 今年的夏天比以往更热。
column5: 今年的夏天比以往更熱。
column6: Jīnnián de xiàtiān bǐ yǐwǎng gèng rè.
column7: This summer is hotter than ever.
column9: Sets the present against the long past, as a noun, modifier or adverb: 與以往不同, 比以往更好, 以往的經驗. It sounds more formal than 以前 and 過去.

column3: Used for the first stretch of a longer span, such as a career, an era or an illness: 早期作品, 早期症状. The later stages are 中期 and 晚期.
column6: Zhè shì tā zǎoqī de zuòpǐn.
column7: This is one of his early works.
column9: Used for the first stretch of a longer span, such as a career, an era or an illness: 早期作品, 早期症狀. The later stages are 中期 and 晚期.

column3: The very first part of a process, project or period, shorter than 早期: 发展初期, 创业初期. It pairs with 中期 and 后期 for the middle and later stages.
column4: 工作初期遇到了很多困难。
column5: 工作初期遇到了很多困難。
column6: Gōngzuò chūqī yùdào le hěn duō kùnnan.
column7: In the early days of the job there were many difficulties.
column9: The very first part of a process, project or period, shorter than 早期: 發展初期, 創業初期. It pairs with 中期 and 後期 for the middle and later stages.

column3: Describes something in its first, untouched state: 原始森林, 原始社会, 原始数据. It can also suggest crude or undeveloped, as in 原始的方法.
column6: Zhèlǐ bǎoliú zhe yuánshǐ sēnlín.
column7: Virgin forest has been preserved here.
column9: Describes something in its first, untouched state: 原始森林, 原始社會, 原始數據. It can also suggest crude or undeveloped, as in 原始的方法.

column3: A written time word that looks back to an event just mentioned and opens the next clause: 此后再没回来过. In everyday speech people say 从那以后 or 后来.
column4: 他十八岁离开家，此后再没回去过。
column5: 他十八歲離開家，此後再沒回去過。
column6: Tā shíbā suì líkāi jiā, cǐhòu zài méi huí qù guo.
column7: He left home at eighteen and never went back after that.
column9: A written time word that looks back to an event just mentioned and opens the next clause: 此後再沒回來過. In everyday speech people say 從那以後 or 後來.

column3: Right after something just mentioned, often followed by 就 or 又 and used in stories and reports: 随后又说. It means soon after, not an open-ended later like 以后.
column6: Nǐ xiān zǒu, wǒ suíhòu jiù dào.
column7: You go first, I will be there right behind you.
column9: Right after something just mentioned, often followed by 就 or 又 and used in stories and reports: 隨後又說. It means soon after, not an open-ended later like 以後.

column3: Two uses: an adverb before the verb for events one after another (先后到达), and a noun for order or ranking (先后顺序, 不分先后 for no particular order).
column6: Tāmen xiānhòu dàodá le Běijīng.
column7: They arrived in Beijing one after another.
column9: Two uses: an adverb before the verb for events one after another (先後到達), and a noun for order or ranking (先後順序, 不分先後 for no particular order).

column3: Goes before the verb to say the action happened right there with no delay: 当场抓住, 当场表示, 当场承认. The scene itself, as a place, is 现场.
column4: 小偷被警察当场抓住了。
column5: 小偷被警察當場抓住了。
column6: Xiǎotōu bèi jǐngchá dāngchǎng zhuāzhù le.
column7: The thief was caught on the spot by the police.
column9: Goes before the verb to say the action happened right there with no delay: 當場抓住, 當場表示, 當場承認. The scene itself, as a place, is 現場.

column3: Pulling out something rooted or fixed in place: 拔草, 拔牙, 拔河, 拔插头. It also means to stand out or rise, as in 海拔, the height above sea level.
column6: Tā bá le yī gēn cǎo.
column7: He pulled out a blade of grass.
column9: Pulling out something rooted or fixed in place: 拔草, 拔牙, 拔河, 拔插頭. It also means to stand out or rise, as in 海拔, the height above sea level.

column3: Pattern: 把 + thing + 插 + 在/进 + place. Beyond putting things in, it covers butting in: 插嘴 (interrupt) and 插队 (cut in line), plus 插头 and 插座 for the plug and socket.
column6: Tā bǎ huā chā zài huāpíng lǐ.
column7: He put the flowers in the vase.
column9: Pattern: 把 + thing + 插 + 在/進 + place. Beyond putting things in, it covers butting in: 插嘴 (interrupt) and 插隊 (cut in line), plus 插頭 and 插座 for the plug and socket.

column3: Undoing something built or closed, usually with a result word: 拆开, 拆掉. It covers tearing down a building and opening a letter or gift (拆礼物). The opposite is 装 or 建.
column6: Tāmen yào chāi zhè zuò jiù lóu.
column7: They are going to tear down this old building.
column9: Undoing something built or closed, usually with a result word: 拆開, 拆掉. It covers tearing down a building and opening a letter or gift (拆禮物). The opposite is 裝 or 建.

column3: For something heavy, or carried by two or more people (两个人抬桌子), versus 搬 for moving things to a new place. It also raises a body part: 抬头, 抬手, 抬腿.
column4: 我们一起把桌子抬上楼。
column5: 我們一起把桌子抬上樓。
column6: Wǒmen yīqǐ bǎ zhuōzi tái shàng lóu.
column7: Let us carry the table upstairs together.
column9: For something heavy, or carried by two or more people (兩個人抬桌子), versus 搬 for moving things to a new place. It also raises a body part: 抬頭, 抬手, 抬腿.

column3: Steadying someone or something by hand: 扶老人, 扶着栏杆, 扶起来. It is not the general word for helping, which is 帮. It also gives 扶梯 for an escalator and 扶贫.
column6: Tā fú zhe lǎorén guò mǎlù.
column7: He helped the old man across the road.
column9: Steadying someone or something by hand: 扶老人, 扶著欄杆, 扶起來. It is not the general word for helping, which is 幫. It also gives 扶梯 for an escalator and 扶貧.

column3: A spoken word for tossing or throwing away: 扔垃圾, 把球扔给我. 扔 and 丢 both mean throw away, but only 丢 also means lose.
column6: Bié bǎ lājī rēng zài dìshang.
column7: Do not throw trash on the ground.
column9: A spoken word for tossing or throwing away: 扔垃圾, 把球扔給我. 扔 and 丟 both mean throw away, but only 丟 also means lose.

column3: Used with a direction word: 递过来, 递过去. It also builds 快递 (courier delivery) and 传递 (pass along).
column6: Qǐng bǎ nà běn shū dì guòlái.
column7: Please hand me that book.
column9: Used with a direction word: 遞過來, 遞過去. It also builds 快遞 (courier delivery) and 傳遞 (pass along).

column3: Pattern: 把 + thing + 递给 + person, with the receiver always after 给. It stresses passing something across, such as a table, where plain 给 only says giving.
column6: Tā bǎ bēizi dìgěi le wǒ.
column7: He handed the cup to me.
column9: Pattern: 把 + thing + 遞給 + person, with the receiver always after 給. It stresses passing something across, such as a table, where plain 給 only says giving.

column3: Gripping between two surfaces, such as chopsticks or tongs: 夹菜, 夹在中间. At the table, 夹菜 is also putting food into someone else's bowl. As a noun: 夹子 (clip), 文件夹 (folder).
column6: Tā yòng kuàizi jiā le yī kuài ròu.
column7: He picked up a piece of meat with chopsticks.
column9: Gripping between two surfaces, such as chopsticks or tongs: 夾菜, 夾在中間. At the table, 夾菜 is also putting food into someone else's bowl. As a noun: 夾子 (clip), 文件夾 (folder).

column3: For picking fruit and flowers, and for taking off things worn on the head or face: 摘眼镜, 摘帽子. For other clothes use 脱. It also means to excerpt, as in 摘要 (summary).
column4: 她在树上摘了一个苹果。
column5: 她在樹上摘了一個蘋果。
column6: Tā zài shù shang zhāi le yī ge píngguǒ.
column7: She picked an apple from the tree.
column9: For picking fruit and flowers, and for taking off things worn on the head or face: 摘眼鏡, 摘帽子. For other clothes use 脫. It also means to excerpt, as in 摘要 (summary).

column3: Stretching out a limb, often followed by 出 or 进: 伸手, 伸出舌头, 伸懒腰, 伸直. 伸手 can also mean asking for money, as in 伸手要钱.
column6: Qǐng bǎ shǒu shēn chūlái.
column7: Please stretch your hand out.
column9: Stretching out a limb, often followed by 出 or 進: 伸手, 伸出舌頭, 伸懶腰, 伸直. 伸手 can also mean asking for money, as in 伸手要錢.

column3: Holding with a closed hand: 握手 (shake hands, a separable verb: 握了握手), 握紧, 握拳. It also means control, as in 掌握 (to master).
column6: Tā jǐnjǐn wò zhe wǒ de shǒu.
column7: He held my hand tightly.
column9: Holding with a closed hand: 握手 (shake hands, a separable verb: 握了握手), 握緊, 握拳. It also means control, as in 掌握 (to master).

column3: A short, repeated blow: 敲门, 敲桌子, 敲鼓, 敲键盘 (type). In speech it can also mean overcharging, as in 敲竹杠.
column6: Tā yòng shǒuzhǐ qiāo zhe zhuōzi.
column7: He was tapping the table with his finger.
column9: A short, repeated blow: 敲門, 敲桌子, 敲鼓, 敲鍵盤 (type). In speech it can also mean overcharging, as in 敲竹槓.

column3: The door is already built in, so no other object follows; for other things use 敲 alone, as in 敲窗户. It is separable: 敲了三下门, 敲了敲门.
column6: Yǒu rén zài qiāomén.
column7: Someone is knocking at the door.
column9: The door is already built in, so no other object follows; for other things use 敲 alone, as in 敲窗戶. It is separable: 敲了三下門, 敲了敲門.

column3: Shaking the head for no, disapproval or helplessness; the partner is 点头 (nod). It is separable, so the verb can double: 摇了摇头. 摇头晃脑 is swaying the head in self-satisfaction.
column6: Tā tīng le zhǐshì yáotóu.
column7: When he heard it, he just shook his head.
column9: Shaking the head for no, disapproval or helplessness; the partner is 點頭 (nod). It is separable, so the verb can double: 搖了搖頭. 搖頭晃腦 is swaying the head in self-satisfaction.

column3: Waving to call someone over or to flag down a vehicle: 招手叫出租车. Waving goodbye is 挥手 instead. It is separable: 招了招手, 向他招招手.
column6: Tā xiàng wǒ zhāoshǒu.
column7: She waved to me.
column9: Waving to call someone over or to flag down a vehicle: 招手叫出租車. Waving goodbye is 揮手 instead. It is separable: 招了招手, 向他招招手.

column3: A separable verb, so 了 goes in the middle: 鼓了掌. Often 为他鼓掌 (applaud him), 热烈鼓掌 or 鼓掌欢迎. 鼓 is a drum 壴 with a hand holding a drumstick 支.
column6: Dàjiā dōu wèi tā gǔzhǎng.
column7: Everyone applauded him.
column9: A separable verb, so 了 goes in the middle: 鼓了掌. Often 為他鼓掌 (applaud him), 熱烈鼓掌 or 鼓掌歡迎. 鼓 is a drum 壴 with a hand holding a drumstick 支.

column3: Mostly looking up, with 看 after it: 抬头看, 抬起头来. The invoice sense turns up when shopping: the shop asks 抬头写什么, meaning what name goes on the invoice. 低头 is the opposite.
column6: Tā táitóu kàn le kàn tiān.
column7: He looked up at the sky.
column9: Mostly looking up, with 看 after it: 抬頭看, 抬起頭來. The invoice sense turns up when shopping: the shop asks 抬頭寫什麼, meaning what name goes on the invoice. 低頭 is the opposite.

column3: Verb and noun: 拥抱一下, 给他一个拥抱. Both characters mean to put arms around; 拥 also appears in 拥挤 (crowded) and 拥有.
column4: 他们热情地拥抱在一起。
column5: 他們熱情地擁抱在一起。
column6: Tāmen rèqíng de yōngbào zài yīqǐ.
column7: They hugged each other warmly.
column9: Verb and noun: 擁抱一下, 給他一個擁抱. Both characters mean to put arms around; 擁 also appears in 擁擠 (crowded) and 擁有.

column3: For people, speech says 站; 立 suits things standing upright, like a sign or a pole. It builds 立刻 (at once), 成立 (to found) and 建立 (to establish).
column6: Ménkǒu lì zhe yī kuài páizi.
column7: A sign stands at the door.
column9: For people, speech says 站; 立 suits things standing upright, like a sign or a pole. It builds 立刻 (at once), 成立 (to found) and 建立 (to establish).

column3: Written and formal; speech says 捡. It survives in 拾到 on lost-and-found notices and in 拾金不昧 (not keeping found money).
column4: 拾到钱包的人，请与失主联系。
column5: 拾到錢包的人，請與失主聯繫。
column6: Shí dào qiánbāo de rén, qǐng yǔ shīzhǔ liánxì.
column7: Whoever found the wallet, please contact the owner.
column9: Written and formal; speech says 撿. It survives in 拾到 on lost-and-found notices and in 拾金不昧 (not keeping found money).

column3: Verb and adjective: 挤公交, 别挤, 很挤. It also squeezes in time (挤时间) and squeezes out toothpaste (挤牙膏). 拥挤 is the more formal word for crowded.
column6: Zǎoshang de dìtiě hěn jǐ.
column7: The subway is very crowded in the morning.
column9: Verb and adjective: 擠公交, 別擠, 很擠. It also squeezes in time (擠時間) and squeezes out toothpaste (擠牙膏). 擁擠 is the more formal word for crowded.

column3: Often with 住 after it: 挡住视线, 挡路, 挡雨, 挡风. It is also a car gear (挂挡), and 挡风玻璃 is the windshield.
column6: Bié dǎng zhe wǒ de lù.
column7: Do not stand in my way.
column9: Often with 住 after it: 擋住視線, 擋路, 擋雨, 擋風. It is also a car gear (掛擋), and 擋風玻璃 is the windshield.

column3: The verb for pianos and guitars: 弹钢琴, 弹吉他; violin takes 拉 and flute 吹. It also means to spring or flick, as in 弹跳 and 弹性 (elasticity).
column6: Tā huì tán gāngqín.
column7: She can play the piano.
column9: The verb for pianos and guitars: 彈鋼琴, 彈吉他; violin takes 拉 and flute 吹. It also means to spring or flick, as in 彈跳 and 彈性 (elasticity).

column3: Either you fall (摔了一跤) or you throw something down hard (把手机摔了), so context decides. Often with a result word: 摔伤, 摔碎, 摔坏. 摔跤 also means wrestling.
column6: Tā bù xiǎoxīn shuāi le yī jiāo.
column7: He accidentally took a fall.
column9: Either you fall (摔了一跤) or you throw something down hard (把手機摔了), so context decides. Often with a result word: 摔傷, 摔碎, 摔壞. 摔跤 also means wrestling.

column3: For a person or animal losing balance: 摔倒在地. A tree or wall that falls is just 倒. It can also mean throwing an opponent to the ground, as in wrestling.
column6: Xiǎohái zài lùshang shuāidǎo le.
column7: The child fell down on the road.
column9: For a person or animal losing balance: 摔倒在地. A tree or wall that falls is just 倒. It can also mean throwing an opponent to the ground, as in wrestling.

column3: A hard hit, stronger than the lighter 碰: 撞车 (crash), 撞到, 撞见 (come across). 撞衫 is two people turning up in the same outfit.
column6: Tā qí chē zhuàng dào le yī kē shù.
column7: He rode his bike into a tree.
column9: A hard hit, stronger than the lighter 碰: 撞車 (crash), 撞到, 撞見 (come across). 撞衫 is two people turning up in the same outfit.

column3: Rolling: 滚下来, 滚走. As a rude command 滚！ means get lost. Boiling water in speech is 水开了; 滚 shows up in 滚水 and 滚烫 (scalding hot).
column6: Qiú gǔn dào zhuōzi xiàmian qù le.
column7: The ball rolled under the table.
column9: Rolling: 滾下來, 滾走. As a rude command 滾！ means get lost. Boiling water in speech is 水開了; 滾 shows up in 滾水 and 滾燙 (scalding hot).

column3: Adjective and verb: 路很滑, 滑倒. It covers sports (滑冰, 滑雪) and 光滑 for smooth. 滑头 is a slippery, sly person. Swiping a phone is 滑手机 in Taiwan and usually 刷手机 on the mainland.
column6: Lù hěn huá, xiǎoxīn diǎnr.
column7: The road is slippery, so be careful.
column9: Adjective and verb: 路很滑, 滑倒. It covers sports (滑冰, 滑雪) and 光滑 for smooth. 滑頭 is a slippery, sly person. Swiping a phone is 滑手機 in Taiwan and usually 刷手機 on the mainland.

column3: For leaving something behind: 把伞落下了, 落在车上, and 丢三落四 (forgetful). Here it is about forgetting to take something, not about falling.
column4: 我把伞落在出租车上了。
column5: 我把傘落在出租車上了。
column6: Wǒ bǎ sǎn là zài chūzūchē shang le.
column7: I left my umbrella in the taxi.
column9: For leaving something behind: 把傘落下了, 落在車上, and 丟三落四 (forgetful). Here it is about forgetting to take something, not about falling.

column3: Leaking of liquid, gas or information: 漏水, 漏气, 漏消息. Also missing something: 漏了一个字, 漏掉. 漏税 is tax evasion.
column6: Wūdǐng lòu yǔ le.
column7: The roof is leaking.
column9: Leaking of liquid, gas or information: 漏水, 漏氣, 漏消息. Also missing something: 漏了一個字, 漏掉. 漏稅 is tax evasion.

column3: The everyday word for losing things, with 了: 手机丢了, 把钥匙丢了. It does not mean losing a game; that is 输. 丢人 is to lose face, and 丢掉 to throw away.
column6: Wǒ de shǒujī diū le.
column7: I lost my phone.
column9: The everyday word for losing things, with 了: 手機丟了, 把鑰匙丟了. It does not mean losing a game; that is 輸. 丟人 is to lose face, and 丟掉 to throw away.

column3: Verb and adjective: 碎了, 打碎, 摔碎, 碎片, 碎玻璃. In 心碎 it is a heart breaking. In 琐碎 it means trivial.
column6: Bōlibēi diào zài dìshang, suì le.
column7: The glass fell on the floor and broke.
column9: Verb and adjective: 碎了, 打碎, 摔碎, 碎片, 碎玻璃. In 心碎 it is a heart breaking. In 瑣碎 it means trivial.

column3: Rotten (苹果烂了), cooked soft (炖烂), worn out (破烂), and slang for bad: 烂电影, 烂人. 烂醉 means dead drunk.
column6: Zhège píngguǒ làn le.
column7: This apple has gone bad.
column9: Rotten (蘋果爛了), cooked soft (燉爛), worn out (破爛), and slang for bad: 爛電影, 爛人. 爛醉 means dead drunk.

column3: Throwing out a whole basin or bucket of liquid in one motion: 泼水, 泼在地上. 泼冷水 means to dampen someone's enthusiasm, and 活泼 is lively.
column6: Tā bǎ yī pén shuǐ pō zài dìshang.
column7: He splashed a basin of water on the ground.
column9: Throwing out a whole basin or bucket of liquid in one motion: 潑水, 潑在地上. 潑冷水 means to dampen someone's enthusiasm, and 活潑 is lively.

column3: Liquids that spill or are sprinkled: 洒水, 汤洒了. Loose solids such as salt or seeds take 撒 instead, and learners mix the two up.
column6: Tāng sǎ le yī zhuōzi.
column7: The soup spilled all over the table.
column9: Liquids that spill or are sprinkled: 灑水, 湯灑了. Loose solids such as salt or seeds take 撒 instead, and learners mix the two up.

column3: Anything shot out in a stream: 喷水, 喷香水, 喷漆, 喷泉. It also gives 打喷嚏 (sneeze). Online, 喷 is to attack someone in harsh words: 被喷了.
column6: Shuǐ cóng guǎnzi lǐ pēn chūlái.
column7: Water is spraying out of the pipe.
column9: Anything shot out in a stream: 噴水, 噴香水, 噴漆, 噴泉. It also gives 打噴嚏 (sneeze). Online, 噴 is to attack someone in harsh words: 被噴了.

column3: Giving off or sending up: 冒烟, 冒汗, 冒泡, 冒出来. Also 冒险 (take a risk), 冒充 (pass oneself off) and 感冒 (a cold).
column6: Guō lǐ mào zhe rèqì.
column7: Steam is rising from the pot.
column9: Giving off or sending up: 冒煙, 冒汗, 冒泡, 冒出來. Also 冒險 (take a risk), 冒充 (pass oneself off) and 感冒 (a cold).

column3: Dyeing, and catching something bad with 上: 染头发, 染成黄色, 染上坏习惯. The noun side is 污染 (pollution) and 染色. It is built from water, a hook and a tree: something hung from a tree into water, so as to dye.
column6: Tā bǎ tóufa rǎn chéng le huángsè.
column7: She dyed her hair blond.
column9: Dyeing, and catching something bad with 上: 染頭髮, 染成黃色, 染上壞習慣. The noun side is 污染 (pollution) and 染色. It is built from water, a hook and a tree: something hung from a tree into water, so as to dye.

column3: Loose or scattered: 鞋带散了, 散装 (sold loose), 松散, and 散文 (prose). Breaking up or dispersing, as in 散步, 散会 and 分散, is the other and more common use of the same character.
column6: Xiédài sǎn le, wǒ jì yīxià.
column7: My shoelace came loose; let me tie it.
column9: Loose or scattered: 鞋帶散了, 散裝 (sold loose), 鬆散, and 散文 (prose). Breaking up or dispersing, as in 散步, 散會 and 分散, is the other and more common use of the same character.

column3: The thing taken follows: 偷东西, 偷钱包; having something stolen is 被偷了. As an adverb it means secretly: 偷看, 偷听, 偷笑, and 偷懒 (slack off).
column6: Yǒu rén tōu le tā de qiánbāo.
column7: Someone stole his wallet.
column9: The thing taken follows: 偷東西, 偷錢包; having something stolen is 被偷了. As an adverb it means secretly: 偷看, 偷聽, 偷笑, and 偷懶 (slack off).

column3: The spoken form with the 儿 ending; 小偷 is the plain word. Often with 抓: 抓小偷. A pickpocket is 扒手. Reports and signs also say 窃贼. The 儿 here is not a syllable of its own, just an r added to the sound before it.
column6: Xiǎotōur bèi jǐngchá zhuāzhù le.
column7: The thief was caught by the police.
column9: The spoken form with the 兒 ending; 小偷 is the plain word. Often with 抓: 抓小偷. A pickpocket is 扒手. Reports and signs also say 竊賊. The 兒 here is not a syllable of its own, just an r added to the sound before it.

column3: The person tricked is the object: 他骗了我, 被骗了, 骗钱. It is stronger than 说谎 (lie), since someone loses out. A swindler is 骗子.
column6: Bié bèi tā piàn le.
column7: Do not be fooled by him.
column9: The person tricked is the object: 他騙了我, 被騙了, 騙錢. It is stronger than 說謊 (lie), since someone loses out. A swindler is 騙子.

column3: The neutral-tone 子 turns the act of 骗 into a type of person, as in 傻子. It is blunt, a real accusation. Fraud as a crime is 诈骗, as in 诈骗电话.
column6: Tā shì ge piànzi, bié xiāngxìn tā.
column7: He is a cheat, so don't trust him.
column9: The neutral-tone 子 turns the act of 騙 into a type of person, as in 傻子. It is blunt, a real accusation. Fraud as a crime is 詐騙, as in 詐騙電話.

column3: It covers both crime and competition: 抢钱 and 抢包 are robbery, but 抢座位, 抢票 and 抢红包 (grabbing digital red envelopes) are just a race. Before a verb, 抢着说 means rushing to speak first; 抢劫 is the formal word for robbery.
column6: Yǒu rén qiǎng le tā de bāo.
column7: Someone snatched her bag.
column9: It covers both crime and competition: 搶錢 and 搶包 are robbery, but 搶座位, 搶票 and 搶紅包 (grabbing digital red envelopes) are just a race. Before a verb, 搶著說 means rushing to speak first; 搶劫 is the formal word for robbery.

column3: A verb plus object, so the other person comes with 跟 and a count goes in the middle: 跟人打架, 打了一架. It means a physical fight; a quarrel with words is 吵架.
column4: 两个男孩在操场上打架。
column5: 兩個男孩在操場上打架。
column6: Liǎng ge nánhái zài cāochǎng shang dǎjià.
column7: Two boys are fighting on the playground.
column9: A verb plus object, so the other person comes with 跟 and a count goes in the middle: 跟人打架, 打了一架. It means a physical fight; a quarrel with words is 吵架.

column3: Both verb and noun: 打击犯罪 cracks down on crime, 受到打击 is to take a blow, often an emotional one. In 打击乐 it names percussion. 击 is read jí in Taiwan.
column4: 失败对他是很大的打击。
column5: 失敗對他是很大的打擊。
column6: Shībài duì tā shì hěn dà de dǎjī.
column7: Failure was a heavy blow to him.
column9: Both verb and noun: 打擊犯罪 cracks down on crime, 受到打擊 is to take a blow, often an emotional one. In 打擊樂 it names percussion. 擊 is read jí in Taiwan.

column3: What you burst through is the object: 闯红灯, 闯进来. It also means to go out and make your own way, as in 闯天下, and 闯祸 is to stir up trouble. It is drawn as a horse rushing through a gate.
column6: Tā chuǎng hóngdēng bèi fákuǎn le.
column7: He was fined for running a red light.
column9: What you burst through is the object: 闖紅燈, 闖進來. It also means to go out and make your own way, as in 闖天下, and 闖禍 is to stir up trouble. It is drawn as a horse rushing through a gate.

column3: Often followed by what you flee: 逃命, 逃学 (skip school), 逃税 (evade taxes), or a place with a direction word: 逃出监狱. For plain running away, 逃跑 and 逃走 are the common two-character forms.
column6: Nàge xiǎotōu táo le.
column7: That thief got away.
column9: Often followed by what you flee: 逃命, 逃學 (skip school), 逃稅 (evade taxes), or a place with a direction word: 逃出監獄. For plain running away, 逃跑 and 逃走 are the common two-character forms.

column3: It stresses running off, often to avoid being caught: 逃跑的人, 想逃跑. It rarely takes an object; the place goes after 从: 从监狱逃跑. 逃走 is the plainer "got away".
column4: 小偷看见警察就逃跑了。
column5: 小偷看見警察就逃跑了。
column6: Xiǎotōu kànjiàn jǐngchá jiù táopǎo le.
column7: The thief ran away when he saw the police.
column9: It stresses running off, often to avoid being caught: 逃跑的人, 想逃跑. It rarely takes an object; the place goes after 從: 從監獄逃跑. 逃走 is the plainer "got away".

column3: Here 走 means "leave", so it is the plain "got away", with no stress on speed; 逃跑 is the more vivid word for fleeing. Often with 趁: 趁机逃走 means slipping away at the right moment.
column4: 他趁大家睡着了逃走了。
column5: 他趁大家睡著了逃走了。
column6: Tā chèn dàjiā shuìzháo le táozǒu le.
column7: He escaped while everyone was asleep.
column9: Here 走 means "leave", so it is the plain "got away", with no stress on speed; 逃跑 is the more vivid word for fleeing. Often with 趁: 趁機逃走 means slipping away at the right moment.

column3: Two patterns: 躲 + 在 + a hiding place (躲在门后), or 躲 + what you avoid: 躲雨 (shelter from the rain), 躲债 (dodge a debt). With a complement it is 躲开 (get out of the way) and 躲不过 (cannot avoid).
column6: Háizi duǒ zài mén hòumian.
column7: The child is hiding behind the door.
column9: Two patterns: 躲 + 在 + a hiding place (躲在門後), or 躲 + what you avoid: 躲雨 (shelter from the rain), 躲債 (dodge a debt). With a complement it is 躲開 (get out of the way) and 躲不過 (cannot avoid).

column3: The person frightened is the object: 吓了我一跳, 吓坏了. 吓人 means scary, and 被吓到 means got scared.
column6: Nǐ xià le wǒ yī tiào!
column7: You gave me a fright!
column9: The person frightened is the object: 嚇了我一跳, 嚇壞了. 嚇人 means scary, and 被嚇到 means got scared.

column3: Common frames: 咬一口 (a bite), 被狗咬了 (bitten by a dog), 咬住 (bite and hold on), and 咬牙 for gritting your teeth in anger or effort.
column6: Xiǎogǒu yǎo le tā yī kǒu.
column7: The puppy bit him.
column9: Common frames: 咬一口 (a bite), 被狗咬了 (bitten by a dog), 咬住 (bite and hold on), and 咬牙 for gritting your teeth in anger or effort.

column3: Rarely used alone; it sits in compounds, with the kind of disaster first (火灾, 水灾, 天灾) or after a verb (救灾, 受灾, 遭灾). It was drawn as a burning house.
column4: 今年这里遭了灾，庄稼都没了。
column5: 今年這裡遭了災，莊稼都沒了。
column6: Jīnnián zhèlǐ zāo le zāi, zhuāngjia dōu méi le.
column7: This place was hit by disaster this year, and the crops are all gone.
column9: Rarely used alone; it sits in compounds, with the kind of disaster first (火災, 水災, 天災) or after a verb (救災, 受災, 遭災). It was drawn as a burning house.

column3: A general, written word for disasters as a type: 自然灾害, 气象灾害, 预防灾害, 造成灾害. 灾难 is more about the suffering a particular disaster brings.
column6: Dìzhèn shì yī zhǒng zìrán zāihài.
column7: An earthquake is a kind of natural disaster.
column9: A general, written word for disasters as a type: 自然災害, 氣象災害, 預防災害, 造成災害. 災難 is more about the suffering a particular disaster brings.

column3: It stresses the human cost: 带来灾难, 灾难性的 (catastrophic). In speech it exaggerates a mess: 这简直是一场灾难. 难 is read nàn here, not nán as in "difficult".
column4: 战争给人们带来了灾难。
column5: 戰爭給人們帶來了災難。
column6: Zhànzhēng gěi rénmen dàilái le zāinàn.
column7: War brought disaster to the people.
column9: It stresses the human cost: 帶來災難, 災難性的 (catastrophic). In speech it exaggerates a mess: 這簡直是一場災難. 難 is read nàn here, not nán as in "difficult".

column3: 区 is an area or district, as in 山区, 市区 and 景区. 灾区 is where the 受灾群众 live and the 救灾物资 are sent.
column6: Yīshēngmen gǎndào le zāiqū.
column7: The doctors rushed to the disaster area.
column9: 區 is an area or district, as in 山區, 市區 and 景區. 災區 is where the 受災群眾 live and the 救災物資 are sent.

column3: A verb plus object in form, but mostly a modifier or in set phrases, in news style: 救灾物资, 救灾工作, 抗洪救灾.
column4: 全国人民都在为救灾出力。
column5: 全國人民都在為救災出力。
column6: Quánguó rénmín dōu zài wèi jiùzāi chūlì.
column7: People across the country are helping with disaster relief.
column9: A verb plus object in form, but mostly a modifier or in set phrases, in news style: 救災物資, 救災工作, 抗洪救災.

column3: The disaster is "received", like 受伤. Mostly a modifier or in reports: 受灾群众, 受灾地区, 受灾严重.
column4: 这个县今年受灾很严重。
column5: 這個縣今年受災很嚴重。
column6: Zhège xiàn jīnnián shòuzāi hěn yánzhòng.
column7: This county was badly hit by disaster this year.
column9: The disaster is "received", like 受傷. Mostly a modifier or in reports: 受災群眾, 受災地區, 受災嚴重.

column3: The written, news word for a serious fire: 发生火灾, 森林火灾, 火灾报警. For a small fire, or in speech, say 着火 or 失火.
column4: 昨晚这里发生了一场火灾。
column5: 昨晚這裡發生了一場火災。
column6: Zuówǎn zhèlǐ fāshēng le yī chǎng huǒzāi.
column7: A fire broke out here last night.
column9: The written, news word for a serious fire: 發生火災, 森林火災, 火災報警. For a small fire, or in speech, say 著火 or 失火.

column3: It names the damage done by water, not the water: 发生水灾, 水灾严重. The flood water itself is 洪水, and speech has 发大水.
column4: 去年夏天这个地区发生了水灾。
column5: 去年夏天這個地區發生了水災。
column6: Qùnián xiàtiān zhège dìqū fāshēng le shuǐzāi.
column7: There was a flood in this area last summer.
column9: It names the damage done by water, not the water: 發生水災, 水災嚴重. The flood water itself is 洪水, and speech has 發大水.

column3: Counted with 次 or 场, and sized in 级: 七级地震. 余震 is an aftershock, and in speech 地震了! announces one as it happens.
column6: Zuótiān wǎnshang fāshēng le dìzhèn.
column7: An earthquake happened last night.
column9: Counted with 次 or 場, and sized in 級: 七級地震. 餘震 is an aftershock, and in speech 地震了! announces one as it happens.

column3: Typical frames: 台风来了, 刮台风, 台风登陆 (makes landfall), 台风天 (a typhoon day). In Taiwan a strong typhoon brings 台风假, a day off work and school; on the mainland one hears of 停课 and 停工 instead.
column4: 台风要来了，今天别出门。
column5: 颱風要來了，今天別出門。
column6: Táifēng yào lái le, jīntiān bié chūmén.
column7: A typhoon is coming, so don't go out today.
column9: Typical frames: 臺風來了, 颳臺風, 臺風登陸 (makes landfall), 臺風天 (a typhoon day). In Taiwan a strong typhoon brings 臺風假, a day off work and school; on the mainland one hears of 停課 and 停工 instead.

column3: Verb and noun: 污染环境, 空气污染, 受到污染. It also works for non-physical harm, as in 精神污染.
column6: Gōngchǎng wūrǎn le héshuǐ.
column7: The factory polluted the river.
column9: Verb and noun: 污染環境, 空氣污染, 受到污染. It also works for non-physical harm, as in 精神污染.

column3: A technical noun from news and environment reports: 污水处理, 排放污水, 生活污水. Everyday "dirty water" is 脏水.
column6: Zhèxiē wūshuǐ bìxū xiān chǔlǐ.
column7: This sewage has to be treated first.
column9: A technical noun from news and environment reports: 污水處理, 排放污水, 生活污水. Everyday "dirty water" is 髒水.

column3: Used when time is short: 抢救病人, 抢救文物. 抢救无效 is the standard report line when a patient dies despite treatment.
column6: Yīshēng quánlì qiǎngjiù bìngrén.
column7: The doctors did all they could to save the patient.
column9: Used when time is short: 搶救病人, 搶救文物. 搶救無效 is the standard report line when a patient dies despite treatment.

column3: A verb plus object, so 报了警 and 马上报警; the emergency number is 报警电话.
column4: 他发现小偷后马上报警了。
column5: 他發現小偷後馬上報警了。
column6: Tā fāxiàn xiǎotōu hòu mǎshàng bàojǐng le.
column7: When he found the thief he called the police at once.
column9: A verb plus object, so 報了警 and 馬上報警; the emergency number is 報警電話.

column3: Almost always before another noun: 消防员, 消防车, 消防队, 消防安全, 消防通道. It is not used for a fire itself; that is 火灾. 消 has water in it: put out something with water.
column6: Wǒmen xuéxí le xiāofáng zhīshi.
column7: We learned about fire safety.
column9: Almost always before another noun: 消防員, 消防車, 消防隊, 消防安全, 消防通道. It is not used for a fire itself; that is 火災. 消 has water in it: put out something with water.

column3: Formal and written. Used as an adjective (不幸的事), as an adverb before a verb (他不幸受伤了; 不幸去世 for a death), and as a noun (遭遇不幸). The opposite is 幸运.
column6: Tā bùxìng shòu le zhòngshāng.
column7: Unfortunately he was badly injured.
column9: Formal and written. Used as an adjective (不幸的事), as an adverb before a verb (他不幸受傷了; 不幸去世 for a death), and as a noun (遭遇不幸). The opposite is 幸運.

column3: Prevent and treat together, for disease and pollution: 防治疾病, 防治污染, 防治结合. Written, from public health and environment reports.
column4: 医生在研究怎样防治这种病。
column5: 醫生在研究怎樣防治這種病。
column6: Yīshēng zài yánjiū zěnyàng fángzhì zhè zhǒng bìng.
column7: The doctors are studying how to prevent and treat this illness.
column9: Prevent and treat together, for disease and pollution: 防治疾病, 防治污染, 防治結合. Written, from public health and environment reports.

column3: Light a candle, torch or cigarette: 点燃蜡烛; figuratively, 点燃希望 or 点燃热情. 燃 was originally written as plain 然, and 火 was added because 然 got borrowed for abstract senses.
column6: Tā diǎnrán le yī zhī làzhú.
column7: He lit a candle.
column9: Light a candle, torch or cigarette: 點燃蠟燭; figuratively, 點燃希望 or 點燃熱情. 燃 was originally written as plain 然, and 火 was added because 然 got borrowed for abstract senses.

column3: A strong, serious word, for loss and grief rather than ordinary unhappiness (难过 is lighter): 悲伤的心情, 感到悲伤, 悲伤地哭了.
column4: 听到这个消息，她很悲伤。
column5: 聽到這個消息，她很悲傷。
column6: Tīngdào zhège xiāoxi, tā hěn bēishāng.
column7: She was very sad to hear the news.
column9: A strong, serious word, for loss and grief rather than ordinary unhappiness (難過 is lighter): 悲傷的心情, 感到悲傷, 悲傷地哭了.

column3: On stage or screen it is a genre, paired with 喜剧. It is also used for real events, especially avoidable ones: 避免悲剧, 以悲剧收场. In casual speech 太悲剧了 says "what bad luck".
column4: 这是一场可以避免的悲剧。
column5: 這是一場可以避免的悲劇。
column6: Zhè shì yī chǎng kěyǐ bìmiǎn de bēijù.
column7: This is a tragedy that could have been avoided.
column9: On stage or screen it is a genre, paired with 喜劇. It is also used for real events, especially avoidable ones: 避免悲劇, 以悲劇收場. In casual speech 太悲劇了 says "what bad luck".

column3: Common in speech as a verb: 发愁, 别愁, 愁什么, 愁死了. As a noun it is in 乡愁 (homesickness) and 忧愁; 愁眉苦脸 is a worried face.
column6: Bié chóu, bànfǎ zǒng huì yǒu de.
column7: Don't worry, there will always be a way.
column9: Common in speech as a verb: 發愁, 別愁, 愁什麼, 愁死了. As a noun it is in 鄉愁 (homesickness) and 憂愁; 愁眉苦臉 is a worried face.

column3: After an adjective with 得 it means "unbearably": 累得慌, 闷得慌, 饿得慌. On its own it is panic: 别慌, 心里发慌, 慌了手脚.
column6: Bié huāng, mànmàn shuō.
column7: Don't panic; speak slowly.
column9: After an adjective with 得 it means "unbearably": 累得慌, 悶得慌, 餓得慌. On its own it is panic: 別慌, 心裡發慌, 慌了手腳.

column3: An adverb before the verb, for something done in a flustered rush: 慌忙站起来, 慌忙离开. It describes what happened, so it is not used in commands; for those, 赶紧 or 快.
column6: Tā huāngmáng zhàn le qǐlái.
column7: He stood up in a flurry.
column9: An adverb before the verb, for something done in a flustered rush: 慌忙站起來, 慌忙離開. It describes what happened, so it is not used in commands; for those, 趕緊 or 快.

column3: The two characters work only as a pair. Common frames: 犹豫了一下, 犹豫不决, 毫不犹豫 (without hesitation), and 别犹豫.
column4: 他犹豫了一下，还是说了。
column5: 他猶豫了一下，還是說了。
column6: Tā yóuyù le yīxià, háishi shuō le.
column7: He hesitated for a moment, but said it anyway.
column9: The two characters work only as a pair. Common frames: 猶豫了一下, 猶豫不決, 毫不猶豫 (without hesitation), and 別猶豫.

column3: The pain is felt out of love, so a parent or partner is the usual subject: 心疼孩子, 看着心疼. It also covers wincing at the cost of something: 心疼钱.
column4: 看到孩子这么累，妈妈很心疼。
column5: 看到孩子這麼累，媽媽很心疼。
column6: Kàndào háizi zhème lèi, māma hěn xīnténg.
column7: Seeing the child so tired, his mother felt sorry for him.
column9: The pain is felt out of love, so a parent or partner is the usual subject: 心疼孩子, 看著心疼. It also covers wincing at the cost of something: 心疼錢.

column3: Pity for a person or animal: 可怜的孩子, 真可怜. Said to someone's face it can sound condescending. After 得 it means "pitifully little": 少得可怜.
column6: Nà zhī xiǎomāo zhēn kělián.
column7: That little cat is so pitiful.
column9: Pity for a person or animal: 可憐的孩子, 真可憐. Said to someone's face it can sound condescending. After 得 it means "pitifully little": 少得可憐.

column3: For a missed chance, waste or loss: 太可惜了. It also opens a clause to mean "too bad that": 可惜他没来. 惜 has 昔, which means the past or an ending, hence overtones of regret.
column4: 这么好的机会错过了，真可惜。
column5: 這麼好的機會錯過了，真可惜。
column6: Zhème hǎo de jīhuì cuòguò le, zhēn kěxī.
column7: What a pity to miss such a good chance.
column9: For a missed chance, waste or loss: 太可惜了. It also opens a clause to mean "too bad that": 可惜他沒來. 惜 has 昔, which means the past or an ending, hence overtones of regret.

column3: What you regret follows, often with 没: 后悔没来. Fixed phrases: 后悔莫及 (too late for regret) and 别后悔 (you'll be sorry).
column4: 我后悔没有早点告诉你。
column5: 我後悔沒有早點告訴你。
column6: Wǒ hòuhuǐ méiyǒu zǎodiǎn gàosu nǐ.
column7: I regret not telling you sooner.
column9: What you regret follows, often with 沒: 後悔沒來. Fixed phrases: 後悔莫及 (too late for regret) and 別後悔 (you'll be sorry).

column3: To voice a grievance about something: 抱怨天气, 向他抱怨. It is everyday grumbling; a formal complaint is 投诉.
column6: Tā zǒngshì bàoyuàn gōngzuò tài duō.
column7: He is always complaining that there is too much work.
column9: To voice a grievance about something: 抱怨天氣, 向他抱怨. It is everyday grumbling; a formal complaint is 投訴.

column3: Mostly in the negative or in compounds: 不能怨别人, 怨气, 埋怨. For "blame" in speech, 怪 is the usual verb.
column6: Zhè shì bù néng yuàn tā.
column7: You can't blame him for this.
column9: Mostly in the negative or in compounds: 不能怨別人, 怨氣, 埋怨. For "blame" in speech, 怪 is the usual verb.

column3: Much stronger than 讨厌. It also means to regret bitterly, and 恨不得 + verb is the pattern for "wish one could": 恨不得马上回家.
column6: Wǒ hèn tā piàn le wǒ.
column7: I hate him for deceiving me.
column9: Much stronger than 討厭. It also means to regret bitterly, and 恨不得 + verb is the pattern for "wish one could": 恨不得馬上回家.

column3: A verb ("I can't stand…": 我讨厌等人) and an adjective ("annoying": 真讨厌). Milder than 恨, and between friends it can be a playful mock complaint.
column6: Wǒ tǎoyàn děng rén.
column7: I hate waiting for people.
column9: A verb ("I can't stand…": 我討厭等人) and an adjective ("annoying": 真討厭). Milder than 恨, and between friends it can be a playful mock complaint.

column3: 耐烦 is used almost only in the negative, so 不耐烦 works as one unit: 不耐烦地说, 很不耐烦. The opposite is 耐心.
column6: Tā bùnàifán de kàn le kàn biǎo.
column7: He looked at his watch impatiently.
column9: 耐煩 is used almost only in the negative, so 不耐煩 works as one unit: 不耐煩地說, 很不耐煩. The opposite is 耐心.

column3: Helpless: 无奈地笑了笑, 感到无奈, 出于无奈. At the start of a clause it gives what blocked a plan: 本想去，无奈下雨了.
column6: Tā wúnài de xiào le xiào.
column7: He smiled helplessly.
column9: Helpless: 無奈地笑了笑, 感到無奈, 出於無奈. At the start of a clause it gives what blocked a plan: 本想去，無奈下雨了.

column3: The person comforted is the object, and the words can follow: 安慰了她几句. It is also an adjective, "comforted, relieved": 很安慰.
column6: Wǒ ānwèi le tā jǐ jù.
column7: I said a few words to comfort her.
column9: The person comforted is the object, and the words can follow: 安慰了她幾句. It is also an adjective, "comforted, relieved": 很安慰.

column3: Formal: the visitor is usually an official, a group or an organization, not a friend. 慰问病人, 慰问信, 春节慰问.
column4: 市长去医院慰问了病人。
column5: 市長去醫院慰問了病人。
column6: Shìzhǎng qù yīyuàn wèiwèn le bìngrén.
column7: The mayor visited the patients in the hospital.
column9: Formal: the visitor is usually an official, a group or an organization, not a friend. 慰問病人, 慰問信, 春節慰問.

column3: 忍不住 + verb is the common pattern: 忍不住笑了. Also 忍一忍 (bear it a bit) and 忍着 (hold back).
column6: Téng jiù hǎn chūlái, bié rěn zhe.
column7: If it hurts, cry out; don't hold it in.
column9: 忍不住 + verb is the common pattern: 忍不住笑了. Also 忍一忍 (bear it a bit) and 忍著 (hold back).

column3: The object is usually the pain or bother, though a person's behavior can be it too: 忍受痛苦, 无法忍受他, 难以忍受. More formal than 忍; speech prefers 受不了.
column6: Wǒ wúfǎ rěnshòu zhè zhǒng zàoyīn.
column7: I can't stand this kind of noise.
column9: The object is usually the pain or bother, though a person's behavior can be it too: 忍受痛苦, 無法忍受他, 難以忍受. More formal than 忍; speech prefers 受不了.

column3: Positive pride in one's own or one's group's achievement: 感到自豪, 为…感到自豪, 令人自豪. 骄傲 can also mean arrogant, but 自豪 never does. 自 began as a picture of a nose, and one folk explanation links its meaning "oneself" to pointing at your own nose.
column4: 我为我的国家感到自豪。
column5: 我為我的國家感到自豪。
column6: Wǒ wèi wǒ de guójiā gǎndào zìháo.
column7: I am proud of my country.
column9: Positive pride in one's own or one's group's achievement: 感到自豪, 為…感到自豪, 令人自豪. 驕傲 can also mean arrogant, but 自豪 never does. 自 began as a picture of a nose, and one folk explanation links its meaning "oneself" to pointing at your own nose.

column3: Works as a verb and an adjective: 令人震惊 is "shocking," 感到震惊 "to be shocked." Often 大为震惊, or 震惊世界 for news that stuns everyone. Heavier than 吃惊: a blow of bad or huge news, not a small surprise.
column4: 这个消息让大家非常震惊。
column5: 這個消息讓大家非常震驚。
column6: Zhège xiāoxi ràng dàjiā fēicháng zhènjīng.
column7: This news shocked everyone.
column9: Works as a verb and an adjective: 令人震驚 is "shocking," 感到震驚 "to be shocked." Often 大為震驚, or 震驚世界 for news that stuns everyone. Heavier than 吃驚: a blow of bad or huge news, not a small surprise.

column3: As a noun it is an urge (控制冲动); as an adjective it describes someone who acts without thinking (他很冲动). 一时冲动 is the stock excuse for a rash choice, 冲动消费 is impulse buying, and 别冲动 is the advice to cool down first.
column6: Bié chōngdòng, xiān lěngjìng yīxià.
column7: Don't be rash; calm down first.
column9: As a noun it is an urge (控制衝動); as an adjective it describes someone who acts without thinking (他很衝動). 一時衝動 is the stock excuse for a rash choice, 衝動消費 is impulse buying, and 別衝動 is the advice to cool down first.

column3: Often means arrogant, as in 他太狂了 (he is full of himself), with 狂妄 as the stronger, written version. The out-of-control sense shows in 狂风 (a raging wind), 狂欢 (a wild party) and 发狂 (go mad).
column6: Nàge rén tài kuáng le.
column7: That person is too full of himself.
column9: Often means arrogant, as in 他太狂了 (he is full of himself), with 狂妄 as the stronger, written version. The out-of-control sense shows in 狂風 (a raging wind), 狂歡 (a wild party) and 發狂 (go mad).

column3: As often an exaggeration as real madness: 忙疯了 is "crazy busy," 你疯了吗？ a cry of disbelief. 疯子 is a madman and 发疯 means to go mad; 疯玩 is to play wildly.
column6: Nǐ fēng le ma?
column7: Have you gone mad?
column9: As often an exaggeration as real madness: 忙瘋了 is "crazy busy," 你瘋了嗎？ a cry of disbelief. 瘋子 is a madman and 發瘋 means to go mad; 瘋玩 is to play wildly.

column3: Before a noun it takes 的 (疯狂的想法), before a verb 地 (疯狂地工作). It is not only blame: 疯狂购物 is a shopping spree and a 疯狂的创意 can be wildly good. More about actions and events than 狂, which can mean arrogant.
column6: Qiúmímen fēngkuáng de hǎnzhe.
column7: The fans were shouting wildly.
column9: Before a noun it takes 的 (瘋狂的想法), before a verb 地 (瘋狂地工作). It is not only blame: 瘋狂購物 is a shopping spree and a 瘋狂的創意 can be wildly good. More about actions and events than 狂, which can mean arrogant.

column3: Stronger than 失望: not just let down but with no hope left. It is a verb (对未来绝望), an adjective (绝望的眼神) and a noun (陷入绝望, fall into despair). 绝 began as a knife cutting silk threads.
column6: Tā duì shēnghuó gǎndào juéwàng.
column7: He felt hopeless about life.
column9: Stronger than 失望: not just let down but with no hope left. It is a verb (對未來絕望), an adjective (絕望的眼神) and a noun (陷入絕望, fall into despair). 絕 began as a knife cutting silk threads.

column3: For deep wants, not plans: you 希望 it will not rain tomorrow, but you 渴望 freedom or love. Stronger and more emotional than 希望, and also a noun: 内心的渴望 (an inner longing). 望 began as a person standing and looking off into the distance.
column6: Háizimen kěwàng dédào ài.
column7: Children long to be loved.
column9: For deep wants, not plans: you 希望 it will not rain tomorrow, but you 渴望 freedom or love. Stronger and more emotional than 希望, and also a noun: 內心的渴望 (an inner longing). 望 began as a person standing and looking off into the distance.

column3: A hope placed on someone else, that they will do well: 对孩子期望很高 (high hopes for the child), 不负期望 (live up to expectations). A little more formal than 希望, and it comes up with parents, teachers and bosses.
column4: 父母对孩子的期望很高。
column5: 父母對孩子的期望很高。
column6: Fùmǔ duì háizi de qīwàng hěn gāo.
column7: Parents have high hopes for their children.
column9: A hope placed on someone else, that they will do well: 對孩子期望很高 (high hopes for the child), 不負期望 (live up to expectations). A little more formal than 希望, and it comes up with parents, teachers and bosses.

column3: Formal when alone: it is the wish in blessings like 愿你幸福 (may you be happy) and 祝愿. In plain speech it needs a partner: say 我愿意 for "I'm willing," not 我愿. It is also the wish in 心愿, 志愿 and 自愿.
column6: Yuàn nǐ yīqiè shùnlì!
column7: May everything go well for you!
column9: Formal when alone: it is the wish in blessings like 願你幸福 (may you be happy) and 祝願. In plain speech it needs a partner: say 我願意 for "I'm willing," not 我願. It is also the wish in 心願, 志願 and 自願.

column3: A word of forms and rules more than chat: 自愿参加 before a verb, or 是自愿的 to say nobody forced you. Its opposite is 被迫 or 强迫. Signs and notices say 自愿原则 (the principle of voluntary participation).
column4: 参加这个活动是自愿的。
column5: 參加這個活動是自願的。
column6: Cānjiā zhège huódòng shì zìyuàn de.
column7: Taking part in this activity is voluntary.
column9: A word of forms and rules more than chat: 自願參加 before a verb, or 是自願的 to say nobody forced you. Its opposite is 被迫 or 強迫. Signs and notices say 自願原則 (the principle of voluntary participation).

column3: What you feel and think after an experience, a trip, a book or a talk. The usual partners are 谈 and 发表, or 有: 谈谈感想, 发表感想, 有什么感想. It looks back on something; for an opinion on an issue, 看法 is the word.
column6: Qǐng tántan nǐ de gǎnxiǎng.
column7: Please tell us what you thought of it.
column9: What you feel and think after an experience, a trip, a book or a talk. The usual partners are 談 and 發表, or 有: 談談感想, 發表感想, 有什麼感想. It looks back on something; for an opinion on an issue, 看法 is the word.

column3: A lasting attitude toward things, more than a passing mood. It goes with 好心态 and 心态平和, and with the verbs 调整 and 保持. Advice for exams, work and hard times keeps coming back to it: 心态好 means you stay calm under pressure.
column6: Bǎochí hǎo xīntài hěn zhòngyào.
column7: It is important to keep a good attitude.
column9: A lasting attitude toward things, more than a passing mood. It goes with 好心態 and 心態平和, and with the verbs 調整 and 保持. Advice for exams, work and hard times keeps coming back to it: 心態好 means you stay calm under pressure.

column3: Being romantically involved is a state, not a single act. The everyday verb is 谈: 谈恋爱 (be dating). You do not 恋爱 a person directly; say 和他恋爱 or 谈恋爱. Also 初恋 (first love) and 恋爱结婚 (marry for love).
column6: Tāmen zhèngzài tán liàn'ài.
column7: They are going out together.
column9: Being romantically involved is a state, not a single act. The everyday verb is 談: 談戀愛 (be dating). You do not 戀愛 a person directly; say 和他戀愛 or 談戀愛. Also 初戀 (first love) and 戀愛結婚 (marry for love).

column3: Describes an atmosphere, a gesture or a setting (a candlelit dinner, a trip), not love itself; that is 爱情 or 恋爱. 很浪漫 is a compliment. 浪漫主义 is Romanticism in the arts, and a 浪漫 person can also be a dreamer who ignores reality.
column4: 这家餐厅的气氛很浪漫。
column5: 這家餐廳的氣氛很浪漫。
column6: Zhè jiā cāntīng de qìfēn hěn làngmàn.
column7: The atmosphere in this restaurant is very romantic.
column9: Describes an atmosphere, a gesture or a setting (a candlelit dinner, a trip), not love itself; that is 愛情 or 戀愛. 很浪漫 is a compliment. 浪漫主義 is Romanticism in the arts, and a 浪漫 person can also be a dreamer who ignores reality.

column3: To enjoy an experience fully and slowly: 享受生活, 享受美食, 享受假期. 我很享受 on its own is a common spoken way to say you are loving it. It also has a formal side, to have a right to something: 享受待遇, 享受优惠.
column6: Wǒ hěn xiǎngshòu zhèyàng de shēnghuó.
column7: I really enjoy this kind of life.
