column9: To enjoy an experience fully and slowly: 享受生活, 享受美食, 享受假期. 我很享受 on its own is a common spoken way to say you are loving it. It also has a formal side, to have a right to something: 享受待遇, 享受優惠.

column3: To enjoy something as beauty (欣赏音乐, 欣赏风景) or to think highly of a person's quality (欣赏他的勇气). It carries taste or respect; for simply liking food or a hobby, say 喜欢.
column6: Wǒ hěn xīnshǎng tā de yǒngqì.
column7: I admire his courage.
column9: To enjoy something as beauty (欣賞音樂, 欣賞風景) or to think highly of a person's quality (欣賞他的勇氣). It carries taste or respect; for simply liking food or a hobby, say 喜歡.

column3: Energy as a quality of life: 充满活力, 有活力, 缺乏活力. Positive, and said of people, teams, cities, companies and even a design. For physical energy to get things done, 精力 is the word, as in 精力充沛.
column6: Niánqīngrén chōngmǎn huólì.
column7: Young people are full of energy.
column9: Energy as a quality of life: 充滿活力, 有活力, 缺乏活力. Positive, and said of people, teams, cities, companies and even a design. For physical energy to get things done, 精力 is the word, as in 精力充沛.

column3: The bond between people or countries, a little formal: 深厚的友谊, 珍惜友谊, 建立友谊. It names the relationship; for being friends, say 朋友: 我们是朋友. It also gives 友谊赛, a friendly match. One old reading takes 友 as two hands, hence friendship.
column4: 我们的友谊已经十年了。
column5: 我們的友誼已經十年了。
column6: Wǒmen de yǒuyì yǐjīng shí nián le.
column7: Our friendship has lasted ten years.
column9: The bond between people or countries, a little formal: 深厚的友誼, 珍惜友誼, 建立友誼. It names the relationship; for being friends, say 朋友: 我們是朋友. It also gives 友誼賽, a friendly match. One old reading takes 友 as two hands, hence friendship.

column3: Leisure, mostly as a modifier: 休闲活动, 休闲时间, 休闲服 (casual clothes), 休闲餐厅. In speech 休息 is to rest; 休闲 is spending free time pleasantly, with a walk, tea or a hobby, as the opposite of work. 休 began as a man leaning against a tree, resting.
column4: 周末我喜欢去公园散散步，休闲一下。
column5: 週末我喜歡去公園散散步，休閒一下。
column6: Zhōumò wǒ xǐhuan qù gōngyuán sànsan bù, xiūxián yīxià.
column7: On weekends I like to take a walk in the park and relax a bit.
column9: Leisure, mostly as a modifier: 休閒活動, 休閒時間, 休閒服 (casual clothes), 休閒餐廳. In speech 休息 is to rest; 休閒 is spending free time pleasantly, with a walk, tea or a hobby, as the opposite of work. 休 began as a man leaning against a tree, resting.

column3: Wit and funniness: 很幽默, 幽默感, 幽默的人. Lighter and cleverer than 搞笑, which is silly, goofy comedy.
column6: Tā shuōhuà hěn yōumò.
column7: He is very funny when he talks.
column9: Wit and funniness: 很幽默, 幽默感, 幽默的人. Lighter and cleverer than 搞笑, which is silly, goofy comedy.

column3: A warm, informal word, a bit old-fashioned, for a carefree life or mood: 过得很快活, 快活的日子. It is not for greetings or holidays; for "Happy New Year" the word is 快乐.
column6: Tāmen guò de hěn kuàihuo.
column7: They lead a happy life.
column9: A warm, informal word, a bit old-fashioned, for a carefree life or mood: 過得很快活, 快活的日子. It is not for greetings or holidays; for "Happy New Year" the word is 快樂.

column3: Lively and outgoing, praise for children and young people: 活泼可爱, 性格活泼. Also for styles, colors and layouts that feel cheerful, and in chemistry it means reactive. The opposite for a person is 文静 (quiet and gentle).
column6: Zhège háizi hěn huópo.
column7: This child is very lively.
column9: Lively and outgoing, praise for children and young people: 活潑可愛, 性格活潑. Also for styles, colors and layouts that feel cheerful, and in chemistry it means reactive. The opposite for a person is 文靜 (quiet and gentle).

column3: Free of things to do right now: 他今天很闲, 闲着 (sit idle). Different from 有空, which is time available for plans. 闲聊 is idle chat and 闲人 an idler, with a faint put-down; 闲话 is gossip.
column6: Tā jīntiān hěn xián.
column7: He has nothing to do today.
column9: Free of things to do right now: 他今天很閒, 閒著 (sit idle). Different from 有空, which is time available for plans. 閒聊 is idle chat and 閒人 an idler, with a faint put-down; 閒話 is gossip.

column3: A spoken word for a short break in the middle of work or a walk: 歇一会儿, 歇歇, 歇口气 (catch your breath), 歇脚 (stop to rest). 歇业 means a shop closes for business. For a long rest, 休息 is the word.
column6: Lèi le jiù xiē yīhuìr ba.
column7: If you're tired, rest a while.
column9: A spoken word for a short break in the middle of work or a walk: 歇一會兒, 歇歇, 歇口氣 (catch your breath), 歇腳 (stop to rest). 歇業 means a shop closes for business. For a long rest, 休息 is the word.

column3: Quick to learn and quick-witted: 聪明的孩子, 很聪明. Said of animals too, and of ideas: 聪明的办法 is a smart way. 小聪明 is petty cleverness, a mild put-down. An early form of 聪 was a heart 心 with a big dot on top for a hole, said to show an open heart and an open mind.
column6: Zhège háizi hěn cōngming.
column7: This child is very clever.
column9: Quick to learn and quick-witted: 聰明的孩子, 很聰明. Said of animals too, and of ideas: 聰明的辦法 is a smart way. 小聰明 is petty cleverness, a mild put-down. An early form of 聰 was a heart 心 with a big dot on top for a hole, said to show an open heart and an open mind.

column3: Silly or foolish, and often fond: 你真傻 is gentle teasing, 傻孩子 is what a parent says. Unlike 笨 (slow, dull), 傻 is about daft behavior: 傻笑, 装傻 (play dumb). 傻眼 is to be stunned speechless.
column6: Wǒ zhēn shǎ, zěnme méi xiǎngdào ne?
column7: How silly of me not to have thought of it!
column9: Silly or foolish, and often fond: 你真傻 is gentle teasing, 傻孩子 is what a parent says. Unlike 笨 (slow, dull), 傻 is about daft behavior: 傻笑, 裝傻 (play dumb). 傻眼 is to be stunned speechless.

column3: Bold, in praise: 大胆尝试 (dare to try), 大胆的想法, 大胆地说. Said sharply, 大胆！ means "how dare you!" Chinese puts courage in the gallbladder, so 胆子大 says the same thing about a person.
column4: 她大胆地说出了自己的想法。
column5: 她大膽地說出了自己的想法。
column6: Tā dàdǎn de shuōchū le zìjǐ de xiǎngfǎ.
column7: She boldly spoke her mind.
column9: Bold, in praise: 大膽嘗試 (dare to try), 大膽的想法, 大膽地說. Said sharply, 大膽！ means "how dare you!" Chinese puts courage in the gallbladder, so 膽子大 says the same thing about a person.

column3: Chinese puts courage in the gallbladder, so 胆子小 says the same thing of a person. 胆小鬼 is a coward, said teasingly to a child or friend. The opposites are 大胆 and 胆子大.
column6: Tā dǎnxiǎo, bù gǎn yī ge rén shuì.
column7: He is timid and dares not sleep alone.
column9: Chinese puts courage in the gallbladder, so 膽子小 says the same thing of a person. 膽小鬼 is a coward, said teasingly to a child or friend. The opposites are 大膽 and 膽子大.

column3: Polite in a way that keeps some distance. 别客气 or 不用客气 answers thanks and tells a guest to relax; 太客气了 thanks someone for a gift; 跟我客气什么 means "no need to stand on ceremony with me." Among close friends, being 客气 can feel cold.
column6: Bùyòng kèqi, qǐng zuò.
column7: No need to stand on ceremony; please sit.
column9: Polite in a way that keeps some distance. 別客氣 or 不用客氣 answers thanks and tells a guest to relax; 太客氣了 thanks someone for a gift; 跟我客氣什麼 means "no need to stand on ceremony with me." Among close friends, being 客氣 can feel cold.

column3: Both a noun (manners) and an adjective (polite): 有礼貌, 没礼貌, 讲礼貌. The person comes after 对: 对客人很有礼貌. Adults tell children 要有礼貌. 礼貌用语 are the polite phrases like 请 and 谢谢. 礼 shows performing rites at an altar.
column6: Duì lǎorén yào yǒu lǐmào.
column7: You must be polite to old people.
column9: Both a noun (manners) and an adjective (polite): 有禮貌, 沒禮貌, 講禮貌. The person comes after 對: 對客人很有禮貌. Adults tell children 要有禮貌. 禮貌用語 are the polite phrases like 請 and 謝謝. 禮 shows performing rites at an altar.

column3: Steady diligence in study or work: 勤奋学习. 勤劳 is hardworking, mostly physical labor (勤劳的农民), and 努力 is the everyday word for trying hard at anything.
column6: Tā xuéxí hěn qínfèn.
column7: He studies diligently.
column9: Steady diligence in study or work: 勤奮學習. 勤勞 is hardworking, mostly physical labor (勤勞的農民), and 努力 is the everyday word for trying hard at anything.

column3: Praise for staying open to advice and criticism: 虚心学习, 虚心接受批评 (accept criticism with an open mind), 他很虚心. The opposite is 骄傲 or 自满.
column6: Tā xūxīn de tīngqǔ yìjiàn.
column7: He listens humbly to advice.
column9: Praise for staying open to advice and criticism: 虛心學習, 虛心接受批評 (accept criticism with an open mind), 他很虛心. The opposite is 驕傲 or 自滿.

column3: Sincere in a warm, open way, stronger than 诚实 (honest, truthful): 真诚的道歉, 真诚地感谢, 待人真诚. Before a verb it takes 地, before a noun 的.
column6: Tā de dàoqiàn hěn zhēnchéng.
column7: His apology was sincere.
column9: Sincere in a warm, open way, stronger than 誠實 (honest, truthful): 真誠的道歉, 真誠地感謝, 待人真誠. Before a verb it takes 地, before a noun 的.

column3: Mild and gentle, not weak: a person's nature (性格温和), a tone of voice, a climate (气候温和), even a medicine or soap. The opposite for a person is 暴躁, hot-tempered. 温 is said to show a person bathing in a container full of warm water.
column6: Tā shuōhuà de shēngyīn hěn wēnhé.
column7: He has a gentle voice.
column9: Mild and gentle, not weak: a person's nature (性格溫和), a tone of voice, a climate (氣候溫和), even a medicine or soap. The opposite for a person is 暴躁, hot-tempered. 溫 is said to show a person bathing in a container full of warm water.

column3: A spoken word that swings between praise and warning. 你真厉害 is "you're amazing"; a 厉害的老师 is a tough, formidable teacher. After 得 it means severely: 疼得厉害, 冷得厉害.
column6: Tā de Yīngyǔ shuō de zhēn lìhai.
column7: His English is really impressive.
column9: A spoken word that swings between praise and warning. 你真厲害 is "you're amazing"; a 厲害的老師 is a tough, formidable teacher. After 得 it means severely: 疼得厲害, 冷得厲害.

column3: Stern about behavior, said of a person or a punishment: 严厉的老师, 严厉批评, 严厉打击 (crack down hard). Harsher than 严格, which only means strict about rules and standards; a 严格 teacher can still be kind.
column6: Lǎoshī duì xuésheng hěn yánlì.
column7: The teacher is very strict with his students.
column9: Stern about behavior, said of a person or a punishment: 嚴厲的老師, 嚴厲批評, 嚴厲打擊 (crack down hard). Harsher than 嚴格, which only means strict about rules and standards; a 嚴格 teacher can still be kind.

column3: Serious in manner, topic or mood: 表情严肃, 严肃的话题, 严肃地说. Of a rule, 严肃处理 means to handle it strictly. It is about gravity; 认真 is about taking care in doing something (认真学习).
column6: Tā de biǎoqíng hěn yánsù.
column7: His expression is very serious.
column9: Serious in manner, topic or mood: 表情嚴肅, 嚴肅的話題, 嚴肅地說. Of a rule, 嚴肅處理 means to handle it strictly. It is about gravity; 認真 is about taking care in doing something (認真學習).

column3: Firm in will or belief, never a hard object (that is 坚硬): 态度坚定, 坚定的信念, 坚定地说. As a verb it means to strengthen one's resolve: 坚定信心. 坚定不移 is "unwavering."
column6: Tā de tàidù hěn jiāndìng.
column7: Her attitude is very firm.
column9: Firm in will or belief, never a hard object (that is 堅硬): 態度堅定, 堅定的信念, 堅定地說. As a verb it means to strengthen one's resolve: 堅定信心. 堅定不移 is "unwavering."

column3: A serious, written word for hard conditions of living or work: 艰苦的环境, 生活艰苦, 艰苦奋斗 (work hard through difficulty). It suits a poor or remote place, not a hard exam or puzzle; for a hard problem, 困难 is the word.
column6: Shānqū de shēnghuó hěn jiānkǔ.
column7: Life in the mountains is hard.
column9: A serious, written word for hard conditions of living or work: 艱苦的環境, 生活艱苦, 艱苦奮鬥 (work hard through difficulty). It suits a poor or remote place, not a hard exam or puzzle; for a hard problem, 困難 is the word.

column3: A person's temper or disposition: 脾气好 and 脾气不好 describe character. 发脾气 is to lose one's temper, and 他有脾气 means he has a temper. 好脾气 is a good-natured person.
column6: Tā píqi bù hǎo, róngyì shēngqì.
column7: He has a bad temper and gets angry easily.
column9: A person's temper or disposition: 脾氣好 and 脾氣不好 describe character. 發脾氣 is to lose one's temper, and 他有脾氣 means he has a temper. 好脾氣 is a good-natured person.

column3: Social standing and dignity in others' eyes: 爱面子 (care about appearances), 给面子 (show respect by agreeing), 丢面子 or 没面子 (lose face). 看在我的面子上 means "do it for my sake." 面 began as a man's face with an eye exaggerated.
column6: Tā hěn ài miànzi.
column7: He cares a lot about saving face.
column9: Social standing and dignity in others' eyes: 愛面子 (care about appearances), 給面子 (show respect by agreeing), 丟面子 or 沒面子 (lose face). 看在我的面子上 means "do it for my sake." 面 began as a man's face with an eye exaggerated.

column3: Its biggest use is thanks for effort: 你辛苦了 to someone who worked or traveled for you, 您辛苦了 more politely, 辛苦你了 when asking a favor. For a gift or a small kindness, use 谢谢 instead.
column4: 你辛苦了，快坐下休息吧。
column5: 你辛苦了，快坐下休息吧。
column6: Nǐ xīnkǔ le, kuài zuòxià xiūxi ba.
column7: You've worked hard; sit down and rest.
column9: Its biggest use is thanks for effort: 你辛苦了 to someone who worked or traveled for you, 您辛苦了 more politely, 辛苦你了 when asking a favor. For a gift or a small kindness, use 謝謝 instead.

column3: Patience as a noun after 有 or 没有 (很有耐心), and as an adverb with 地 (耐心地解释). The opposite is 不耐烦 (impatient). The 耐 is the one in 耐用 (durable) and 耐看 (good-looking over time).
column6: Lǎoshī hěn yǒu nàixīn.
column7: The teacher is very patient.
column9: Patience as a noun after 有 or 沒有 (很有耐心), and as an adverb with 地 (耐心地解釋). The opposite is 不耐煩 (impatient). The 耐 is the one in 耐用 (durable) and 耐看 (good-looking over time).

column3: Sensitive to senses (对声音敏感) or to a topic: 敏感话题 is a touchy subject. Of a person, 太敏感 means taking things too personally; in business or science it is praise: 对数字很敏感 (good with numbers).
column6: Tā duì shēngyīn hěn mǐngǎn.
column7: She is very sensitive to sound.
column9: Sensitive to senses (對聲音敏感) or to a topic: 敏感話題 is a touchy subject. Of a person, 太敏感 means taking things too personally; in business or science it is praise: 對數字很敏感 (good with numbers).

column3: Formal, and only before a noun: 不良习惯, 不良影响, 不良少年 (a delinquent), 营养不良 (malnutrition). In plain speech you say 这个习惯不好, not 很不良.
column6: Áoyè shì yī zhǒng bùliáng xíguàn.
column7: Staying up late is a bad habit.
column9: Formal, and only before a noun: 不良習慣, 不良影響, 不良少年 (a delinquent), 營養不良 (malnutrition). In plain speech you say 這個習慣不好, not 很不良.

column3: Cultivation of character that shows in behavior: 有修养 (well-bred), 个人修养, 文化修养. A person with it stays calm and polite in a quarrel. It can also mean trained skill in a field: 艺术修养. For manners taught by parents, 教养 is closer.
column4: 他是一个很有修养的人。
column5: 他是一個很有修養的人。
column6: Tā shì yī ge hěn yǒu xiūyǎng de rén.
column7: He is a very cultivated person.
column9: Cultivation of character that shows in behavior: 有修養 (well-bred), 個人修養, 文化修養. A person with it stays calm and polite in a quarrel. It can also mean trained skill in a field: 藝術修養. For manners taught by parents, 教養 is closer.

column3: Spoken: something costs real effort or is beyond you. It sits after 得 or 觉得: 做得吃力, 学得很吃力. 吃 here is not eating but bearing, as in 吃苦. 吃力不讨好 is working hard and getting no thanks.
column4: 这个工作他做得有点吃力。
column5: 這個工作他做得有點吃力。
column6: Zhège gōngzuò tā zuò de yǒudiǎn chīlì.
column7: He finds this job a bit of a strain.
column9: Spoken: something costs real effort or is beyond you. It sits after 得 or 覺得: 做得吃力, 學得很吃力. 吃 here is not eating but bearing, as in 吃苦. 吃力不討好 is working hard and getting no thanks.

column3: A polite, written word for calling on someone to show respect: 拜访老师, 拜访客户, 登门拜访 (visit at their home). For dropping in on a friend, 去看 or 去找 is the everyday phrase.
column4: 我明天去拜访一位老师。
column5: 我明天去拜訪一位老師。
column6: Wǒ míngtiān qù bàifǎng yī wèi lǎoshī.
column7: Tomorrow I am going to call on a teacher.
column9: A polite, written word for calling on someone to show respect: 拜訪老師, 拜訪客戶, 登門拜訪 (visit at their home). For dropping in on a friend, 去看 or 去找 is the everyday phrase.

column3: The pattern is 邀请 + person + 参加 + event: 邀请我参加婚礼. It is also a noun: 接受邀请, 邀请函 (invitation letter). More formal than 请, and used for events and trips; for a meal you pay for, say 请你吃饭.
column4: 他邀请我参加他的婚礼。
column5: 他邀請我參加他的婚禮。
column6: Tā yāoqǐng wǒ cānjiā tā de hūnlǐ.
column7: He invited me to his wedding.
column9: The pattern is 邀請 + person + 參加 + event: 邀請我參加婚禮. It is also a noun: 接受邀請, 邀請函 (invitation letter). More formal than 請, and used for events and trips; for a meal you pay for, say 請你吃飯.

column3: The person comes right after 陪, then what you do together: 陪妈妈去医院, 陪孩子玩, 陪朋友聊天. It is giving your company and time. 陪同 is the formal version for guests, 陪伴 for steady companionship.
column6: Wǒ péi māma qù yīyuàn.
column7: I am going to the hospital with my mother.
column9: The person comes right after 陪, then what you do together: 陪媽媽去醫院, 陪孩子玩, 陪朋友聊天. It is giving your company and time. 陪同 is the formal version for guests, 陪伴 for steady companionship.

column3: A gift, and courtesy or ceremony: 送礼 "give a gift", 礼物 "present", 礼貌 "politeness", 礼节 "etiquette", 婚礼 "wedding", 行礼 "bow, salute". On its own it is mainly a gift in 送礼 and 收礼. The left 礻 is the sign for spirits and rites, found in 祝 and 神.
column6: Guònián yào gěi zhǎngbèi sòng lǐ.
column7: At New Year you should give gifts to the older generation.
column9: A gift, and courtesy or ceremony: 送禮 "give a gift", 禮物 "present", 禮貌 "politeness", 禮節 "etiquette", 婚禮 "wedding", 行禮 "bow, salute". On its own it is mainly a gift in 送禮 and 收禮. The left 礻 is the sign for spirits and rites, found in 祝 and 神.

column3: To give as a present, formal and written: 赠书 "give a book", 赠言 "parting words", 赠予 "bestow", 赠品 "freebie". Given by a person to another in a polite or official way, and often the gift of an organization. In daily speech 送 is used instead. 贝 "shell, money" is the meaning part, as in many words about wealth or giving, and 曾 gives the sound.
column6: Tā zèng le wǒ yī běn shū.
column7: She gave me a book as a present.
column9: To give as a present, formal and written: 贈書 "give a book", 贈言 "parting words", 贈予 "bestow", 贈品 "freebie". Given by a person to another in a polite or official way, and often the gift of an organization. In daily speech 送 is used instead. 貝 "shell, money" is the meaning part, as in many words about wealth or giving, and 曾 gives the sound.

column3: To give as a gift, often free: 赠送礼品 "give a gift", 免费赠送 "give away for free", 买一赠送一 "buy one, get one". Common in shops and promotions, and for presents between organizations. Between friends people say 送. 赠 is the formal "present" and 送 is "send, give".
column6: Shāngdiàn zèngsòng yī ge xiǎo lǐwù.
column7: The shop gives a small gift.
column9: To give as a gift, often free: 贈送禮品 "give a gift", 免費贈送 "give away for free", 買一贈送一 "buy one, get one". Common in shops and promotions, and for presents between organizations. Between friends people say 送. 贈 is the formal "present" and 送 is "send, give".

column3: To offer or present with respect, to donate: 献花 "present flowers", 献血 "donate blood", 献给 + person "dedicate to", 贡献 "contribute", 奉献 "devote". Often something offered to a person you respect, a cause or a country. 献 is mostly in compounds; on its own, you see 献花 and 献血 most.
column6: Xuéshengmen xiàng lǎoshī xiàn huā.
column7: The students presented flowers to the teacher.
column9: To offer or present with respect, to donate: 獻花 "present flowers", 獻血 "donate blood", 獻給 + person "dedicate to", 貢獻 "contribute", 奉獻 "devote". Often something offered to a person you respect, a cause or a country. 獻 is mostly in compounds; on its own, you see 獻花 and 獻血 most.

column3: To congratulate, and congratulations: 祝贺你 "congratulations to you", 向他祝贺 "congratulate him", 表示祝贺 "offer congratulations", 祝贺成功. It is for a person's success or a happy event, and takes the person as object. 祝 shows a person kneeling before an altar, and 贺 puts 加 "add" over 贝 "wealth": adding to someone's fortune.
column6: Zhùhè nǐ kǎoshàng le dàxué!
column7: Congratulations on getting into university!
column9: To congratulate, and congratulations: 祝賀你 "congratulations to you", 向他祝賀 "congratulate him", 表示祝賀 "offer congratulations", 祝賀成功. It is for a person's success or a happy event, and takes the person as object. 祝 shows a person kneeling before an altar, and 賀 puts 加 "add" over 貝 "wealth": adding to someone's fortune.

column3: To respect and honor a person, and respectful: 尊敬老师 "respect teachers", 受人尊敬 "be respected", 令人尊敬 "worthy of respect". It is for a person you look up to because of age, character or position. In letters, 尊敬的 + title opens a formal address, like "Dear". 尊 has a hand 寸 offering a vessel of wine 酋.
column6: Wǒmen dōu hěn zūnjìng tā.
column7: We all respect him.
column9: To respect and honor a person, and respectful: 尊敬老師 "respect teachers", 受人尊敬 "be respected", 令人尊敬 "worthy of respect". It is for a person you look up to because of age, character or position. In letters, 尊敬的 + title opens a formal address, like "Dear". 尊 has a hand 寸 offering a vessel of wine 酋.

column3: To respect, to treat with consideration; respect: 尊重别人 "respect others", 尊重选择 "respect a choice", 互相尊重 "mutual respect", 受到尊重. Unlike 尊敬, which looks up to a person, 尊重 can apply to opinions, rules and rights as well as to people. It means not overriding or looking down on something. 重 is read zhòng here.
column4: 我们要尊重别人的选择。
column5: 我們要尊重別人的選擇。
column6: Wǒmen yào zūnzhòng biéren de xuǎnzé.
column7: We must respect other people's choices.
column9: To respect, to treat with consideration; respect: 尊重別人 "respect others", 尊重選擇 "respect a choice", 互相尊重 "mutual respect", 受到尊重. Unlike 尊敬, which looks up to a person, 尊重 can apply to opinions, rules and rights as well as to people. It means not overriding or looking down on something. 重 is read zhòng here.

column3: Concern, care for people, shown with warmth: 关怀老人 "show care for the elderly", 得到关怀, 亲切的关怀, 人文关怀 "humane concern". Written and used for institutions or leaders caring for others, and for an attentive person. 关 is "to be concerned" and 怀 is "to cherish" (the heart 忄).
column6: Lǎoshī hěn guānhuái měi ge xuésheng.
column7: The teacher cares about every student.
column9: Concern, care for people, shown with warmth: 關懷老人 "show care for the elderly", 得到關懷, 親切的關懷, 人文關懷 "humane concern". Written and used for institutions or leaders caring for others, and for an attentive person. 關 is "to be concerned" and 懷 is "to cherish" (the heart 忄).

column3: A return for effort or kindness; to repay: 得到回报 "be rewarded", 回报社会 "give back to society", 投资回报 "return on investment", 没有回报. As a noun, it is the result of work or money put in. As a verb, it means to repay a kindness. 回 "return" + 报 "report, repay". It can also mean to report back, in a work context.
column6: Tā de nǔlì dédào le huíbào.
column7: His efforts were rewarded.
column9: A return for effort or kindness; to repay: 得到回報 "be rewarded", 回報社會 "give back to society", 投資回報 "return on investment", 沒有回報. As a noun, it is the result of work or money put in. As a verb, it means to repay a kindness. 回 "return" + 報 "report, repay". It can also mean to report back, in a work context.

column3: To repay a kindness or favor: 报答父母 "repay one's parents", 报答恩情 "repay a debt of gratitude", 无以报答 "I can't repay you enough". It is used only for good turns and is somewhat formal and emotional. 回报 is more about results; 报答 is about gratitude. 答 here is "to answer, to respond" in the sense of answering a kindness.
column4: 我一定会报答你的恩情。
column5: 我一定會報答你的恩情。
column6: Wǒ yīdìng huì bàodá nǐ de ēnqíng.
column7: I will repay your kindness for sure.
column9: To repay a kindness or favor: 報答父母 "repay one's parents", 報答恩情 "repay a debt of gratitude", 無以報答 "I can't repay you enough". It is used only for good turns and is somewhat formal and emotional. 回報 is more about results; 報答 is about gratitude. 答 here is "to answer, to respond" in the sense of answering a kindness.

column3: Greeting card: 新年贺卡 "New Year card", 生日贺卡 "birthday card", 寄贺卡 "send a card", 电子贺卡 "e-card". 贺 is "to congratulate" and 卡 is a loan from English "card". 卡 is read kǎ in this sense, and it is drawn as 上 over 下, like something squeezed between up and down; it also has the reading qiǎ, "to be stuck".
column4: 我给朋友寄了一张贺卡。
column5: 我給朋友寄了一張賀卡。
column6: Wǒ gěi péngyou jì le yī zhāng hèkǎ.
column7: I sent my friend a greeting card.
column9: Greeting card: 新年賀卡 "New Year card", 生日賀卡 "birthday card", 寄賀卡 "send a card", 電子賀卡 "e-card". 賀 is "to congratulate" and 卡 is a loan from English "card". 卡 is read kǎ in this sense, and it is drawn as 上 over 下, like something squeezed between up and down; it also has the reading qiǎ, "to be stuck".

column3: To share something good, such as joy, experience or information: 分享快乐 "share joy", 分享经验 "share experience", 分享照片 "share photos", 和大家分享. On social media, 分享 is the "share" button. It is for giving others a part of something you enjoy, not for dividing a cost (that is 分担). 享 "to enjoy".
column4: 我想和大家分享这个好消息。
column5: 我想和大家分享這個好消息。
column6: Wǒ xiǎng hé dàjiā fēnxiǎng zhège hǎo xiāoxi.
column7: I'd like to share this good news with everyone.
column9: To share something good, such as joy, experience or information: 分享快樂 "share joy", 分享經驗 "share experience", 分享照片 "share photos", 和大家分享. On social media, 分享 is the "share" button. It is for giving others a part of something you enjoy, not for dividing a cost (that is 分擔). 享 "to enjoy".

column3: Too, excessively, usually of something undesirable: 过于紧张 "too nervous", 过于简单 "too simple", 过于担心 "worry too much", 不要过于… "don't be too…". It is a written word that goes before an adjective or verb. More formal than 太, and not used for praise: you cannot say 过于好. 过 here is "beyond", the same as in 过度.
column4: 他过于紧张，说不出话来。
column5: 他過於緊張，說不出話來。
column6: Tā guòyú jǐnzhāng, shuō bu chū huà lái.
column7: He was too nervous to say a word.
column9: Too, excessively, usually of something undesirable: 過於緊張 "too nervous", 過於簡單 "too simple", 過於擔心 "worry too much", 不要過於… "don't be too…". It is a written word that goes before an adjective or verb. More formal than 太, and not used for praise: you cannot say 過於好. 過 here is "beyond", the same as in 過度.

column3: Excessive, too much, to excess: 过度劳累 "overwork", 过度使用 "overuse", 过度饮酒 "drink to excess", 消费过度. It goes before a verb or noun as a modifier and is neutral to negative; the thing is too much of what is usually fine. 过 "beyond" + 度 "degree, measure": past the limit.
column4: 过度使用手机对眼睛不好。
column5: 過度使用手機對眼睛不好。
column6: Guòdù shǐyòng shǒujī duì yǎnjing bù hǎo.
column7: Overusing a phone is bad for the eyes.
column9: Excessive, too much, to excess: 過度勞累 "overwork", 過度使用 "overuse", 過度飲酒 "drink to excess", 消費過度. It goes before a verb or noun as a modifier and is neutral to negative; the thing is too much of what is usually fine. 過 "beyond" + 度 "degree, measure": past the limit.

column3: Full, complete, one hundred percent: 信心十足 "full of confidence", 十足的傻瓜 "a complete fool", 干劲十足 "full of energy". It follows the quality it adds to, with a noun like 信心 or 干劲: 信心十足. 十 is "ten", meaning a full measure, and 足 "enough, foot". 足 is a picture of a leg above the foot.
column6: Tā jīntiān xìnxīn shízú.
column7: He is full of confidence today.
column9: Full, complete, one hundred percent: 信心十足 "full of confidence", 十足的傻瓜 "a complete fool", 幹勁十足 "full of energy". It follows the quality it adds to, with a noun like 信心 or 幹勁: 信心十足. 十 is "ten", meaning a full measure, and 足 "enough, foot". 足 is a picture of a leg above the foot.

column3: Especially, in particular: 我喜欢水果，尤其是苹果 "I like fruit, especially apples", 尤其重要 "especially important", 尤其是…. It picks one thing out of a group as the most. Usually before an adjective, verb or 是 + noun. Compare 特别, which says "especially" in a more general sense; 尤其 needs a larger group to pick from.
column4: 我喜欢水果，尤其是苹果。
column5: 我喜歡水果，尤其是蘋果。
column6: Wǒ xǐhuan shuǐguǒ, yóuqí shì píngguǒ.
column7: I like fruit, especially apples.
column9: Especially, in particular: 我喜歡水果，尤其是蘋果 "I like fruit, especially apples", 尤其重要 "especially important", 尤其是…. It picks one thing out of a group as the most. Usually before an adjective, verb or 是 + noun. Compare 特別, which says "especially" in a more general sense; 尤其 needs a larger group to pick from.

column3: Slightly, a little: 稍等 "wait a moment", 稍大一点 "a little bigger", 稍作休息 "take a short rest", 稍有不同 "slightly different". It goes before a verb or adjective, and is written; in speech 稍微 is more common. 稍 has 禾 "grain" and 肖, which gives the sound.
column6: Qǐng shāo děng.
column7: Please wait a moment.
column9: Slightly, a little: 稍等 "wait a moment", 稍大一點 "a little bigger", 稍作休息 "take a short rest", 稍有不同 "slightly different". It goes before a verb or adjective, and is written; in speech 稍微 is more common. 稍 has 禾 "grain" and 肖, which gives the sound.

column3: A little, slightly: 稍微快一点儿 "a bit faster", 稍微休息一下 "rest a little", 稍微有点 + adjective "a bit…". It sits before a verb or adjective and is usually followed by 一点, 一下 or 有点, which soften it. 微 has the meaning "tiny".
column4: 今天比昨天稍微冷一点儿。
column5: 今天比昨天稍微冷一點兒。
column6: Jīntiān bǐ zuótiān shāowēi lěng yīdiǎnr.
column7: Today is a little colder than yesterday.
column9: A little, slightly: 稍微快一點兒 "a bit faster", 稍微休息一下 "rest a little", 稍微有點 + adjective "a bit…". It sits before a verb or adjective and is usually followed by 一點, 一下 or 有點, which soften it. 微 has the meaning "tiny".

column3: Almost, nearly (and it did not happen): 差点儿迟到了 "almost was late", 差点儿摔倒 "nearly fell". With an unwanted event, 差点儿 and 差点儿没 both say it almost happened and did not: 差点儿摔倒, 差点儿没摔倒. The 儿 ending is northern; in the south it is 差点. 差 is read chà here.
column6: Wǒ chàdiǎnr chídào le.
column7: I was almost late.
column9: Almost, nearly (and it did not happen): 差點兒遲到了 "almost was late", 差點兒摔倒 "nearly fell". With an unwanted event, 差點兒 and 差點兒沒 both say it almost happened and did not: 差點兒摔倒, 差點兒沒摔倒. The 兒 ending is northern; in the south it is 差點. 差 is read chà here.

column3: Almost, the same as 差点儿 with a full 一点儿: 差一点儿就成功了 "nearly succeeded", 差一点儿摔倒. It has the same meaning. It is a little stronger in speech, since 一点儿 stresses how small the gap was. 差 is read chà here, "to fall short".
column6: Wǒ chàyīdiǎnr wàng le.
column7: I almost forgot.
column9: Almost, the same as 差點兒 with a full 一點兒: 差一點兒就成功了 "nearly succeeded", 差一點兒摔倒. It has the same meaning. It is a little stronger in speech, since 一點兒 stresses how small the gap was. 差 is read chà here, "to fall short".

column3: Roughly, in general: 大致相同 "roughly the same", 大致了解 "get a rough idea", 大致可以 "more or less acceptable", 大致上. An adverb before a verb or adjective, a little formal. It gives the broad outline without exact details. 大 "big" + 致 "to reach, to result", so "in broad terms".
column6: Wǒ dàzhì kàn le yī biàn.
column7: I looked it over roughly.
column9: Roughly, in general: 大致相同 "roughly the same", 大致了解 "get a rough idea", 大致可以 "more or less acceptable", 大致上. An adverb before a verb or adjective, a little formal. It gives the broad outline without exact details. 大 "big" + 致 "to reach, to result", so "in broad terms".

column3: At least, at the minimum: 起码要一年 "it takes at least a year", 起码的要求 "the basic requirement", 起码的礼貌 "basic manners". As an adverb, it states the minimum; as a modifier, it means "basic". Spoken and flexible. 起 "start" + 码 "a mark of number", so "from the lowest number".
column4: 起码要学一年才能说好。
column5: 起碼要學一年才能說好。
column6: Qǐmǎ yào xué yī nián cái néng shuō hǎo.
column7: It takes at least a year of study to speak well.
column9: At least, at the minimum: 起碼要一年 "it takes at least a year", 起碼的要求 "the basic requirement", 起碼的禮貌 "basic manners". As an adverb, it states the minimum; as a modifier, it means "basic". Spoken and flexible. 起 "start" + 碼 "a mark of number", so "from the lowest number".

column3: Rare, hard to come by; also "not easy to find in someone": 难得的机会 "a rare chance", 很难得 "it is rare", 难得来一次 "seldom come". Also praise: 他这么年轻就这么稳重，真难得 "so young and so steady, that is commendable". 难 is read nán "difficult" here, and 得 de "obtain".
column6: Zhème hǎo de tiānqì hěn nándé.
column7: Such lovely weather is rare.
column9: Rare, hard to come by; also "not easy to find in someone": 難得的機會 "a rare chance", 很難得 "it is rare", 難得來一次 "seldom come". Also praise: 他這麼年輕就這麼穩重，真難得 "so young and so steady, that is commendable". 難 is read nán "difficult" here, and 得 de "obtain".

column3: Hard to, difficult to, before a verb: 难以相信 "hard to believe", 难以想象 "hard to imagine", 难以理解 "hard to understand", 难以形容. Written and formal, almost always with a verb of thinking or saying, and not used with 很. Spoken Chinese uses 很难 + verb for the same idea. 以 only joins it to the verb.
column6: Zhè zhǒng gǎnjué nányǐ xíngróng.
column7: This feeling is hard to describe.
column9: Hard to, difficult to, before a verb: 難以相信 "hard to believe", 難以想象 "hard to imagine", 難以理解 "hard to understand", 難以形容. Written and formal, almost always with a verb of thinking or saying, and not used with 很. Spoken Chinese uses 很難 + verb for the same idea. 以 only joins it to the verb.

column3: Not easy, difficult: 来之不易 "hard-won", 很不易 "it is not easy", 实属不易. Formal and written. It also means "unchanging" in a set phrase such as 千古不易. 易 is "easy", which is the opposite of 难; 易 is also in 容易 and 交易. 不易 is used in praise of effort: 成功很不易.
column6: Chénggōng hěn bùyì.
column7: Success is not easy.
column9: Not easy, difficult: 來之不易 "hard-won", 很不易 "it is not easy", 實屬不易. Formal and written. It also means "unchanging" in a set phrase such as 千古不易. 易 is "easy", which is the opposite of 難; 易 is also in 容易 and 交易. 不易 is used in praise of effort: 成功很不易.

column3: Inevitably, can't help but: 不免有些紧张 "can't help being a bit nervous", 不免担心 "naturally worried", 不免感到… "inevitably feel…". Said of an effect that follows from a situation. It goes before a verb and is written or formal, and most often with a negative feeling. 免 means "to avoid", so 不免 is "cannot avoid".
column4: 第一次上台，他不免有些紧张。
column5: 第一次上臺，他不免有些緊張。
column6: Dìyī cì shàngtái, tā bùmiǎn yǒuxiē jǐnzhāng.
column7: On stage for the first time, he could not help being a little nervous.
column9: Inevitably, can't help but: 不免有些緊張 "can't help being a bit nervous", 不免擔心 "naturally worried", 不免感到… "inevitably feel…". Said of an effect that follows from a situation. It goes before a verb and is written or formal, and most often with a negative feeling. 免 means "to avoid", so 不免 is "cannot avoid".

column3: As far as possible: 尽可能多 "as many as possible", 尽可能早 "as early as possible", 尽可能地帮助 "help as much as possible". The pattern is 尽可能 + adjective or verb, often with 地. 尽 is read jǐn here, "to the utmost", not jìn "to exhaust". Also written 尽量, which is more common in speech.
column6: Qǐng jǐnkěnéng zǎodiǎn lái.
column7: Please come as early as you can.
column9: As far as possible: 盡可能多 "as many as possible", 盡可能早 "as early as possible", 盡可能地幫助 "help as much as possible". The pattern is 盡可能 + adjective or verb, often with 地. 盡 is read jǐn here, "to the utmost", not jìn "to exhaust". Also written 盡量, which is more common in speech.

column3: To read aloud, clearly and with expression: 朗读课文 "read the text aloud", 大声朗读, 朗读比赛 "recitation contest". A language-learning exercise in China, used for reading out a text, poem or speech. 朗 means "bright, clear" (with 月 "moon" for the meaning), and 读 is "read". The 读 has 讠 "speech" on the left.
column4: 老师让我们大声朗读课文。
column5: 老師讓我們大聲朗讀課文。
column6: Lǎoshī ràng wǒmen dàshēng lǎngdú kèwén.
column7: The teacher had us read the text aloud.
column9: To read aloud, clearly and with expression: 朗讀課文 "read the text aloud", 大聲朗讀, 朗讀比賽 "recitation contest". A language-learning exercise in China, used for reading out a text, poem or speech. 朗 means "bright, clear" (with 月 "moon" for the meaning), and 讀 is "read". The 讀 has 言 "speech" on the left.

column3: To answer, to reply: 答题 "answer questions", 回答 "answer", 答对 "answer correctly", 答案 "the answer", 问答. Used for answering a question or a call. On its own it is somewhat written; in speech 回答 is usual, and 答 appears in set combinations. 答 has ⺮ "bamboo" on top and 合 "to fit" below.
column6: Tā dá de hěn duì.
column7: He answered correctly.
column9: To answer, to reply: 答題 "answer questions", 回答 "answer", 答對 "answer correctly", 答案 "the answer", 問答. Used for answering a question or a call. On its own it is somewhat written; in speech 回答 is usual, and 答 appears in set combinations. 答 has ⺮ "bamboo" on top and 合 "to fit" below.

column3: To reply formally, and a reply: 尽快答复 "reply soon", 等待答复 "wait for an answer", 给…一个答复 "give … an answer", 书面答复 "a written answer". It is mostly for questions, requests and proposals from a person or an organization, and it often means a definite answer (yes or no). More formal than 回答, which is for any question. 复 here has the sense "reply".
column6: Qǐng jǐnkuài dáfù wǒ.
column7: Please reply to me as soon as you can.
column9: To reply formally, and a reply: 盡快答復 "reply soon", 等待答復 "wait for an answer", 給…一個答復 "give … an answer", 書面答復 "a written answer". It is mostly for questions, requests and proposals from a person or an organization, and it often means a definite answer (yes or no). More formal than 回答, which is for any question. 復 here has the sense "reply".

column3: To ask about, to inquire: 询问价格 "ask the price", 询问情况 "ask about the situation", 向…询问. It is more formal than 问, and the thing you ask about follows. It is a polite or official way of asking for information, not for a casual question. 询 has 讠 "speech" and 旬, which gives the sound. 问 is "ask".
column6: Tā xúnwèn le jiàgé.
column7: He asked about the price.
column9: To ask about, to inquire: 詢問價格 "ask the price", 詢問情況 "ask about the situation", 向…詢問. It is more formal than 問, and the thing you ask about follows. It is a polite or official way of asking for information, not for a casual question. 詢 has 言 "speech" and 旬, which gives the sound. 問 is "ask".

column3: To guess: 猜一猜 "have a guess", 猜对了 "guessed right", 猜不到 "cannot guess", 猜谜语 "guess a riddle". The thing guessed follows directly or comes as a clause: 你猜他多大. Often in the doubled form 猜猜. 猜 has 犭 "dog" and 青 for the sound; 青 also gives the sound in 清 and 情.
column6: Nǐ cāi tā jīnnián duō dà?
column7: How old do you guess he is?
column9: To guess: 猜一猜 "have a guess", 猜對了 "guessed right", 猜不到 "cannot guess", 猜謎語 "guess a riddle". The thing guessed follows directly or comes as a clause: 你猜他多大. Often in the doubled form 猜猜. 猜 has 犭 "dog" and 青 for the sound; 青 also gives the sound in 清 and 情.

column3: To guess, to conjecture; a guess: 只是猜测 "just a guess", 据我猜测 "as I guess", 猜测原因 "guess the reason". More formal than 猜 and used for reasoned guesses in news and discussion; people say 猜 for a game or a quick guess. 测 is "to measure", so a guess is a rough measurement.
column6: Zhè zhǐshì wǒ de cāicè.
column7: This is only my guess.
column9: To guess, to conjecture; a guess: 只是猜測 "just a guess", 據我猜測 "as I guess", 猜測原因 "guess the reason". More formal than 猜 and used for reasoned guesses in news and discussion; people say 猜 for a game or a quick guess. 測 is "to measure", so a guess is a rough measurement.

column3: A slogan, a chant: 喊口号 "shout slogans", 提出口号 "put forward a slogan", 响亮的口号 "a catchy slogan". Used for a rallying cry at events, protests, marches and school sports days, and for advertising and political slogans. 口 "mouth" + 号 "call, number": a call said aloud. Note that 号 here is read hào, not háo.
column6: Dàjiā yīqǐ hǎn kǒuhào.
column7: Everyone shouted the slogan together.
column9: A slogan, a chant: 喊口號 "shout slogans", 提出口號 "put forward a slogan", 響亮的口號 "a catchy slogan". Used for a rallying cry at events, protests, marches and school sports days, and for advertising and political slogans. 口 "mouth" + 號 "call, number": a call said aloud. Note that 號 here is read hào, not háo.

column3: A way of putting it, a version or opinion: 这种说法 "this way of saying", 另一种说法 "another version", 官方说法 "the official line", 有一种说法 "one view has it that". The second syllable is neutral: shuōfa. Read shuōfǎ, it is another word, Buddhist: "to preach the teachings". 说 "say" + 法 "method".
column6: Zhè zhǒng shuōfa bù tài zhǔnquè.
column7: This way of putting it is not very accurate.
column9: A way of putting it, a version or opinion: 這種說法 "this way of saying", 另一種說法 "another version", 官方說法 "the official line", 有一種說法 "one view has it that". The second syllable is neutral: shuōfa. Read shuōfǎ, it is another word, Buddhist: "to preach the teachings". 說 "say" + 法 "method".

column3: Words, speech: 言语粗鲁 "rough words", 言语不通 "language barrier", 没有言语 "not say a word", 言语能力 "language ability". A written word for what a person says, which suggests their tone, or for language ability in speech. 言 is "speech", and 语 is "language", with 讠 "speech" on the left.
column4: 听了这些言语，他很生气。
column5: 聽了這些言語，他很生氣。
column6: Tīng le zhèxiē yányǔ, tā hěn shēngqì.
column7: Hearing these words made him angry.
column9: Words, speech: 言語粗魯 "rough words", 言語不通 "language barrier", 沒有言語 "not say a word", 言語能力 "language ability". A written word for what a person says, which suggests their tone, or for language ability in speech. 言 is "speech", and 語 is "language", with 言 "speech" on the left.

column3: The Chinese language, as Chinese people overseas, especially in Singapore and Malaysia, call it: 说华语 "speak Chinese", 华语教学 "Chinese teaching", 华语电影 "Chinese-language films". In Taiwan it is a name for Mandarin, as in 华语文. In mainland China people say 汉语 or 普通话. 华 is "China, Chinese" and 语 "language".
column6: Tā huì shuō Huáyǔ.
column7: He can speak Chinese.
column9: The Chinese language, as Chinese people overseas, especially in Singapore and Malaysia, call it: 說華語 "speak Chinese", 華語教學 "Chinese teaching", 華語電影 "Chinese-language films". In Taiwan it is a name for Mandarin, as in 華語文. In mainland China people say 漢語 or 普通話. 華 is "China, Chinese" and 語 "language".

column3: To pass on a message, an order or a feeling: 传达消息 "pass on news", 传达给大家 "convey to everyone", 传达室 "the reception desk of a building". The thing conveyed is a message, an instruction or a feeling, going from one person or group to another. 传 is "to pass on" and 达 "to reach", so something that arrives.
column4: 请把这个消息传达给大家。
column5: 請把這個消息傳達給大家。
column6: Qǐng bǎ zhège xiāoxi chuándá gěi dàjiā.
column7: Please pass this news on to everyone.
column9: To pass on a message, an order or a feeling: 傳達消息 "pass on news", 傳達給大家 "convey to everyone", 傳達室 "the reception desk of a building". The thing conveyed is a message, an instruction or a feeling, going from one person or group to another. 傳 is "to pass on" and 達 "to reach", so something that arrives.

column3: To misunderstand; a misunderstanding: 产生误解 "cause a misunderstanding", 消除误解 "clear up a misunderstanding", 误解了他 "misjudge him", 一场误解. Used for people and for ideas. 误 is "mistake" and 解 is "to understand, to untie". 解 shows a knife 刀 separating the horns 角 of an ox 牛.
column6: Zhè shì yī ge wùjiě.
column7: This is a misunderstanding.
column9: To misunderstand; a misunderstanding: 產生誤解 "cause a misunderstanding", 消除誤解 "clear up a misunderstanding", 誤解了他 "misjudge him", 一場誤解. Used for people and for ideas. 誤 is "mistake" and 解 is "to understand, to untie". 解 shows a knife 刀 separating the horns 角 of an ox 牛.

column3: To explain or instruct, to hand over, to account for: 交代工作 "give instructions about work", 交代清楚 "explain clearly", 交代一下, 交代任务. It can also mean to confess, as in 交代罪行, and to say what happened, as in 交代原因. A boss or a parent is the usual subject. Also in the phrase 没法交代 "cannot give an account".
column4: 老师交代了明天的作业。
column5: 老師交代了明天的作業。
column6: Lǎoshī jiāodài le míngtiān de zuòyè.
column7: The teacher gave instructions about tomorrow's homework.
column9: To explain or instruct, to hand over, to account for: 交代工作 "give instructions about work", 交代清楚 "explain clearly", 交代一下, 交代任務. It can also mean to confess, as in 交代罪行, and to say what happened, as in 交代原因. A boss or a parent is the usual subject. Also in the phrase 沒法交代 "cannot give an account".

column3: A subject of study, an academic discipline: 基础学科 "basic subjects", 理科学科 "science subjects", 学科考试, 跨学科 "interdisciplinary". Used in schools and universities for subjects as areas, like math, physics, history. For a course on a timetable, 课 is used. 科 has 禾 "grain" and 斗 "a measure", a hand measuring grain.
column4: 数学是我最喜欢的学科。
column5: 數學是我最喜歡的學科。
column6: Shùxué shì wǒ zuì xǐhuan de xuékē.
column7: Math is my favorite subject.
column9: A subject of study, an academic discipline: 基礎學科 "basic subjects", 理科學科 "science subjects", 學科考試, 跨學科 "interdisciplinary". Used in schools and universities for subjects as areas, like math, physics, history. For a course on a timetable, 課 is used. 科 has 禾 "grain" and 斗 "a measure", a hand measuring grain.

column3: To take a course as an elective; an elective: 选修课 "an elective course", 选修一门课 "take a course as an elective", 必修 "compulsory". Its opposite is 必修. At Chinese schools and universities, 选修课 is also a standard word. 选 "choose" + 修 "study, cultivate".
column6: Wǒ xuǎnxiū le yī mén Fǎyǔ kè.
column7: I took a French course as an elective.
column9: To take a course as an elective; an elective: 選修課 "an elective course", 選修一門課 "take a course as an elective", 必修 "compulsory". Its opposite is 必修. At Chinese schools and universities, 選修課 is also a standard word. 選 "choose" + 修 "study, cultivate".

column3: A research topic or problem; a project: 研究课题 "a research topic", 科研课题, 课题组 "research team", 新课题 "a new problem". Used in universities, research and policy for a topic being studied. Also used more loosely, for a problem to be tackled, as in 社会的新课题. 课 is "lesson" and 题 "topic, question".
column6: Zhège kètí hěn yǒu yìsi.
column7: This research topic is very interesting.
column9: A research topic or problem; a project: 研究課題 "a research topic", 科研課題, 課題組 "research team", 新課題 "a new problem". Used in universities, research and policy for a topic being studied. Also used more loosely, for a problem to be tackled, as in 社會的新課題. 課 is "lesson" and 題 "topic, question".

column3: To learn the basics, a first step into a subject; beginner level: 入门书 "an introductory book", 入门级 "entry level", 刚入门 "just starting", 很难入门. A book or course for beginners is 入门. It is a separable verb, the literal meaning being "to enter the door". Used for skills, hobbies and subjects.
column6: Zhè běn shū shìhé rùmén.
column7: This book suits beginners.
column9: To learn the basics, a first step into a subject; beginner level: 入門書 "an introductory book", 入門級 "entry level", 剛入門 "just starting", 很難入門. A book or course for beginners is 入門. It is a separable verb, the literal meaning being "to enter the door". Used for skills, hobbies and subjects.

column3: To know well, to be familiar with: 熟悉环境 "know the surroundings", 对…很熟悉 "be familiar with…", 不熟悉, 熟悉的声音 "a familiar voice". It is used for people, places and subjects, and it has the sense of having had time to get used to. 熟 means "ripe, cooked", with 灬 "fire", and 悉 "know all about".
column6: Wǒ duì zhège chéngshì hěn shúxī.
column7: I know this city very well.
column9: To know well, to be familiar with: 熟悉環境 "know the surroundings", 對…很熟悉 "be familiar with…", 不熟悉, 熟悉的聲音 "a familiar voice". It is used for people, places and subjects, and it has the sense of having had time to get used to. 熟 means "ripe, cooked", with 灬 "fire", and 悉 "know all about".

column3: To master, to have a grasp of; to hold in one's hands: 掌握技术 "master a skill", 掌握方法, 掌握情况 "be on top of the situation", 掌握命运 "control one's destiny". With a skill or knowledge, it means you know it well enough to use it; with power, it means to control it. 掌 is the palm and 握 "to grasp": you hold it in your hand.
column4: 他已经掌握了这门技术。
column5: 他已經掌握了這門技術。
column6: Tā yǐjīng zhǎngwò le zhè mén jìshù.
column7: He has already mastered this skill.
column9: To master, to have a grasp of; to hold in one's hands: 掌握技術 "master a skill", 掌握方法, 掌握情況 "be on top of the situation", 掌握命運 "control one's destiny". With a skill or knowledge, it means you know it well enough to use it; with power, it means to control it. 掌 is the palm and 握 "to grasp": you hold it in your hand.

column3: Memory, and to remember: 童年的记忆 "childhood memories", 记忆力 "the power of memory", 记忆犹新 "still fresh in the memory", 好的记忆. Used for the ability to remember and for particular memories, and as a written verb. 记 "record" + 忆 "recall". 忆 has 忄 "heart" and 乙, which gives the sound.
column6: Zhè shì wǒ tóngnián de jìyì.
column7: This is a memory from my childhood.
column9: Memory, and to remember: 童年的記憶 "childhood memories", 記憶力 "the power of memory", 記憶猶新 "still fresh in the memory", 好的記憶. Used for the ability to remember and for particular memories, and as a written verb. 記 "record" + 憶 "recall". 憶 has 忄 "heart" and 意, which gives the sound.

column3: To recall; memories: 回忆往事 "recall the past", 美好的回忆 "fond memories", 回忆起 "think back to", 回忆录 "memoirs". Unlike 记忆, which is the memory itself, 回忆 is the act of going back over the past and the images it brings. 回 "return" + 忆 "recall".
column6: Tā zài huíyì xiǎoshíhou de shì.
column7: He is remembering things from his childhood.
column9: To recall; memories: 回憶往事 "recall the past", 美好的回憶 "fond memories", 回憶起 "think back to", 回憶錄 "memoirs". Unlike 記憶, which is the memory itself, 回憶 is the act of going back over the past and the images it brings. 回 "return" + 憶 "recall".

column3: To look back on, to review: 回顾过去 "look back at the past", 回顾历史, 回顾一年的工作, 回顾展 "retrospective exhibition". Used for looking back at a period, an event or a career, often in reports or speeches. 回 "back" + 顾 "to look", where 顾 has 页 "head" on the right.
column4: 我们来回顾一下今年的工作。
column5: 我們來回顧一下今年的工作。
column6: Wǒmen lái huígù yīxià jīnnián de gōngzuò.
column7: Let's look back over this year's work.
column9: To look back on, to review: 回顧過去 "look back at the past", 回顧歷史, 回顧一年的工作, 回顧展 "retrospective exhibition". Used for looking back at a period, an event or a career, often in reports or speeches. 回 "back" + 顧 "to look", where 顧 has 頁 "head" on the right.

column3: To imitate, to copy: 模仿他说话 "imitate how he speaks", 模仿能力 "ability to imitate", 模仿秀 "impersonation show". Used for copying a person's voice, style or movement. It is neutral or positive, as when learning a language or a skill. For counterfeits, people say 仿冒. 模 has 木 and 莫, 仿 has 亻 "person".
column4: 孩子喜欢模仿大人说话。
column5: 孩子喜歡模仿大人說話。
column6: Háizi xǐhuan mófǎng dàrén shuōhuà.
column7: Children like to imitate how adults talk.
column9: To imitate, to copy: 模仿他說話 "imitate how he speaks", 模仿能力 "ability to imitate", 模仿秀 "impersonation show". Used for copying a person's voice, style or movement. It is neutral or positive, as when learning a language or a skill. For counterfeits, people say 仿冒. 模 has 木 and 莫, 仿 has 亻 "person".

column3: To demonstrate how to do something; a model example: 示范动作 "demonstrate a movement", 做示范 "give a demonstration", 示范作用 "a model effect", 示范区 "a model zone". A teacher or an expert shows the right way. 示 is an altar and, in compounds, "to show", and 范 "a model, a pattern".
column4: 老师先给我们示范了一遍。
column5: 老師先給我們示範了一遍。
column6: Lǎoshī xiān gěi wǒmen shìfàn le yī biàn.
column7: The teacher first demonstrated it for us.
column9: To demonstrate how to do something; a model example: 示範動作 "demonstrate a movement", 做示範 "give a demonstration", 示範作用 "a model effect", 示範區 "a model zone". A teacher or an expert shows the right way. 示 is an altar and, in compounds, "to show", and 範 "a model, a pattern".

column3: To inspire, to enlighten; an inspiration: 受到启发 "be inspired", 给我启发 "give me ideas", 启发式教学 "heuristic teaching". It says something gave someone a new idea or understanding, and it is not about feelings of excitement (that is 激励). 启 shows a door 户 being opened with a mouth 口, and 发 is "to send out".
column4: 这本书给了我很多启发。
column5: 這本書給了我很多啟發。
column6: Zhè běn shū gěi le wǒ hěn duō qǐfā.
column7: This book gave me a lot of inspiration.
column9: To inspire, to enlighten; an inspiration: 受到啟發 "be inspired", 給我啟發 "give me ideas", 啟發式教學 "heuristic teaching". It says something gave someone a new idea or understanding, and it is not about feelings of excitement (that is 激勵). 啟 shows a door 戶 being opened with a mouth 口, and 發 is "to send out".

column3: A dormitory, student housing: 学生宿舍 "student dorm", 住宿舍 "live in a dorm", 宿舍楼 "dormitory building", 宿舍管理员. In China most students and many workers have it. 宿 is read sù here ("to lodge"), and it shows a person under a roof 宀 on a mat. 舍 is "house".
column6: Wǒ de sùshè lí jiàoshì hěn jìn.
column7: My dormitory is very close to the classroom.
column9: A dormitory, student housing: 學生宿舍 "student dorm", 住宿舍 "live in a dorm", 宿舍樓 "dormitory building", 宿舍管理員. In China most students and many workers have it. 宿 is read sù here ("to lodge"), and it shows a person under a roof 宀 on a mat. 舍 is "house".

column3: A skill, a technical ability: 生活技能 "life skills", 职业技能 "job skills", 掌握技能, 技能培训 "skills training". It is a trained ability, usually practical; for natural talent, use 才能. 技 has 扌 "hand" and 支, and 能 is "ability", an old picture of a bear.
column6: Tā yǒu hěn duō shēnghuó jìnéng.
column7: He has many practical life skills.
column9: A skill, a technical ability: 生活技能 "life skills", 職業技能 "job skills", 掌握技能, 技能培訓 "skills training". It is a trained ability, usually practical; for natural talent, use 才能. 技 has 扌 "hand" and 支, and 能 is "ability", an old picture of a bear.

column3: An academic degree: 博士学位 "a doctorate", 硕士学位 "a master's degree", 获得学位 "earn a degree", 学位证书 "degree certificate". The degree in the sense of title, not the degree as in temperature. 学 "study" + 位 "place, position", where 位 shows a person 亻 standing 立 in a place.
column6: Tā zài dú bóshì xuéwèi.
column7: He is studying for a doctorate.
column9: An academic degree: 博士學位 "a doctorate", 碩士學位 "a master's degree", 獲得學位 "earn a degree", 學位證書 "degree certificate". The degree in the sense of title, not the degree as in temperature. 學 "study" + 位 "place, position", where 位 shows a person 亻 standing 立 in a place.

column3: To publish a book, magazine or recording: 出版社 "publishing house", 出版新书 "publish a new book", 出版物 "publications", 公开出版. The subject is usually a publisher or an author's work: 这本书已经出版了. 出 "out" + 版 "printing block, edition": to bring out an edition. 版 has 片 "slice, page" and 反 for the sound.
column6: Zhè běn shū qùnián chūbǎn le.
column7: This book was published last year.
column9: To publish a book, magazine or recording: 出版社 "publishing house", 出版新書 "publish a new book", 出版物 "publications", 公開出版. The subject is usually a publisher or an author's work: 這本書已經出版了. 出 "out" + 版 "printing block, edition": to bring out an edition. 版 has 片 "slice, page" and 反 for the sound.

column3: An edition, a version, and a page of a newspaper: 新版 "new edition", 头版 "front page", 版本 "version", 英文版 "English version", 版面 "layout". As a measure of editions it works as a noun: 第二版. On its own it is mostly a bound form; the compounds are where you meet it. 片 "slice" in 版 suggests a flat board.
column6: Zhè běn shū chū le xīn bǎn.
column7: A new edition of this book has come out.
column9: An edition, a version, and a page of a newspaper: 新版 "new edition", 頭版 "front page", 版本 "version", 英文版 "English version", 版面 "layout". As a measure of editions it works as a noun: 第二版. On its own it is mostly a bound form; the compounds are where you meet it. 片 "slice" in 版 suggests a flat board.

column3: Genuine, an authorized copy rather than a pirated one: 正版软件 "licensed software", 购买正版 "buy the real thing", 正版书, 支持正版. The opposite is 盗版 "pirated". Used for books, software, films, music and games. 正 "proper" + 版 "edition": the proper edition.
column6: Qǐng gòumǎi zhèngbǎn ruǎnjiàn.
column7: Please buy licensed software.
column9: Genuine, an authorized copy rather than a pirated one: 正版軟件 "licensed software", 購買正版 "buy the real thing", 正版書, 支持正版. The opposite is 盜版 "pirated". Used for books, software, films, music and games. 正 "proper" + 版 "edition": the proper edition.

column3: An electronic edition, a digital version: 电子版本 "digital version", 有电子版吗？ "is there a digital copy?", 发电子版 "send the file". The paper version is 纸质版. 电子 "electronic" + 版 "edition". It is a noun and is usually spoken about a document or book.
column6: Wǒ yǒu zhè běn shū de diànzǐbǎn.
column7: I have an electronic version of this book.
column9: An electronic edition, a digital version: 電子版本 "digital version", 有電子版嗎？ "is there a digital copy?", 發電子版 "send the file". The paper version is 紙質版. 電子 "electronic" + 版 "edition". It is a noun and is usually spoken about a document or book.

column3: To print, and printing: 印刷厂 "printing works", 印刷术 "the art of printing", 印刷质量 "print quality", 印刷品 "printed matter". Both characters have a sense of pressing or brushing ink onto a page. 刷 shows a person bent over with a towel 巾, the sense of brushing, and has 刂 on the right.
column6: Zhè běn shū yìnshuā de hěn qīngchu.
column7: This book is printed very clearly.
column9: To print, and printing: 印刷廠 "printing works", 印刷術 "the art of printing", 印刷質量 "print quality", 印刷品 "printed matter". Both characters have a sense of pressing or brushing ink onto a page. 刷 shows a person bent over with a towel 巾, the sense of brushing, and has 刂 on the right.

column3: To edit; an editor: 编辑文章 "edit an article", 她是编辑 "she is an editor", 责任编辑 "the editor in charge", 编辑部 "editorial office". The same word is the verb and the noun. On a computer, 编辑 is "edit" in menus. 编 has 纟 "thread" (arranging threads) and 辑 has 车 "cart".
column6: Tā zài chūbǎnshè dāng biānjí.
column7: She works as an editor at a publishing house.
column9: To edit; an editor: 編輯文章 "edit an article", 她是編輯 "she is an editor", 責任編輯 "the editor in charge", 編輯部 "editorial office". The same word is the verb and the noun. On a computer, 編輯 is "edit" in menus. 編 has 糹 "thread" (arranging threads) and 輯 has 車 "cart".

column3: A dictionary, mostly a dictionary of words and phrases rather than of single characters: 汉语辞典 "Chinese dictionary", 查辞典 "look it up in the dictionary". The more common spelling on the mainland is 词典, and it is the same word. 辞 shows a tongue 舌 and bitter 辛, and means "words, to resign".
column6: Zhè běn cídiǎn hěn hǎoyòng.
column7: This dictionary is very useful.
column9: A dictionary, mostly a dictionary of words and phrases rather than of single characters: 漢語辭典 "Chinese dictionary", 查辭典 "look it up in the dictionary". The more common spelling on the mainland is 詞典, and it is the same word. 辭 shows 辛 "bitter" on the right, and means "words, to resign".

column3: Prose, and especially the essay as a literary form: 写散文 "write essays", 散文集 "a collection of essays", 散文诗 "prose poem", 散文家 "essayist". In Chinese literature it is a form of its own, free in structure, covering essays, sketches and reflections, and it does not mean "novels". 散 is read sǎn here, "loose", not sàn.
column6: Tā xiě le yī piān sǎnwén.
column7: He wrote an essay.
column9: Prose, and especially the essay as a literary form: 寫散文 "write essays", 散文集 "a collection of essays", 散文詩 "prose poem", 散文家 "essayist". In Chinese literature it is a form of its own, free in structure, covering essays, sketches and reflections, and it does not mean "novels". 散 is read sǎn here, "loose", not sàn.

column3: Poetry, poems: 现代诗歌 "modern poetry", 诗歌朗诵 "poetry reading", 写诗歌, 古代诗歌. A general term for poetry as a whole. A single poem is 一首诗. 诗 is "poem" and 歌 "song", since poetry was once sung. 歌 has 欠 "yawning mouth" on the right.
column6: Tā xǐhuan dú xiàndài shīgē.
column7: She likes reading modern poetry.
column9: Poetry, poems: 現代詩歌 "modern poetry", 詩歌朗誦 "poetry reading", 寫詩歌, 古代詩歌. A general term for poetry as a whole. A single poem is 一首詩. 詩 is "poem" and 歌 "song", since poetry was once sung. 歌 has 欠 "yawning mouth" on the right.

column3: A set expression, usually of four characters, with a story or a classical source: 学成语 "learn idioms", 成语故事 "idiom story", 一个成语 "an idiom", 用成语. Learners meet them in HSK reading and writing, and they are used in speech and writing to sound educated. The meaning is often not the sum of the characters. 成 "become, form" + 语 "expression".
column6: Zhège chéngyǔ shì shénme yìsi?
column7: What does this idiom mean?
column9: A set expression, usually of four characters, with a story or a classical source: 學成語 "learn idioms", 成語故事 "idiom story", 一個成語 "an idiom", 用成語. Learners meet them in HSK reading and writing, and they are used in speech and writing to sound educated. The meaning is often not the sum of the characters. 成 "become, form" + 語 "expression".

column3: Subject matter, the theme of a work: 历史题材 "historical subject", 题材新颖 "original subject matter", 电影题材, 选择题材. It is what a book, film or painting is about. 题 is "topic" and 材 "material", so the material for a work. 材 has 木 "wood" and 才 for the sound.
column6: Zhè bù diànyǐng de tícái hěn xīn.
column7: The subject of this film is very fresh.
column9: Subject matter, the theme of a work: 歷史題材 "historical subject", 題材新穎 "original subject matter", 電影題材, 選擇題材. It is what a book, film or painting is about. 題 is "topic" and 材 "material", so the material for a work. 材 has 木 "wood" and 才 for the sound.

column3: The plot, the storyline of a work: 故事情节 "the plot", 情节复杂 "a complicated plot", 情节发展 "plot development", 案件情节 "details of a case". Used for stories, films and also for the details of a legal case. 情 "feeling, situation" + 节 "section". 节 comes from the sections of bamboo, and so means a part of something.
column4: 这个故事的情节很复杂。
column5: 這個故事的情節很複雜。
column6: Zhège gùshi de qíngjié hěn fùzá.
column7: The plot of this story is very complicated.
column9: The plot, the storyline of a work: 故事情節 "the plot", 情節複雜 "a complicated plot", 情節發展 "plot development", 案件情節 "details of a case". Used for stories, films and also for the details of a legal case. 情 "feeling, situation" + 節 "section". 節 comes from the sections of bamboo, and so means a part of something.

column3: Calligraphy: 练书法 "practice calligraphy", 书法家 "calligrapher", 书法比赛, 毛笔书法 "brush calligraphy". An art, and also a subject children take at school. 书 is "write" and 法 "method, way": the way of writing. 法 has 氵 "water" and 去 "go".
column6: Tā cóngxiǎo liànxí shūfǎ.
column7: He has practiced calligraphy since he was little.
column9: Calligraphy: 練書法 "practice calligraphy", 書法家 "calligrapher", 書法比賽, 毛筆書法 "brush calligraphy". An art, and also a subject children take at school. 書 is "write" and 法 "method, way": the way of writing. 法 has 氵 "water" and 去 "go".

column3: Literature and the arts: 文艺活动 "arts event", 文艺晚会 "a variety show", 文艺作品 "literary and artistic works", 文艺青年 "an arty young person". It is a broad term, used for performances, writing, music and other arts in general. In speech 文艺 is also a mild term for someone with artistic tastes. 艺 has 艹 "grass" and 乙.
column6: Tā xǐhuan wényì huódòng.
column7: She likes cultural events.
column9: Literature and the arts: 文藝活動 "arts event", 文藝晚會 "a variety show", 文藝作品 "literary and artistic works", 文藝青年 "an arty young person". It is a broad term, used for performances, writing, music and other arts in general. In speech 文藝 is also a mild term for someone with artistic tastes. 藝 has 艹 "grass" and 乙.

column3: A piano: 弹钢琴 "play the piano", 钢琴家 "pianist", 钢琴课, 钢琴曲. 钢 is "steel" (钅 "metal" and 冈), since the strings are steel, and 琴 is any stringed instrument. 琴 shows two strings above 今, which gives the sound. The verb for playing is 弹, and 练钢琴 means to practice.
column4: 她每天练一个小时钢琴。
column5: 她每天練一個小時鋼琴。
column6: Tā měitiān liàn yī ge xiǎoshí gāngqín.
column7: She practices the piano for an hour every day.
column9: A piano: 彈鋼琴 "play the piano", 鋼琴家 "pianist", 鋼琴課, 鋼琴曲. 鋼 is "steel" (釒 "metal" and 岡), since the strings are steel, and 琴 is any stringed instrument. 琴 shows two strings above 今, which gives the sound. The verb for playing is 彈, and 練鋼琴 means to practice.

column3: A stringed instrument. Used in names of many instruments: 钢琴 "piano", 小提琴 "violin", 古琴 (the zither), 口琴 "harmonica". On its own, 拉琴 is "play a bowed instrument" and 弹琴 "play one plucked with the fingers, or with keys". Two strings 玨 on top and 今 for the sound.
column6: Tā huì lā qín.
column7: She can play a bowed instrument.
column9: A stringed instrument. Used in names of many instruments: 鋼琴 "piano", 小提琴 "violin", 古琴 (the zither), 口琴 "harmonica". On its own, 拉琴 is "play a bowed instrument" and 彈琴 "play one plucked with the fingers, or with keys". Two strings 玨 on top and 今 for the sound.

column3: A song: 流行歌曲 "pop song", 经典歌曲, 一首歌曲, 歌曲排行榜 "chart". It is a slightly more formal word than 歌, for songs as pieces of music. The measure is 首: 一首歌曲. 曲 here means "tune", and it is read qǔ, not qū "bent" (though it is the same character, shown as a folded object).
column6: Zhè shǒu gēqǔ hěn hǎotīng.
column7: This song sounds lovely.
column9: A song: 流行歌曲 "pop song", 經典歌曲, 一首歌曲, 歌曲排行榜 "chart". It is a slightly more formal word than 歌, for songs as pieces of music. The measure is 首: 一首歌曲. 曲 here means "tune", and it is read qǔ, not qū "bent" (though it is the same character, shown as a folded object).

column3: An album, a special collection: 音乐专辑 "music album", 新专辑 "new album", 发行专辑 "release an album", 专辑封面. In music it is the usual word for an album; it can also mean a special issue or feature, as of a magazine. 专 "special" + 辑 "to compile", where 辑 has 车 "cart" and 咠 for the sound.
column4: 这位歌手出了一张新专辑。
column5: 這位歌手出了一張新專輯。
column6: Zhè wèi gēshǒu chū le yī zhāng xīn zhuānjí.
column7: This singer has released a new album.
column9: An album, a special collection: 音樂專輯 "music album", 新專輯 "new album", 發行專輯 "release an album", 專輯封面. In music it is the usual word for an album; it can also mean a special issue or feature, as of a magazine. 專 "special" + 輯 "to compile", where 輯 has 車 "cart" and 咠 for the sound.

column3: To dance, and a dance: 跳舞 "dance", 舞蹈 "dance, the art", 舞台 "stage", 舞会 "ball", 起舞. On its own as a verb it is poetic: 载歌载舞, 手舞足蹈 "dance for joy". In daily speech, 跳舞 is how you say it. 舞 has 舛, a pair of feet, under 無.
column6: Táishang de rén yòu chàng yòu wǔ.
column7: The people on the stage were singing and dancing.
column9: To dance, and a dance: 跳舞 "dance", 舞蹈 "dance, the art", 舞臺 "stage", 舞會 "ball", 起舞. On its own as a verb it is poetic: 載歌載舞, 手舞足蹈 "dance for joy". In daily speech, 跳舞 is how you say it. 舞 has 舛, a pair of feet, under 無.

column3: A play, a show, especially opera or drama: 看戏 "watch a play", 京戏 "Peking opera", 演戏 "act", 一出戏 "a play", 好戏 "a good show". It also means "play, joke": 戏弄. The measure for plays is 出: 一出戏. 戏 also has a figurative use, 没戏 "no chance". 戏 shows a hand 又 and a spear 戈.
column6: Zhè chū xì hěn hǎokàn.
column7: This play is very good to watch.
column9: A play, a show, especially opera or drama: 看戲 "watch a play", 京戲 "Peking opera", 演戲 "act", 一出戲 "a play", 好戲 "a good show". It also means "play, joke": 戲弄. The measure for plays is 齣: 一出戲. 戲 also has a figurative use, 沒戲 "no chance". 戲 shows 虍 and 豆 beside a spear 戈.

column3: Drama, theater as an art form: 戏剧表演 "drama performance", 戏剧节 "theater festival", 学习戏剧 "study drama", 戏剧性 "dramatic". It is a general term for stage plays, covering spoken drama and also opera. 戏 "play" + 剧 "drama". A single show is 一出戏, or 话剧 for a spoken drama.
column6: Tā zài dàxué xuéxí xìjù.
column7: He studies drama at university.
column9: Drama, theater as an art form: 戲劇表演 "drama performance", 戲劇節 "theater festival", 學習戲劇 "study drama", 戲劇性 "dramatic". It is a general term for stage plays, covering spoken drama and also opera. 戲 "play" + 劇 "drama". A single show is 一出戲, or 話劇 for a spoken drama.

column3: A comedy: 喜剧电影 "comedy film", 喜剧演员 "comedian", 看喜剧, 喜剧片. The opposite is 悲剧. 喜 "joy" + 剧 "drama". 喜 shows drums 壴 above a mouth 口: singing and drumming for joy.
column6: Wǒ xǐhuan kàn xǐjù diànyǐng.
column7: I like watching comedy films.
column9: A comedy: 喜劇電影 "comedy film", 喜劇演員 "comedian", 看喜劇, 喜劇片. The opposite is 悲劇. 喜 "joy" + 劇 "drama". 喜 shows drums 壴 above a mouth 口: singing and drumming for joy.

column3: To play a role, to act as: 扮演角色 "play a role", 扮演医生 "play a doctor", 扮演重要角色 "play an important part". It is also used outside the stage: 母亲扮演着重要角色 "mothers play an important role". 扮 "to dress up" and 演 "to perform". 演 has 氵 "water" and 寅 for sound.
column4: 她在电影里扮演一位老师。
column5: 她在電影裡扮演一位老師。
column6: Tā zài diànyǐng lǐ bànyǎn yī wèi lǎoshī.
column7: She plays a teacher in the film.
column9: To play a role, to act as: 扮演角色 "play a role", 扮演醫生 "play a doctor", 扮演重要角色 "play an important part". It is also used outside the stage: 母親扮演著重要角色 "mothers play an important role". 扮 "to dress up" and 演 "to perform". 演 has 氵 "water" and 寅 for sound.

column3: Crosstalk, a comic dialogue between two performers: 说相声 "perform crosstalk", 听相声, 相声演员. A traditional northern art, with fast jokes and wordplay, and now often heard on stage and online. 声 is neutral here, though it is shēng by itself. 相 is read xiàng here, "mutual, a pair".
column6: Tā xǐhuan tīng xiàngsheng.
column7: He likes listening to crosstalk.
column9: Crosstalk, a comic dialogue between two performers: 說相聲 "perform crosstalk", 聽相聲, 相聲演員. A traditional northern art, with fast jokes and wordplay, and now often heard on stage and online. 聲 is neutral here, though it is shēng by itself. 相 is read xiàng here, "mutual, a pair".

column3: A script, a play's text: 写剧本 "write a script", 电影剧本 "screenplay", 剧本创作, 改编剧本 "adapt a script". It is the written text for a play, film or TV series. 剧 "drama" + 本 "root, original, book". 本 is a tree 木 with its root marked by a stroke.
column6: Tā zhèngzài xiě yī ge jùběn.
column7: He is writing a script.
column9: A script, a play's text: 寫劇本 "write a script", 電影劇本 "screenplay", 劇本創作, 改編劇本 "adapt a script". It is the written text for a play, film or TV series. 劇 "drama" + 本 "root, original, book". 本 is a tree 木 with its root marked by a stroke.

column3: A drum, and to beat or to bulge: 敲鼓 "beat a drum", 打鼓, 鼓励 "encourage", 鼓起来 "swell up", 鼓掌 "applaud". As a verb it can mean to rouse, as in 鼓足勇气 "summon up courage". The left part 壴 is a drum, and the right 支 a hand with a stick.
column6: Háizi zài qiāo gǔ.
column7: The child is beating a drum.
column9: A drum, and to beat or to bulge: 敲鼓 "beat a drum", 打鼓, 鼓勵 "encourage", 鼓起來 "swell up", 鼓掌 "applaud". As a verb it can mean to rouse, as in 鼓足勇氣 "summon up courage". The left part 壴 is a drum, and the right 支 a hand with a stick.

column3: Sound, voice, tone: 声音 "sound", 大声 "loudly", 声调 "tone", 名声 "reputation", 声明 "statement". As a measure word it counts sounds and cries: 一声 "one cry", 叫了两声, said yìshēng. In names of the tones, 一声 is first tone, said yīshēng. On its own, it is the measure; the noun 声音 is more common for "sound".
column6: Wǒ tīngjiàn yī shēng jùxiǎng.
column7: I heard a loud bang.
column9: Sound, voice, tone: 聲音 "sound", 大聲 "loudly", 聲調 "tone", 名聲 "reputation", 聲明 "statement". As a measure word it counts sounds and cries: 一聲 "one cry", 叫了兩聲, said yìshēng. In names of the tones, 一聲 is first tone, said yīshēng. On its own, it is the measure; the noun 聲音 is more common for "sound".

column3: Photography, and to photograph or film: 摄影师 "photographer", 摄影展 "photo exhibition", 爱好摄影 "enjoy photography", 摄影机 "camera". The art and craft of taking pictures. For taking one photo, use 拍照. 摄 "to take in" + 影 "shadow, image". 影 has 彡 for light and 景 for sound.
column6: Tā xǐhuan shèyǐng.
column7: He likes photography.
column9: Photography, and to photograph or film: 攝影師 "photographer", 攝影展 "photo exhibition", 愛好攝影 "enjoy photography", 攝影機 "camera". The art and craft of taking pictures. For taking one photo, use 拍照. 攝 "to take in" + 影 "shadow, image". 影 has 彡 for light and 景 for sound.

column3: A photographer or a cinematographer: 专业摄影师 "professional photographer", 摄影师拍照, 电影摄影师 "director of photography". 师 is a suffix for a skilled person, as in 老师, 医师 and 厨师. The suffix needs the compound; 摄影 is the art, 摄影师 the person.
column6: Shèyǐngshī zhèngzài pāizhào.
column7: The photographer is taking pictures.
column9: A photographer or a cinematographer: 專業攝影師 "professional photographer", 攝影師拍照, 電影攝影師 "director of photography". 師 is a suffix for a skilled person, as in 老師, 醫師 and 廚師. The suffix needs the compound; 攝影 is the art, 攝影師 the person.

column3: To record video; video recording: 摄像头 "webcam, camera lens", 摄像设备 "recording equipment", 用手机摄像 "record on the phone", 摄像师 "videographer". It refers to video as opposed to still photos (摄影). 像 means "image, likeness", 亻 "person" with 象, which gives the sound.
column6: Tāmen yòng shǒujī shèxiàng.
column7: They are recording video on a phone.
column9: To record video; video recording: 攝像頭 "webcam, camera lens", 攝像設備 "recording equipment", 用手機攝像 "record on the phone", 攝像師 "videographer". It refers to video as opposed to still photos (攝影). 像 means "image, likeness", 亻 "person" with 象, which gives the sound.

column3: A video camera: 数码摄像机 "digital video camera", 一台摄像机, 摄像机镜头. 机 "machine" is the ending for devices: 照相机, 收音机, 飞机. The measure is 台. Nowadays phones do the job, so it is more often a specialized machine.
column6: Tā mǎi le yī tái shèxiàngjī.
column7: He bought a video camera.
column9: A video camera: 數碼攝像機 "digital video camera", 一臺攝像機, 攝像機鏡頭. 機 "machine" is the ending for devices: 照相機, 收音機, 飛機. The measure is 臺. Nowadays phones do the job, so it is more often a specialized machine.

column3: To shoot a film or take photos: 拍摄电影 "shoot a film", 拍摄照片 "take photos", 拍摄现场 "filming location", 拍摄技巧. More formal and professional than 拍, which is the everyday verb. 拍 has 扌 "hand" and 白 for the sound; 摄 is "to capture".
column6: Zhè bù diànyǐng zài Běijīng pāishè.
column7: This film was shot in Beijing.
column9: To shoot a film or take photos: 拍攝電影 "shoot a film", 拍攝照片 "take photos", 拍攝現場 "filming location", 拍攝技巧. More formal and professional than 拍, which is the everyday verb. 拍 has 扌 "hand" and 白 for the sound; 攝 is "to capture".

column3: A picture, scene on a screen or in a film or painting: 电影画面 "film picture", 画面清晰 "the picture is clear", 美丽的画面, 静止画面 "still frame". It is the visible image as a whole, and in a computer it is the screen contents. 画 is "picture" and 面 "surface". 画 shows a painting on an easel.
column6: Diànyǐng de huàmiàn hěn měi.
column7: The pictures in the film are beautiful.
column9: A picture, scene on a screen or in a film or painting: 電影畫面 "film picture", 畫面清晰 "the picture is clear", 美麗的畫面, 靜止畫面 "still frame". It is the visible image as a whole, and in a computer it is the screen contents. 畫 is "picture" and 面 "surface". 畫 shows a painting on an easel.

column3: Comics, cartoons; a caricature: 看漫画 "read comics", 漫画家 "cartoonist", 日本漫画, 漫画书. It covers manga and other comic art, and also a single satirical cartoon. 漫 "casual" + 画 "picture". 漫 has 氵 "water" and 曼 for the sound.
column6: Háizi xǐhuan kàn mànhuà.
column7: Children like to read comics.
column9: Comics, cartoons; a caricature: 看漫畫 "read comics", 漫畫家 "cartoonist", 日本漫畫, 漫畫書. It covers manga and other comic art, and also a single satirical cartoon. 漫 "casual" + 畫 "picture". 漫 has 氵 "water" and 曼 for the sound.

column3: An exhibition; to put on display: 举办展览 "hold an exhibition", 参观展览 "visit an exhibition", 艺术展览 "art exhibition", 展览馆 "exhibition hall". It is both a noun and a verb. 展 "to spread out" + 览 "to view". 展 once pictured clothes laid out for sale. 览 has 见 "see".
column6: Zhège zhǎnlǎn hěn shòu huānyíng.
column7: This exhibition is very popular.
column9: An exhibition; to put on display: 舉辦展覽 "hold an exhibition", 參觀展覽 "visit an exhibition", 藝術展覽 "art exhibition", 展覽館 "exhibition hall". It is both a noun and a verb. 展 "to spread out" + 覽 "to view". 展 once pictured clothes laid out for sale. 覽 has 見 "see".

column3: To show, to display: 展示成果 "show results", 展示才华 "show one's talent", 展示产品 "display a product", 向大家展示. It is a clear and open showing, with stress on bringing something into view. 示 shows an altar and carries the sense of "to show". Compare 展览, which is for an exhibition.
column4: 他向大家展示了新产品。
column5: 他向大家展示了新產品。
column6: Tā xiàng dàjiā zhǎnshì le xīn chǎnpǐn.
column7: He showed everyone the new product.
column9: To show, to display: 展示成果 "show results", 展示才華 "show one's talent", 展示產品 "display a product", 向大家展示. It is a clear and open showing, with stress on bringing something into view. 示 shows an altar and carries the sense of "to show". Compare 展覽, which is for an exhibition.

column3: A scene, a sight: 热闹的景象 "a lively scene", 一派繁荣景象 "a scene of prosperity", 眼前的景象 "the sight before one's eyes". Used for what you see in front of you, often full of life or feeling. 景 shows the sun 日 over a city 京, and 象 is "image". Not the same as 画面, which is on a screen.
column6: Yǎnqián de jǐngxiàng ràng rén nánwàng.
column7: The sight before our eyes was unforgettable.
column9: A scene, a sight: 熱鬧的景象 "a lively scene", 一派繁榮景象 "a scene of prosperity", 眼前的景象 "the sight before one's eyes". Used for what you see in front of you, often full of life or feeling. 景 shows the sun 日 over a city 京, and 象 is "image". Not the same as 畫面, which is on a screen.

column3: Scenery, a view: 田园风光 "rural scenery", 北国风光 "scenery of the north", 风光秀丽 "beautiful scenery". Also, in speech, "grand, honored": 风光无限 "full of glory", 很风光. 风 "wind" + 光 "light". 光 shows fire over a person.
column6: Zhèlǐ de fēngguāng hěn měi.
column7: The scenery here is very beautiful.
column9: Scenery, a view: 田園風光 "rural scenery", 北國風光 "scenery of the north", 風光秀麗 "beautiful scenery". Also, in speech, "grand, honored": 風光無限 "full of glory", 很風光. 風 "wind" + 光 "light". 光 shows fire over a person.

column3: Craft, technology of making things: 传统工艺 "traditional craft", 工艺品 "handicrafts", 制作工艺, 工艺美术 "arts and crafts". It names the method or skill of making something, from handicrafts to industrial processes. 工 is a tool, and 艺 "art, skill".
column6: Zhè shì yī zhǒng chuántǒng gōngyì.
column7: This is a traditional craft.
column9: Craft, technology of making things: 傳統工藝 "traditional craft", 工藝品 "handicrafts", 製作工藝, 工藝美術 "arts and crafts". It names the method or skill of making something, from handicrafts to industrial processes. 工 is a tool, and 藝 "art, skill".

column3: To show, to reveal, to unfold before one's eyes: 展现魅力 "show off charm", 展现在眼前 "unfold before one's eyes", 充分展现, 展现出. The thing shown becomes visible, with 出 or 在: 展现出美丽. 展 "to spread" + 现 "to appear", where 现 pairs 王 "jade" with 见 "see".
column4: 这幅画展现了乡村的美。
column5: 這幅畫展現了鄉村的美。
column6: Zhè fú huà zhǎnxiàn le xiāngcūn de měi.
column7: This painting shows the beauty of the countryside.
column9: To show, to reveal, to unfold before one's eyes: 展現魅力 "show off charm", 展現在眼前 "unfold before one's eyes", 充分展現, 展現出. The thing shown becomes visible, with 出 or 在: 展現出美麗. 展 "to spread" + 現 "to appear", where 現 pairs 王 "jade" with 見 "see".

column3: To show, to appear, obvious: 显得 "appear, look", 显然 "obviously", 显示 "display", 明显 "clear", 显出. On its own it means to show or to be visible, as in 显在脸上. Rarely used alone in speech; compounds like 明显 are more common. 日 "sun" is the meaning part.
column6: Tā de gāoxìng xiǎn zài liǎn shang.
column7: His joy showed on his face.
column9: To show, to appear, obvious: 顯得 "appear, look", 顯然 "obviously", 顯示 "display", 明顯 "clear", 顯出. On its own it means to show or to be visible, as in 顯在臉上. Rarely used alone in speech; compounds like 明顯 are more common. 日 "sun" is the meaning part.

column3: Badminton, and the shuttlecock: 打羽毛球 "play badminton", 羽毛球拍 "badminton racket", 羽毛球场 "court". 羽毛 "feather" + 球 "ball": the shuttlecock is made of feathers. The verb is 打. Badminton is very popular in China, and Chinese players are among the best. 羽 is a pair of feathers and 毛 a single one.
column6: Wǒmen zhōumò dǎ yǔmáoqiú.
column7: We play badminton at the weekend.
