column9: Badminton, and the shuttlecock: 打羽毛球 "play badminton", 羽毛球拍 "badminton racket", 羽毛球場 "court". 羽毛 "feather" + 球 "ball": the shuttlecock is made of feathers. The verb is 打. Badminton is very popular in China, and Chinese players are among the best. 羽 is a pair of feathers and 毛 a single one.

column3: A referee, a judge; to referee: 当裁判 "be the referee", 裁判员 "official", 裁判长 "chief judge", 裁判结果, 裁判比赛. In sport it is the referee or umpire, and in law the judgment of a court. 裁 once meant cutting cloth, and is now "to decide"; 判 "to judge" has 刂 "knife" and 半 for sound.
column6: Cáipàn chuī le shàozi.
column7: The referee blew the whistle.
column9: A referee, a judge; to referee: 當裁判 "be the referee", 裁判員 "official", 裁判長 "chief judge", 裁判結果, 裁判比賽. In sport it is the referee or umpire, and in law the judgment of a court. 裁 once meant cutting cloth, and is now "to decide"; 判 "to judge" has 刂 "knife" and 半 for sound.

column3: A champion; first place: 世界冠军 "world champion", 获得冠军 "win the title", 冠军赛 "championship", 拿冠军. 冠 is read guàn here, "first, best" (and guān for a hat). Second place is 亚军, third 季军. 冠 shows a man putting on a cap with his hand; 军 is "army", the team.
column6: Tā dé le yóuyǒng guànjūn.
column7: She won the swimming championship.
column9: A champion; first place: 世界冠軍 "world champion", 獲得冠軍 "win the title", 冠軍賽 "championship", 拿冠軍. 冠 is read guàn here, "first, best" (and guān for a hat). Second place is 亞軍, third 季軍. 冠 shows a man putting on a cap with his hand; 軍 is "army", the team.

column3: Second place, runner-up: 获得亚军 "take second place", 亚军奖杯, 夺得亚军. The ranking is 冠军, 亚军, 季军. 亚 here is "second", 军 is the team or group.
column6: Wǒmen duì dé le yàjūn.
column7: Our team came second.
column9: Second place, runner-up: 獲得亞軍 "take second place", 亞軍獎杯, 奪得亞軍. The ranking is 冠軍, 亞軍, 季軍. 亞 here is "second", 軍 is the team or group.

column3: A competition, a contest; to compete: 数学竞赛 "math contest", 体育竞赛 "sports competition", 知识竞赛 "quiz", 参加竞赛, 竞赛项目. It is a formal contest with rules and a prize. 竞 "to compete" + 赛 "match, race". 竞 shows two people standing 立 facing off.
column6: Xuéxiào jǔbàn le shùxué jìngsài.
column7: The school held a math competition.
column9: A competition, a contest; to compete: 數學競賽 "math contest", 體育競賽 "sports competition", 知識競賽 "quiz", 參加競賽, 競賽項目. It is a formal contest with rules and a prize. 競 "to compete" + 賽 "match, race". 競 shows two people standing 立 facing off.

column3: A grand prix, a major prize competition: 国际大奖赛 "international grand prix", 钢琴大奖赛, 方程式大奖赛 "the Formula One Grand Prix". 大 "big" + 奖 "prize" + 赛 "contest". A three-character word, in which 赛 is a suffix-like ending as in 比赛, 决赛.
column6: Tā cānjiā le guójì dàjiǎngsài.
column7: He took part in the international grand prix.
column9: A grand prix, a major prize competition: 國際大獎賽 "international grand prix", 鋼琴大獎賽, 方程式大獎賽 "the Formula One Grand Prix". 大 "big" + 獎 "prize" + 賽 "contest". A three-character word, in which 賽 is a suffix-like ending as in 比賽, 決賽.

column3: Victory or defeat, the outcome: 决定胜负 "decide the outcome", 分出胜负 "settle who wins", 不分胜负 "end in a draw", 胜负已定. Two opposites joined: 胜 "win" and 负 "lose, be defeated". Used for contests and fights, and also for any rivalry.
column6: Bǐsài de shèngfù hái hěn nán shuō.
column7: It is still hard to say who will win the match.
column9: Victory or defeat, the outcome: 決定勝負 "decide the outcome", 分出勝負 "settle who wins", 不分勝負 "end in a draw", 勝負已定. Two opposites joined: 勝 "win" and 負 "lose, be defeated". Used for contests and fights, and also for any rivalry.

column3: To open a conference, an exhibition or a festival: 开幕式 "opening ceremony", 展览开幕 "the exhibition opens", 会议开幕, 开幕词. Literally "to open the curtain". The opposite is 闭幕. It is a separable verb, so the date can follow: 明天开幕. 幕 has 巾 "cloth" at the bottom, meaning a curtain.
column6: Zhǎnlǎn míngtiān kāimù.
column7: The exhibition opens tomorrow.
column9: To open a conference, an exhibition or a festival: 開幕式 "opening ceremony", 展覽開幕 "the exhibition opens", 會議開幕, 開幕詞. Literally "to open the curtain". The opposite is 閉幕. It is a separable verb, so the date can follow: 明天開幕. 幕 has 巾 "cloth" at the bottom, meaning a curtain.

column3: An opening ceremony: 奥运会开幕式 "the opening ceremony of the Olympics", 参加开幕式, 开幕式表演. 式 here is a suffix meaning "ceremony" or "style".
column4: 开幕式在晚上八点开始。
column5: 開幕式在晚上八點開始。
column6: Kāimùshì zài wǎnshang bā diǎn kāishǐ.
column7: The opening ceremony starts at eight in the evening.
column9: An opening ceremony: 奧運會開幕式 "the opening ceremony of the Olympics", 參加開幕式, 開幕式表演. 式 here is a suffix meaning "ceremony" or "style".

column3: To close an event, to end a meeting or a show: 闭幕式 "closing ceremony", 会议闭幕 "the meeting ends", 闭幕词 "closing speech". Literally "the curtain closes". It pairs with 开幕. A separable verb. 闭 "to close" has 门 "door" on the outside.
column6: Bǐsài zuótiān bìmù le.
column7: The competition closed yesterday.
column9: To close an event, to end a meeting or a show: 閉幕式 "closing ceremony", 會議閉幕 "the meeting ends", 閉幕詞 "closing speech". Literally "the curtain closes". It pairs with 開幕. A separable verb. 閉 "to close" has 門 "door" on the outside.

column3: A closing ceremony: 闭幕式表演 "closing performance", 参加闭幕式, 奥运会闭幕式. It pairs with 开幕式. In sports and conferences, the two ceremonies mark the beginning and the end. 式 "ceremony" is a suffix: 闭幕 + 式.
column6: Bìmùshì fēicháng jīngcǎi.
column7: The closing ceremony was wonderful.
column9: A closing ceremony: 閉幕式表演 "closing performance", 參加閉幕式, 奧運會閉幕式. It pairs with 開幕式. In sports and conferences, the two ceremonies mark the beginning and the end. 式 "ceremony" is a suffix: 閉幕 + 式.

column3: A ceremony, a celebration: 毕业典礼 "graduation ceremony", 开学典礼 "opening-of-term ceremony", 结婚典礼 "wedding", 隆重的典礼. It is a formal ceremony with ritual and speeches, for public occasions at schools and organizations. 典 means "rules, canon" and 礼 "rite, courtesy".
column6: Bìyè diǎnlǐ zài lǐtáng jǔxíng.
column7: The graduation ceremony is held in the hall.
column9: A ceremony, a celebration: 畢業典禮 "graduation ceremony", 開學典禮 "opening-of-term ceremony", 結婚典禮 "wedding", 隆重的典禮. It is a formal ceremony with ritual and speeches, for public occasions at schools and organizations. 典 means "rules, canon" and 禮 "rite, courtesy".

column3: To compete; competition: 竞争对手 "rival", 激烈的竞争 "fierce competition", 公平竞争 "fair competition", 竞争力 "competitiveness". Used for business, jobs, markets and contests in general. It is a verb and a noun: 公司之间竞争. 竞 "to compete" + 争 "to strive, to fight for".
column4: 公司之间的竞争很激烈。
column5: 公司之間的競爭很激烈。
column6: Gōngsī zhījiān de jìngzhēng hěn jīliè.
column7: The competition between companies is fierce.
column9: To compete; competition: 競爭對手 "rival", 激烈的競爭 "fierce competition", 公平競爭 "fair competition", 競爭力 "competitiveness". Used for business, jobs, markets and contests in general. It is a verb and a noun: 公司之間競爭. 競 "to compete" + 爭 "to strive, to fight for".

column3: To reward; a reward: 奖励学生 "reward students", 物质奖励 "material reward", 奖励制度 "reward system", 得到奖励. A reward for good work or results, to encourage; it is not a punishment's opposite in general (that is 惩罚). 奖 "prize" + 励 "to encourage", where 励 has 力 "strength".
column6: Lǎoshī jiǎnglì le tā yī běn shū.
column7: The teacher rewarded him with a book.
column9: To reward; a reward: 獎勵學生 "reward students", 物質獎勵 "material reward", 獎勵制度 "reward system", 得到獎勵. A reward for good work or results, to encourage; it is not a punishment's opposite in general (that is 懲罰). 獎 "prize" + 勵 "to encourage", where 勵 has 力 "strength".

column3: To put together, to fight with all one has: 拼命 "go all out", 拼搏 "struggle hard", 拼图 "jigsaw", 拼音 "pinyin", 拼车 "carpool", 拼一拼 "give it a go". The sense of joining runs to the sense of risking everything for a goal: 拼到最后 "fight to the end". 拼 has 扌 "hand" and 并 for the sound, "side by side".
column6: Wǒmen yào pīn dào zuìhòu.
column7: We must fight until the end.
column9: To put together, to fight with all one has: 拼命 "go all out", 拼搏 "struggle hard", 拼圖 "jigsaw", 拼音 "pinyin", 拼車 "carpool", 拼一拼 "give it a go". The sense of joining runs to the sense of risking everything for a goal: 拼到最後 "fight to the end". 拼 has 扌 "hand" and 并 for the sound, "side by side".

column3: To shoot, to fire, to emit: 射箭 "shoot an arrow, archery", 射门 "shoot at goal", 射中 "hit the target", 发射 "launch", 照射 "shine on", 射线 "ray". It covers anything sent out in a line, such as arrows, balls and light. 射 shows a bow 身 and a hand 寸.
column6: Tā yī jiàn shè zhòng le mùbiāo.
column7: He hit the target with one arrow.
column9: To shoot, to fire, to emit: 射箭 "shoot an arrow, archery", 射門 "shoot at goal", 射中 "hit the target", 發射 "launch", 照射 "shine on", 射線 "ray". It covers anything sent out in a line, such as arrows, balls and light. 射 shows a bow 身 and a hand 寸.

column3: Shooting, firing a gun, as a sport and in war: 射击比赛 "shooting competition", 射击运动员 "shooter", 练习射击, 向目标射击. As a sport it is an Olympic event. 射 "shoot" + 击 "strike".
column6: Tā zài liànxí shèjī.
column7: He is practicing shooting.
column9: Shooting, firing a gun, as a sport and in war: 射擊比賽 "shooting competition", 射擊運動員 "shooter", 練習射擊, 向目標射擊. As a sport it is an Olympic event. 射 "shoot" + 擊 "strike".

column3: A key on a keyboard or a button on a device: 按键 "press a key", 回车键 "the Enter key". It is mostly met in compounds such as 键盘 and 关键 "crucial". The 钅 on the left is the metal radical, the same one you know from 钱 and 铁.
column6: Qǐng àn zhège jiàn.
column7: Please press this key.
column9: A key on a keyboard or a button on a device: 按鍵 "press a key", 回車鍵 "the Enter key". It is mostly met in compounds such as 鍵盤 and 關鍵 "crucial". The 釒 on the left is the metal radical, the same one you know from 錢 and 鐵.

column3: A computer or piano keyboard: 敲键盘 "tap on the keyboard", 键盘上 "on the keyboard". 键 is one key and 盘 a flat tray or disk, so it is "the tray of keys". 盘 also appears in 光盘 "CD" and 棋盘 "chessboard".
column6: Wǒ de jiànpán huài le.
column7: My keyboard is broken.
column9: A computer or piano keyboard: 敲鍵盤 "tap on the keyboard", 鍵盤上 "on the keyboard". 鍵 is one key and 盤 a flat tray or disk, so it is "the tray of keys". 盤 also appears in 光盤 "CD" and 棋盤 "chessboard".

column3: The computer mouse: 点击鼠标, 鼠标垫 "mouse pad", 移动鼠标. 鼠 is the animal "mouse" (a picture of one, with paws and a tail) and 标 a mark or pointer, so the word is literally "mouse pointer". The animal itself is 老鼠.
column6: Qǐng yòng shǔbiāo diǎn yīxià zhèlǐ.
column7: Please click here with the mouse.
column9: The computer mouse: 點擊鼠標, 鼠標墊 "mouse pad", 移動鼠標. 鼠 is the animal "mouse" (a picture of one, with paws and a tail) and 標 a mark or pointer, so the word is literally "mouse pointer". The animal itself is 老鼠.

column3: Software, the programs on a computer or phone: 下载软件, 安装软件, 办公软件 "office software". It is "soft items": 软 "soft" and 件, a measure word for items, which can be remembered as a man 亻 dividing up a cow 牛. The opposite is 硬件.
column4: 这个软件可以免费下载。
column5: 這個軟件可以免費下載。
column6: Zhège ruǎnjiàn kěyǐ miǎnfèi xiàzài.
column7: You can download this software for free.
column9: Software, the programs on a computer or phone: 下載軟件, 安裝軟件, 辦公軟件 "office software". It is "soft items": 軟 "soft" and 件, a measure word for items, which can be remembered as a man 亻 dividing up a cow 牛. The opposite is 硬件.

column3: Hardware, the physical parts of a computer: 电脑硬件, 硬件设施. The pair of 软件, with 硬 "hard" in place of 软 "soft". 硬件 can also mean facilities in general, such as a school's buildings and equipment, as opposed to 软件 for teaching quality and management.
column6: Zhè tái diànnǎo de yìngjiàn hěn hǎo.
column7: This computer has very good hardware.
column9: Hardware, the physical parts of a computer: 電腦硬件, 硬件設施. The pair of 軟件, with 硬 "hard" in place of 軟 "soft". 硬件 can also mean facilities in general, such as a school's buildings and equipment, as opposed to 軟件 for teaching quality and management.

column3: A robot: 扫地机器人 "robot vacuum cleaner", 聊天机器人 "chatbot". It is simply 机器 "machine" plus 人 "person". 机器人 is the usual word for both factory robots and software that talks to you.
column6: Zhège jīqìrén huì shuōhuà.
column7: This robot can talk.
column9: A robot: 掃地機器人 "robot vacuum cleaner", 聊天機器人 "chatbot". It is simply 機器 "machine" plus 人 "person". 機器人 is the usual word for both factory robots and software that talks to you.

column3: A QR code: 扫二维码 "scan a QR code" is something you do daily in China, to pay, add a contact or open a page. It is "two-dimensional code": 二 "two", 维 "dimension" and 码 "code, number", the 码 of 号码 and 密码.
column6: Qǐng sǎo yīxià zhège èrwéimǎ.
column7: Please scan this QR code.
column9: A QR code: 掃二維碼 "scan a QR code" is something you do daily in China, to pay, add a contact or open a page. It is "two-dimensional code": 二 "two", 維 "dimension" and 碼 "code, number", the 碼 of 號碼 and 密碼.

column3: A TV or radio channel, also a channel on a video site: 换频道 "change the channel", 体育频道 "sports channel". 频 means "frequency" and 道 "way", so a channel is a path on a frequency. 频 also occurs in 视频.
column6: Qǐng huàn yī ge píndào.
column7: Please change to another channel.
column9: A TV or radio channel, also a channel on a video site: 換頻道 "change the channel", 體育頻道 "sports channel". 頻 means "frequency" and 道 "way", so a channel is a path on a frequency. 頻 also occurs in 視頻.

column3: To search, especially online or through a database: 搜索引擎 "search engine", 在网上搜索资料. It looks through a whole body of data, while 找 means to look for one thing. The 扌 "hand" in 搜 shows a hands-on search.
column4: 我在网上搜索了很多资料。
column5: 我在網上搜索了很多資料。
column6: Wǒ zài wǎngshàng sōusuǒ le hěn duō zīliào.
column7: I searched the internet for a lot of information.
column9: To search, especially online or through a database: 搜索引擎 "search engine", 在網上搜索資料. It looks through a whole body of data, while 找 means to look for one thing. The 扌 "hand" in 搜 shows a hands-on search.

column3: A blog, and also its author: 写博客 "write a blog", 博客文章 "blog post". It is a sound-loan from English "blog". The 客 "guest" is used for a kind of person, as in 黑客 "hacker". Weibo-style short posts have taken over much of this, see 微博.
column6: Tā měitiān dōu xiě bókè.
column7: He writes his blog every day.
column9: A blog, and also its author: 寫博客 "write a blog", 博客文章 "blog post". It is a sound-loan from English "blog". The 客 "guest" is used for a kind of person, as in 黑客 "hacker". Weibo-style short posts have taken over much of this, see 微博.

column3: A microblog, and nearly always "Weibo", the Chinese platform like Twitter: 发微博 "post on Weibo", 刷微博 "scroll Weibo". 微 "tiny" plus 博, from 博客 "blog". Count posts with 条: 一条微博.
column6: Tā gāng fā le yī tiáo wēibó.
column7: He just posted on Weibo.
column9: A microblog, and nearly always "Weibo", the Chinese platform like Twitter: 發微博 "post on Weibo", 刷微博 "scroll Weibo". 微 "tiny" plus 博, from 博客 "blog". Count posts with 條: 一條微博.

column3: A video, a clip on a phone or the internet: 看视频, 发视频, 视频通话 "video call". 视 is "see" (the 见 radical) and 频 "frequency". For a film at the cinema use 电影, not 视频.
column6: Wǒmen yòng shìpín liáotiān ba.
column7: Let's chat by video.
column9: A video, a clip on a phone or the internet: 看視頻, 發視頻, 視頻通話 "video call". 視 is "see" (the 見 radical) and 頻 "frequency". For a film at the cinema use 電影, not 視頻.

column3: A user of a product or service: 手机用户, 用户名 "username", 新用户 "new user". It is "users" 用 plus 户, which was a single door and so a household or account. The same 户 is in 客户 and 账户.
column6: Zhège ruǎnjiàn yǒu yīyì yònghù.
column7: This software has a hundred million users.
column9: A user of a product or service: 手機用戶, 用戶名 "username", 新用戶 "new user". It is "users" 用 plus 戶, which was a single door and so a household or account. The same 戶 is in 客戶 and 帳戶.

column3: To output: a computer outputs data, a machine outputs power. 输入 "input" is the opposite. In writing it also means to export goods or labor. 输 has 车 "cart" for moving things, as in 运输 "transport", and 出 means out.
column4: 这个软件可以输出图片。
column5: 這個軟件可以輸出圖片。
column6: Zhège ruǎnjiàn kěyǐ shūchū túpiàn.
column7: This software can export pictures.
column9: To output: a computer outputs data, a machine outputs power. 輸入 "input" is the opposite. In writing it also means to export goods or labor. 輸 has 車 "cart" for moving things, as in 運輸 "transport", and 出 means out.

column3: To search; on its own mostly in speech as 搜一下 "do a search", and in compounds: 搜索, 搜查 "search a place", 搜集 "collect". The 叟 on the right still sounds almost like the whole character (sǒu). The 扌 "hand" is the meaning part.
column6: Nǐ zài wǎngshàng sōu yīxià ba.
column7: Search for it online.
column9: To search; on its own mostly in speech as 搜一下 "do a search", and in compounds: 搜索, 搜查 "search a place", 蒐集 "collect". The 叟 on the right still sounds almost like the whole character (sǒu). The 扌 "hand" is the meaning part.

column3: Price, almost only in compounds: 原价 "original price", 低价 "low price", 价值 "value". For one thing's price people say 价格 or 价钱. Price changes: 降价 "cut the price", 涨价 "the price rises".
column6: Zhè shuāng xié yuánjià sān bǎi yuán.
column7: These shoes originally cost 300 yuan.
column9: Price, almost only in compounds: 原價 "original price", 低價 "low price", 價值 "value". For one thing's price people say 價格 or 價錢. Price changes: 降價 "cut the price", 漲價 "the price rises".

column3: The general level of prices, as in the news: 物价上涨 "prices are rising", 物价高 "the cost of living is high", 稳定物价. It speaks about prices overall, not the price of one item, which is 价格. 物 "things" plus 价 "price".
column6: Zhège chéngshì de wùjià hěn gāo.
column7: Prices in this city are very high.
column9: The general level of prices, as in the news: 物價上漲 "prices are rising", 物價高 "the cost of living is high", 穩定物價. It speaks about prices overall, not the price of one item, which is 價格. 物 "things" plus 價 "price".

column3: To go up in price: the goods are the subject, as in 牛肉涨价了 "beef has gone up". The opposite is 降价. It is a verb plus object, so you can say 涨了价 or put an amount after 涨: 涨了两块钱. The same word is also used for someone raising prices.
column6: Zuìjìn niúròu yòu zhǎngjià le.
column7: Beef has gone up in price again lately.
column9: To go up in price: the goods are the subject, as in 牛肉漲價了 "beef has gone up". The opposite is 降價. It is a verb plus object, so you can say 漲了價 or put an amount after 漲: 漲了兩塊錢. The same word is also used for someone raising prices.

column3: To rise, of prices and of water: 价格涨了, 水位涨了, 涨工资 "get a raise". The opposite is 跌 or 降. A surprise: when it means swollen or flushed it is read zhàng, as in 涨红了脸 "face turned red". 氵 "water" is the meaning part and 张 gives the sound.
column6: Héshuǐ zhǎng de hěn kuài.
column7: The river is rising fast.
column9: To rise, of prices and of water: 價格漲了, 水位漲了, 漲工資 "get a raise". The opposite is 跌 or 降. A surprise: when it means swollen or flushed it is read zhàng, as in 漲紅了臉 "face turned red". 氵 "water" is the meaning part and 張 gives the sound.

column3: To rise, in the written style, of prices, wages or water levels: 价格上涨, 房价上涨. It takes no object and the thing that rises is the subject. 上 "up" and 涨 "rise" together. In speech you more often hear just 涨.
column6: Jīnnián fángjià shàngzhǎng le bù shǎo.
column7: House prices have gone up a lot this year.
column9: To rise, in the written style, of prices, wages or water levels: 價格上漲, 房價上漲. It takes no object and the thing that rises is the subject. 上 "up" and 漲 "rise" together. In speech you more often hear just 漲.

column3: The price you pay in effort, loss or sacrifice, not in money: 付出代价 "pay the price", 以健康为代价 "at the cost of one's health". For an ordinary price use 价格. 代 "replace" and 价 "price": something given in exchange.
column4: 他为这个错误付出了很大的代价。
column5: 他為這個錯誤付出了很大的代價。
column6: Tā wèi zhège cuòwù fùchū le hěn dà de dàijià.
column7: He paid a heavy price for this mistake.
column9: The price you pay in effort, loss or sacrifice, not in money: 付出代價 "pay the price", 以健康為代價 "at the cost of one's health". For an ordinary price use 價格. 代 "replace" and 價 "price": something given in exchange.

column3: Buying and selling, and so a business or a deal: 做买卖 "be in business", 小买卖 "a small business". The two characters are almost the same: 卖 is 买 with 十 on top. As a noun, "business", its second syllable is neutral: mǎimai.
column6: Tā zuò de shì xiǎo mǎimai.
column7: He runs a small business.
column9: Buying and selling, and so a business or a deal: 做買賣 "be in business", 小買賣 "a small business". The two characters are almost the same: 賣 is 買 with 士 on top. As a noun, "business", its second syllable is neutral: mǎimai.

column3: To buy goods in quantity for a company, school or household: 采购员 "buyer", 采购设备 "procure equipment". It sounds more businesslike than 买. 采 shows a hand 爫 picking fruit from a tree 木. 购 has 贝 "shell", the money radical.
column4: 公司要采购一批新电脑。
column5: 公司要採購一批新電腦。
column6: Gōngsī yào cǎigòu yī pī xīn diànnǎo.
column7: The company is going to buy a batch of new computers.
column9: To buy goods in quantity for a company, school or household: 採購員 "buyer", 採購設備 "procure equipment". It sounds more businesslike than 買. 採 shows a hand 爫 picking fruit from a tree 木. 購 has 貝 "shell", the money radical.

column3: To buy up, in two settings: an organization buying produce in bulk (收购粮食 "buy grain from farmers"), and one company buying another (被收购 "be taken over"). 收 "gather in" plus 购 "buy". The 贝 in 购 is the money radical, as in 费 and 贵.
column4: 这家公司被大公司收购了。
column5: 這家公司被大公司收購了。
column6: Zhè jiā gōngsī bèi dà gōngsī shōugòu le.
column7: This company was bought by a big company.
column9: To buy up, in two settings: an organization buying produce in bulk (收購糧食 "buy grain from farmers"), and one company buying another (被收購 "be taken over"). 收 "gather in" plus 購 "buy". The 貝 in 購 is the money radical, as in 費 and 貴.

column3: For a deal to be closed: 成交了 "it's a deal", 成交价 "the price paid", 成交量 "trading volume". The subject is the deal, not a person: 这笔生意成交了. 成 "complete" plus 交 "hand over". Used in shops, markets and the stock exchange.
column4: 经过谈判，这笔生意终于成交了。
column5: 經過談判，這筆生意終於成交了。
column6: Jīngguò tánpàn, zhè bǐ shēngyi zhōngyú chéngjiāo le.
column7: After negotiating, the deal was finally closed.
column9: For a deal to be closed: 成交了 "it's a deal", 成交價 "the price paid", 成交量 "trading volume". The subject is the deal, not a person: 這筆生意成交了. 成 "complete" plus 交 "hand over". Used in shops, markets and the stock exchange.

column3: A trademark or brand mark: 注册商标 "register a trademark". 商 is trade and 标 a mark. A brand is 品牌, and 商标 is the registered mark of one.
column6: Zhège shāngbiāo hěn yǒumíng.
column7: This trademark is very famous.
column9: A trademark or brand mark: 註冊商標 "register a trademark". 商 is trade and 標 a mark. A brand is 品牌, and 商標 is the registered mark of one.

column3: Goods, an article, in compounds: 食品 "food", 商品 "commodity", 礼品 "gift", 产品 "product". Also quality or character, as in 人品, and to taste, as in 品尝. It is three 口 stacked, which can be pictured as a heap of goods or many mouths.
column6: Zhè jiā diàn de shípǐn hěn xīnxiān.
column7: The food in this shop is very fresh.
column9: Goods, an article, in compounds: 食品 "food", 商品 "commodity", 禮品 "gift", 產品 "product". Also quality or character, as in 人品, and to taste, as in 品嘗. It is three 口 stacked, which can be pictured as a heap of goods or many mouths.

column3: A variety or breed of plants, animals or products: 新品种, 苹果品种, 品种多 "a wide range". 种 is read zhǒng here, "kind", but zhòng in 种花 "plant flowers". Its 禾 "grain" shows that it first spoke of seeds.
column6: Zhèlǐ yǒu hěn duō píngguǒ pǐnzhǒng.
column7: There are many varieties of apple here.
column9: A variety or breed of plants, animals or products: 新品種, 蘋果品種, 品種多 "a wide range". 種 is read zhǒng here, "kind", but zhòng in 種花 "plant flowers". Its 禾 "grain" shows that it first spoke of seeds.

column3: A consumer: 消费者权益 "consumer rights", 保护消费者. 消费 is "spend, consume" and 者 turns it into the person who does it, as in 学者 and 记者. 消 has 氵 "water" and 费 has 贝 "shell", the money radical.
column6: Shāngdiàn yào ràng xiāofèizhě mǎnyì.
column7: Shops have to satisfy their consumers.
column9: A consumer: 消費者權益 "consumer rights", 保護消費者. 消費 is "spend, consume" and 者 turns it into the person who does it, as in 學者 and 記者. 消 has 氵 "water" and 費 has 貝 "shell", the money radical.

column3: A client or customer of a company: 重要客户, 客户服务 "customer service", 接待客户. It is for business dealings and accounts. A person buying in a shop is called 顾客 instead. 客 is a person 各 under a roof 宀, a guest, and 户 is a household.
column4: 我今天要见一个重要的客户。
column5: 我今天要見一個重要的客戶。
column6: Wǒ jīntiān yào jiàn yī ge zhòngyào de kèhù.
column7: I am meeting an important client today.
column9: A client or customer of a company: 重要客戶, 客戶服務 "customer service", 接待客戶. It is for business dealings and accounts. A person buying in a shop is called 顧客 instead. 客 is a person 各 under a roof 宀, a guest, and 戶 is a household.

column3: A lottery ticket: 买彩票 "buy a ticket", 中彩票 "win the lottery". 彩 means colorful, as in 精彩 "wonderful", and 票 is a ticket, as in 车票 and 电影票. A prize is 奖, so people also say 中奖 "win a prize".
column6: Tā mǎi le yī zhāng cǎipiào.
column7: He bought a lottery ticket.
column9: A lottery ticket: 買彩票 "buy a ticket", 中彩票 "win the lottery". 彩 means colorful, as in 精彩 "wonderful", and 票 is a ticket, as in 車票 and 電影票. A prize is 獎, so people also say 中獎 "win a prize".

column3: Savings in a bank, and also the act of depositing: 银行存款, 我的存款, 存款三万元. The opposite is 取款 "withdraw money". 存 is "keep, store" and 款 is a sum of money, the same 款 as in 贷款, 付款 and 罚款.
column6: Wǒ de cúnkuǎn bù duō.
column7: I do not have much in savings.
column9: Savings in a bank, and also the act of depositing: 銀行存款, 我的存款, 存款三萬元. The opposite is 取款 "withdraw money". 存 is "keep, store" and 款 is a sum of money, the same 款 as in 貸款, 付款 and 罰款.

column3: A loan from a bank, or to take one: 申请贷款 "apply for a loan", 房屋贷款 "mortgage", 向银行贷款 "borrow from a bank". Said from the borrower's side; the bank "gives" one with 发放贷款. The 贝 in 贷 is the money radical, and 代 supplies the sound.
column4: 他向银行贷款买了房子。
column5: 他向銀行貸款買了房子。
column6: Tā xiàng yínháng dàikuǎn mǎi le fángzi.
column7: He took out a bank loan to buy a house.
column9: A loan from a bank, or to take one: 申請貸款 "apply for a loan", 房屋貸款 "mortgage", 向銀行貸款 "borrow from a bank". Said from the borrower's side; the bank "gives" one with 發放貸款. The 貝 in 貸 is the money radical, and 代 supplies the sound.

column3: To owe: 欠钱, 欠你一个人情 "I owe you a favor". It also means to lack, mostly in set phrases such as 欠考虑 "not well thought out". The character is a person with mouth wide open, yawning, and the same shape stands in 款 and 次.
column6: Tā hái qiàn wǒ yībǎi kuài qián.
column7: He still owes me a hundred yuan.
column9: To owe: 欠錢, 欠你一個人情 "I owe you a favor". It also means to lack, mostly in set phrases such as 欠考慮 "not well thought out". The character is a person with mouth wide open, yawning, and the same shape stands in 款 and 次.

column3: To pay for something broken, or to lose money in business: 赔钱 "lose money", 赔了不少钱, 我赔你一个 "I'll replace it for you". 赔不是 means to apologize. The opposite of losing money in business is 赚. The 贝 on the left is the money radical.
column6: Tā zuò shēngyi péi le hěn duō qián.
column7: He lost a lot of money in business.
column9: To pay for something broken, or to lose money in business: 賠錢 "lose money", 賠了不少錢, 我賠你一個 "I'll replace it for you". 賠不是 means to apologize. The opposite of losing money in business is 賺. The 貝 on the left is the money radical.

column3: To pay compensation for harm or loss you caused: 赔偿损失, 要求赔偿, 赔偿金 "compensation payment". It is a formal word used in contracts and the law. 偿 has the same sound part as 尝 (cháng) and 亻 "person" for the meaning.
column4: 他打坏了东西，必须赔偿。
column5: 他打壞了東西，必須賠償。
column6: Tā dǎhuài le dōngxi, bìxū péicháng.
column7: He broke something, so he has to pay compensation.
column9: To pay compensation for harm or loss you caused: 賠償損失, 要求賠償, 賠償金 "compensation payment". It is a formal word used in contracts and the law. 償 has 賞 as its sound part and 亻 "person" for the meaning.

column3: To make up for a loss with money, time or something else: 经济补偿 "financial compensation", 补偿损失. Unlike 赔偿, the one paying need not be at fault: it can be an employer or a government. 补 has 衤 "clothes", so it started as mending a garment.
column6: Gōngsī gěi le tā yī bǐ bǔcháng.
column7: The company gave him a sum as compensation.
column9: To make up for a loss with money, time or something else: 經濟補償 "financial compensation", 補償損失. Unlike 賠償, the one paying need not be at fault: it can be an employer or a government. 補 has 衤 "clothes", so it started as mending a garment.

column3: A subsidy or allowance, and the verb to subsidize: 政府补贴, 交通补贴 "travel allowance", 补贴家用 "help pay for the household". 补 "make up" plus 贴, which with 贝 "money" means money added to make up the difference.
column6: Zhèngfǔ gěi nóngmín fā bǔtiē.
column7: The government pays subsidies to farmers.
column9: A subsidy or allowance, and the verb to subsidize: 政府補貼, 交通補貼 "travel allowance", 補貼家用 "help pay for the household". 補 "make up" plus 貼, which with 貝 "money" means money added to make up the difference.

column3: To earn by work: 挣钱, 挣工资 "earn a wage". In speech the earning is hard-won. A different word in another reading: 挣扎 (zhēngzhá) "to struggle". The character is 争 "fight" with 扌 "hand", which fits both meanings.
column6: Tā yī ge yuè zhèng wǔqiān kuài qián.
column7: He earns five thousand yuan a month.
column9: To earn by work: 掙錢, 掙工資 "earn a wage". In speech the earning is hard-won. A different word in another reading: 掙扎 (zhēngzhá) "to struggle". The character is 爭 "fight" with 扌 "hand", which fits both meanings.

column3: To make money by working: 挣钱养家 "earn to support a family", 挣钱不容易. 挣 stresses the effort of working for it, while 赚钱 is wider and also covers profit from trading. Spoken, and the usual word for ordinary wages. 钱 has 钅 for the metal of coins.
column4: 他每天辛苦地挣钱养家。
column5: 他每天辛苦地掙錢養家。
column6: Tā měitiān xīnkǔ de zhèngqián yǎngjiā.
column7: He works hard every day to earn money for his family.
column9: To make money by working: 掙錢養家 "earn to support a family", 掙錢不容易. 掙 stresses the effort of working for it, while 賺錢 is wider and also covers profit from trading. Spoken, and the usual word for ordinary wages. 錢 has 釒 for the metal of coins.

column3: Welfare or benefits, especially those a job or the state provides: 员工福利, 社会福利, 福利好. 福 "good fortune" with 利 "benefit". 利 shows grain 禾 being cut with a knife 刂, a harvest, which is also where profit and sharpness meet in 利润.
column6: Zhè jiā gōngsī de fúlì hěn hǎo.
column7: This company has very good benefits.
column9: Welfare or benefits, especially those a job or the state provides: 員工福利, 社會福利, 福利好. 福 "good fortune" with 利 "benefit". 利 shows grain 禾 being cut with a knife 刂, a harvest, which is also where profit and sharpness meet in 利潤.

column3: Funds set aside for an organization or project: 研究经费, 活动经费, 经费不足 "not enough funds". It is for institutions, not for a person's own money, which is 钱 or 费用. 费 has 贝 "money"; 经 has 纟 "thread".
column6: Xuéxiào de jīngfèi bù gòu yòng.
column7: The school's funds are not enough.
column9: Funds set aside for an organization or project: 研究經費, 活動經費, 經費不足 "not enough funds". It is for institutions, not for a person's own money, which is 錢 or 費用. 費 has 貝 "money"; 經 has 糹 "thread".

column3: To support someone with money, for example for school or research: 资助学生, 受到资助. The object is the person helped: 资助他上大学. 资 has 贝 "money" (as in 投资) and 助 "help" has 力 "strength", so it is help given in money.
column6: Yǒurén zīzhù tā shàng dàxué.
column7: Someone is paying for him to go to university.
column9: To support someone with money, for example for school or research: 資助學生, 受到資助. The object is the person helped: 資助他上大學. 資 has 貝 "money" (as in 投資) and 助 "help" has 力 "strength", so it is help given in money.

column3: Spending, as a noun, and to pay out as a verb: 每月支出, 减少支出, 收入和支出 "income and expenses". The opposite is 收入. 支 is "pay out" in this sense, and 出 "out".
column4: 我们每个月的支出很大。
column5: 我們每個月的支出很大。
column6: Wǒmen měi ge yuè de zhīchū hěn dà.
column7: Our monthly spending is large.
column9: Spending, as a noun, and to pay out as a verb: 每月支出, 減少支出, 收入和支出 "income and expenses". The opposite is 收入. 支 is "pay out" in this sense, and 出 "out".

column3: To punish or fine, mostly in compounds: 罚款 "a fine", 处罚 "penalize", 罚站 "make someone stand as punishment". In speech you can say 罚钱 or 罚了他两百块. The 刂 "knife" in the character marks a hard penalty.
column6: Chídào yào fá qián.
column7: You are fined if you are late.
column9: To punish or fine, mostly in compounds: 罰款 "a fine", 處罰 "penalize", 罰站 "make someone stand as punishment". In speech you can say 罰錢 or 罰了他兩百塊. The 刂 "knife" in the character marks a hard penalty.

column3: A fine, and to fine: 交罚款 "pay a fine", 被罚款 "be fined", 罚款两百元. As a verb it takes no object after it: 他被罚款了, or the person comes before: 罚他的款. 款 is the sum of money, as in 存款 and 贷款.
column6: Tā luàn tíngchē bèi fákuǎn le.
column7: He was fined for parking illegally.
column9: A fine, and to fine: 交罰款 "pay a fine", 被罰款 "be fined", 罰款兩百元. As a verb it takes no object after it: 他被罰款了, or the person comes before: 罰他的款. 款 is the sum of money, as in 存款 and 貸款.

column3: To lose money in business: 亏钱, 亏本 "sell at a loss", 亏了五万. The opposite is 赚. It also appears in 多亏, "luckily, thanks to": 多亏你 "thanks to you". In speech, 亏 can also be an ironic "you have the nerve", as in 亏你说得出口.
column6: Zhè jiā diàn yīzhí zài kuī qián.
column7: This shop has been losing money all the time.
column9: To lose money in business: 虧錢, 虧本 "sell at a loss", 虧了五萬. The opposite is 賺. It also appears in 多虧, "luckily, thanks to": 多虧你 "thanks to you". In speech, 虧 can also be an ironic "you have the nerve", as in 虧你說得出口.

column3: Has never, did not yet: 不曾见过 "have never seen", 不曾想到 "never imagined". It is a written word; speech uses 没(有) with 过. Note that 曾 is céng in this use; as a surname it is Zēng. It negates only experience that did happen, not habit.
column6: Wǒ cónglái bùcéng jiànguò tā.
column7: I have never seen him.
column9: Has never, did not yet: 不曾見過 "have never seen", 不曾想到 "never imagined". It is a written word; speech uses 沒(有) with 過. Note that 曾 is céng in this use; as a surname it is Zēng. It negates only experience that did happen, not habit.

column3: From time to time, now and then: placed before the verb, 不时看手机 "keep glancing at the phone". The actions are repeated at irregular moments, so it is a bit more frequent than 偶尔. It occurs in written and in spoken Chinese, and in 不时之需 "unexpected needs".
column6: Tā bùshí kàn yīxià shǒujī.
column7: He looks at his phone from time to time.
column9: From time to time, now and then: placed before the verb, 不時看手機 "keep glancing at the phone". The actions are repeated at irregular moments, so it is a bit more frequent than 偶爾. It occurs in written and in spoken Chinese, and in 不時之需 "unexpected needs".

column3: Without stopping: 不停地说 "talk nonstop", and after a verb with 得 or 个: 下个不停 "rain without stopping", 笑个不停. It carries a feeling of too much. The opposite is 停下来. 停 has 亻 beside 亭, and 亭 (tíng) gives the sound.
column6: Yǔ xià ge bùtíng.
column7: It keeps raining without stopping.
column9: Without stopping: 不停地說 "talk nonstop", and after a verb with 得 or 個: 下個不停 "rain without stopping", 笑個不停. It carries a feeling of too much. The opposite is 停下來. 停 has 亻 beside 亭, and 亭 (tíng) gives the sound.

column3: Often, frequently, placed before the verb: 时常想起, 时常联系. Close to 常常 but more written and less common in conversation. 时 is the sun 日 with 寸 on the side, and 常 has 巾 "cloth", although the word has nothing to do with cloth now.
column6: Tā shícháng gěi wǒ dǎ diànhuà.
column7: He often calls me.
column9: Often, frequently, placed before the verb: 時常想起, 時常聯繫. Close to 常常 but more written and less common in conversation. 時 is the sun 日 with 寸 on the side, and 常 has 巾 "cloth", although the word has nothing to do with cloth now.

column3: Occasionally, once in a while, before the verb: 偶尔去一次 "go once in a while". It states a low frequency, whereas 偶然 is about something by chance. Note the apostrophe in the pinyin, ǒu'ěr, because the second syllable starts with a vowel.
column6: Wǒ ǒu'ěr qù nà jiā kāfēiguǎn.
column7: I go to that café once in a while.
column9: Occasionally, once in a while, before the verb: 偶爾去一次 "go once in a while". It states a low frequency, whereas 偶然 is about something by chance. Note the apostrophe in the pinyin, ǒu'ěr, because the second syllable starts with a vowel.

column3: By chance, accidental: 偶然的机会 "a chance opportunity", 偶然发现 "discover by accident". It can be an adjective (这是偶然的) or an adverb before a verb. The opposite is 必然 "inevitable". 然 has 灬 "fire" and once meant to burn.
column6: Wǒmen shì ǒurán rènshi de.
column7: We got to know each other by chance.
column9: By chance, accidental: 偶然的機會 "a chance opportunity", 偶然發現 "discover by accident". It can be an adjective (這是偶然的) or an adverb before a verb. The opposite is 必然 "inevitable". 然 has 灬 "fire" and once meant to burn.

column3: All along, always up to now: 他一向很准时, 我一向不吃辣. It describes a habit or state that has held until the present, so it is not used for a single event or for the future. It sits before the verb or adjective, and often with 很 or a negative.
column6: Tā yīxiàng hěn zhǔnshí.
column7: He has always been punctual.
column9: All along, always up to now: 他一向很準時, 我一向不吃辣. It describes a habit or state that has held until the present, so it is not used for a single event or for the future. It sits before the verb or adjective, and often with 很 or a negative.

column3: Still, as before, in writing, often looking back with some feeling: 风景依旧 "the scenery is unchanged", 依旧如此. It says that something stayed the same after a change or after time passed. 依 "rely on" has the sound part 衣, which sounds just the same, yī.
column4: 十年后，他依旧住在这里。
column5: 十年後，他依舊住在這裡。
column6: Shí nián hòu, tā yījiù zhù zài zhèlǐ.
column7: Ten years later, he still lives here.
column9: Still, as before, in writing, often looking back with some feeling: 風景依舊 "the scenery is unchanged", 依舊如此. It says that something stayed the same after a change or after time passed. 依 "rely on" has the sound part 衣, which sounds just the same, yī.

column3: Still, as before: 仍旧坚持, 仍旧没有变. Much like 依旧, though 仍旧 usually describes an action or situation going on in spite of the change around it. 仍然 is the common spoken form. 仍 has 亻 and 乃, whose sound it follows.
column4: 虽然很累，他仍旧坚持工作。
column5: 雖然很累，他仍舊堅持工作。
column6: Suīrán hěn lèi, tā réngjiù jiānchí gōngzuò.
column7: Although he was tired, he kept on working.
column9: Still, as before: 仍舊堅持, 仍舊沒有變. Much like 依舊, though 仍舊 usually describes an action or situation going on in spite of the change around it. 仍然 is the common spoken form. 仍 has 亻 and 乃, whose sound it follows.

column3: Once more, again, a more formal alternative to 又 or 再 for one more time: 再次强调 "stress again", 再次见面. It works for the future and for the past. 再 "again" with 次 "occasion"; 次 contains the yawn-person 欠.
column4: 他再次向大家表示感谢。
column5: 他再次向大家表示感謝。
column6: Tā zàicì xiàng dàjiā biǎoshì gǎnxiè.
column7: He thanked everyone once more.
column9: Once more, again, a more formal alternative to 又 or 再 for one more time: 再次強調 "stress again", 再次見面. It works for the future and for the past. 再 "again" with 次 "occasion"; 次 contains the yawn-person 欠.

column3: Not any more, never again; it must be followed by a negative: 再也不, 再也没有, 再也不能. It is stronger than 不再, as it states that something has now ended for good. Say it before the verb: 他再也没回来.
column6: Wǒ zàiyě bù xiǎng chī le.
column7: I never want to eat that again.
column9: Not any more, never again; it must be followed by a negative: 再也不, 再也沒有, 再也不能. It is stronger than 不再, as it states that something has now ended for good. Say it before the verb: 他再也沒回來.

column3: Once, as soon as something happens, with a warning that things then change: 一旦…就…, 一旦发生 "once it happens". It starts a clause, often about a bad or important event. 旦 is the sun 日 above the horizon 一, a sunrise, so it first meant "one morning" or "in a day".
column6: Yīdàn kāishǐ, jiù bùyào fàngqì.
column7: Once you start, do not give up.
column9: Once, as soon as something happens, with a warning that things then change: 一旦…就…, 一旦發生 "once it happens". It starts a clause, often about a bad or important event. 旦 is the sun 日 above the horizon 一, a sunrise, so it first meant "one morning" or "in a day".

column3: The head of a bureau or office: 公安局长 "chief of police", 邮政局长. Titles are formed as department plus 长 (zhǎng "head"), as in 校长, 市长, 厂长. 长 is read zhǎng here, not cháng "long". 局 is an office of government.
column6: Júzhǎng zhèngzài kāihuì.
column7: The bureau chief is in a meeting.
column9: The head of a bureau or office: 公安局長 "chief of police", 郵政局長. Titles are formed as department plus 長 (zhǎng "head"), as in 校長, 市長, 廠長. 長 is read zhǎng here, not cháng "long". 局 is an office of government.

column3: The director of a factory: 厂长，您好. Like 局长 and 校长, it is a place plus 长, "head", and 长 is read zhǎng here, not cháng. 厂 is the shape of the factory's wall and roof.
column6: Chǎngzhǎng jīntiān yào lái jiǎnchá.
column7: The factory director is coming to inspect today.
column9: The director of a factory: 廠長，您好. Like 局長 and 校長, it is a place plus 長, "head", and 長 is read zhǎng here, not cháng. 廠 has 广 and 敞.

column3: The leader of a group: the head of a tour group (旅游团团长), a delegation, a performing troupe, and in the army the commander of a regiment. Recently it also means the organizer of a group purchase online. 团 is a 囗 enclosure with 才 inside, people gathered in one place, hence "group".
column4: 团长带我们参观了博物馆。
column5: 團長帶我們參觀了博物館。
column6: Tuánzhǎng dài wǒmen cānguān le bówùguǎn.
column7: The group leader took us around the museum.
column9: The leader of a group: the head of a tour group (旅遊團團長), a delegation, a performing troupe, and in the army the commander of a regiment. Recently it also means the organizer of a group purchase online. 團 is a 囗 enclosure with 專 inside, hence "group".

column3: A skilled worker or master of a trade, and a polite way to address one: a driver, a repairman, a cook. 师傅，请问… is how you call a taxi driver. A teacher of a craft or of martial arts is a 师傅 too. The 傅 is neutral: shīfu.
column4: 师傅，请问去火车站怎么走？
column5: 師傅，請問去火車站怎麼走？
column6: Shīfu, qǐngwèn qù huǒchēzhàn zěnme zǒu?
column7: Excuse me, how do I get to the train station?
column9: A skilled worker or master of a trade, and a polite way to address one: a driver, a repairman, a cook. 師傅，請問… is how you call a taxi driver. A teacher of a craft or of martial arts is a 師傅 too. The 傅 is neutral: shīfu.

column3: An adviser or consultant, a job title: 法律顾问 "legal adviser", 技术顾问, 担任顾问. The person gives advice from outside the line of command. 顾 is "look after, consider" and 问 "ask", which is why it is a person consulted.
column6: Tā shì gōngsī de fǎlǜ gùwèn.
column7: He is the company's legal adviser.
column9: An adviser or consultant, a job title: 法律顧問 "legal adviser", 技術顧問, 擔任顧問. The person gives advice from outside the line of command. 顧 is "look after, consider" and 問 "ask", which is why it is a person consulted.

column3: An assistant as a job or title: 经理助理, 助理研究员. It is an official position, usually beside a senior person. 助 has 力 "strength" and 且 as sound, the same sound part as in 组 and 姐 (zǔ, jiě), now read zhù.
column6: Tā shì jīnglǐ de zhùlǐ.
column7: She is the manager's assistant.
column9: An assistant as a job or title: 經理助理, 助理研究員. It is an official position, usually beside a senior person. 助 has 力 "strength" and 且 as sound, the same sound part as in 組 and 姐 (zǔ, jiě), now read zhù.

column3: A helper in some work: 得力助手 "capable right-hand man", a doctor's or a researcher's assistant. It describes the help given rather than a rank, unlike 助理. 手 is a drawing of a hand with fingers spread.
column4: 我需要一个助手帮我整理资料。
column5: 我需要一個助手幫我整理資料。
column6: Wǒ xūyào yī ge zhùshǒu bāng wǒ zhěnglǐ zīliào.
column7: I need an assistant to help me organize the material.
column9: A helper in some work: 得力助手 "capable right-hand man", a doctor's or a researcher's assistant. It describes the help given rather than a rank, unlike 助理. 手 is a drawing of a hand with fingers spread.

column3: The president or chief executive of a large company or bank: 集团总裁, 副总裁 "vice president". The 总裁 runs the business, while the 董事长 "chairman" leads the board (董事会), which decides and oversees. 裁 has 衣 "clothing" and 戈, and means to cut cloth, hence "decide", as in 裁判 and 裁员.
column6: Tā shì zhè jiā jítuán de zǒngcái.
column7: He is the chief executive of this group.
column9: The president or chief executive of a large company or bank: 集團總裁, 副總裁 "vice president". The 總裁 runs the business, while the 董事長 "chairman" leads the board (董事會), which decides and oversees. 裁 has 衣 "clothing" and 戈, and means to cut cloth, hence "decide", as in 裁判 and 裁員.

column3: A manager or supervisor: 部门主管 "department head", 我的主管 "my boss". It is also a verb: 主管销售 "be in charge of sales", and an adjective before a noun: 主管部门 "the responsible department". 主 is a lamp with its flame, the main thing, and so the one in charge.
column6: Wǒ de zhǔguǎn jīntiān bù zài.
column7: My supervisor is not in today.
column9: A manager or supervisor: 部門主管 "department head", 我的主管 "my boss". It is also a verb: 主管銷售 "be in charge of sales", and an adjective before a noun: 主管部門 "the responsible department". 主 is a lamp with its flame, the main thing, and so the one in charge.

column3: The person in charge of a task, project or place: 项目负责人 "project leader", 负责人是谁？. 负责 is "be responsible" and 人 "person". Both 负 and 责 carry 贝, the money radical, because responsibility used to mean debt.
column4: 请问这里的负责人是谁？
column5: 請問這裡的負責人是誰？
column6: Qǐngwèn zhèlǐ de fùzérén shì shéi?
column7: Excuse me, who is in charge here?
column9: The person in charge of a task, project or place: 項目負責人 "project leader", 負責人是誰？. 負責 is "be responsible" and 人 "person". Both 負 and 責 carry 貝, the money radical, because responsibility used to mean debt.

column3: A doctorate, or a person who holds one: 读博士, 博士学位, 博士生 "doctoral student", 王博士 "Dr. Wang". It is the academic title and not the physician's: a medical doctor is 医生. 博 "wide" and 士 "scholar": a widely learned person.
column6: Tā zài Měiguó dú bóshì.
column7: She is studying for a doctorate in America.
column9: A doctorate, or a person who holds one: 讀博士, 博士學位, 博士生 "doctoral student", 王博士 "Dr. Wang". It is the academic title and not the physician's: a medical doctor is 醫生. 博 "wide" and 士 "scholar": a widely learned person.

column3: A master's degree, or the person who has one: 读硕士, 硕士学位, 硕士毕业. The degrees go 学士 (bachelor's), 硕士, 博士. 硕 on its own means big, with 页 "head" beside 石.
column6: Tā jīnnián shuòshì bìyè.
column7: He finishes his master's degree this year.
column9: A master's degree, or the person who has one: 讀碩士, 碩士學位, 碩士畢業. The degrees go 學士 (bachelor's), 碩士, 博士. 碩 on its own means big, with 頁 "head" beside 石.

column3: A scholar, someone who studies a field seriously: 著名学者, 历史学者. 者 makes "the person who" and occurs in 记者, 作者 and 消费者. A student is 学生. 学 shows a child 子 under a roof 冖.
column4: 这位学者研究古代历史。
column5: 這位學者研究古代歷史。
column6: Zhè wèi xuézhě yánjiū gǔdài lìshǐ.
column7: This scholar studies ancient history.
column9: A scholar, someone who studies a field seriously: 著名學者, 歷史學者. 者 makes "the person who" and occurs in 記者, 作者 and 消費者. A student is 學生. 學 shows a child 子 under a roof 冖.

column3: A position in an organization, thought of as a seat to be filled: 招聘职位, 高级职位 "senior position", 申请职位. It stresses the rank and place on the ladder. 位 is a person 亻 standing 立 in a place, as in 座位 and 位置.
column4: 他在公司里的职位很高。
column5: 他在公司裡的職位很高。
column6: Tā zài gōngsī lǐ de zhíwèi hěn gāo.
column7: He holds a high position in the company.
column9: A position in an organization, thought of as a seat to be filled: 招聘職位, 高級職位 "senior position", 申請職位. It stresses the rank and place on the ladder. 位 is a person 亻 standing 立 in a place, as in 座位 and 位置.

column3: One's post and duties: 担任职务 "hold a post", 职务是经理, 免去职务 "remove from office". It stresses the task and the title that go with a job. 职 has the same sound part 只 as 织.
column4: 他在公司担任什么职务？
column5: 他在公司擔任什麼職務？
column6: Tā zài gōngsī dānrèn shénme zhíwù?
column7: What post does he hold in the company?
column9: One's post and duties: 擔任職務 "hold a post", 職務是經理, 免去職務 "remove from office". It stresses the task and the title that go with a job. 職 has 戠 as its sound part.

column3: Work, especially physical labor: 体力劳动 "manual labor", 参加劳动, 劳动节 "May Day". As a noun it also names work as a value: 热爱劳动 "love work". It is not used for an office job. Both 劳 and 动 contain 力 "strength", the shape of a plow.
column4: 学生们在学校参加劳动。
column5: 學生們在學校參加勞動。
column6: Xuéshengmen zài xuéxiào cānjiā láodòng.
column7: The students take part in labor at school.
column9: Work, especially physical labor: 體力勞動 "manual labor", 參加勞動, 勞動節 "May Day". As a noun it also names work as a value: 熱愛勞動 "love work". It is not used for an office job. Both 勞 and 動 contain 力 "strength", the shape of a plow.

column3: Human labor, manpower: 人力不足 "short of workers", 节省人力, 人力资源 "human resources". It counts people as a resource, rather than as individuals. 力 is a picture of a plow, a tool that turns strength into work.
column4: 这项工作需要很多人力。
column5: 這項工作需要很多人力。
column6: Zhè xiàng gōngzuò xūyào hěn duō rénlì.
column7: This job needs a lot of manpower.
column9: Human labor, manpower: 人力不足 "short of workers", 節省人力, 人力資源 "human resources". It counts people as a resource, rather than as individuals. 力 is a picture of a plow, a tool that turns strength into work.

column3: To host or organize an event as its main sponsor: 主办单位 "the organizer", 由…主办 "organized by", 主办奥运会. The object is something big, such as a conference or a competition. 办 "handle" has 力 "strength".
column6: Zhè cì bǐsài yóu xuéxiào zhǔbàn.
column7: This competition is hosted by the school.
column9: To host or organize an event as its main sponsor: 主辦單位 "the organizer", 由…主辦 "organized by", 主辦奧運會. The object is something big, such as a conference or a competition. 辦 "handle" has 力 "strength".

column3: To take on the running of an event or a job on commission: 承办方 "the contractor", 由…承办 "run by". The 主办 side owns the event and gives it to the 承办 side, which does the work. 承 means to accept and bear.
column4: 这个活动由一家公司承办。
column5: 這個活動由一家公司承辦。
column6: Zhège huódòng yóu yī jiā gōngsī chéngbàn.
column7: A company is running this event.
column9: To take on the running of an event or a job on commission: 承辦方 "the contractor", 由…承辦 "run by". The 主辦 side owns the event and gives it to the 承辦 side, which does the work. 承 means to accept and bear.

column3: To carry out a plan, order or law: 执行任务, 严格执行, 执行力 "ability to carry things out". Here 行 is xíng. It is a formal word for following through on something already decided. 执 is a hand 扌 holding on to something small.
column4: 大家必须严格执行这个规定。
column5: 大家必須嚴格執行這個規定。
column6: Dàjiā bìxū yángé zhíxíng zhège guīdìng.
column7: Everyone must strictly carry out this rule.
column9: To carry out a plan, order or law: 執行任務, 嚴格執行, 執行力 "ability to carry things out". Here 行 is xíng. It is a formal word for following through on something already decided. 執 has 幸 and 丸, something small.

column3: To organize an event or a group of people, and an organization: 组织活动, 联合国组织, 非政府组织. In biology it is tissue, as in 肌肉组织. Both characters have 纟 "thread", and it can be pictured as weaving threads into a whole.
column4: 学校组织学生去参观博物馆。
column5: 學校組織學生去參觀博物館。
column6: Xuéxiào zǔzhī xuésheng qù cānguān bówùguǎn.
column7: The school organized the students to visit a museum.
column9: To organize an event or a group of people, and an organization: 組織活動, 聯合國組織, 非政府組織. In biology it is tissue, as in 肌肉組織. Both characters have 糹 "thread", and it can be pictured as weaving threads into a whole.

column3: To found something new: 创立公司, 创立学派, 创立理论. It is for a first founding, often something important or lasting. 建立 is wider and is also for setting up relations or systems. 立 is a person standing on the ground.
column4: 他三十年前创立了这家公司。
column5: 他三十年前創立了這家公司。
column6: Tā sānshí nián qián chuànglì le zhè jiā gōngsī.
column7: He founded this company thirty years ago.
column9: To found something new: 創立公司, 創立學派, 創立理論. It is for a first founding, often something important or lasting. 建立 is wider and is also for setting up relations or systems. 立 is a person standing on the ground.

column3: To be on duty, to work a shift: 值班室 "duty room", 值夜班 "work the night shift", 今天谁值班？. A verb plus its object, so it takes 了 in the middle: 值了一天班. 班 shows a piece of jade cut in two with a knife 刂, so a unit of people or time.
column6: Jīnwǎn lúndào wǒ zhíbān.
column7: Tonight it is my turn on duty.
column9: To be on duty, to work a shift: 值班室 "duty room", 值夜班 "work the night shift", 今天誰值班？. A verb plus its object, so it takes 了 in the middle: 值了一天班. 班 shows a piece of jade cut in two with a knife 刂, so a unit of people or time.

column3: To resign from a job: 辞职信 "resignation letter", 他辞职了, 主动辞职. It is a verb plus object, so something like 辞了职 and 辞去职务 can split it. 辞 "decline, say goodbye" and 职 "post". It does not mean being fired, which is 被开除.
column4: 他决定辞职，自己做生意。
column5: 他決定辭職，自己做生意。
column6: Tā juédìng cízhí, zìjǐ zuò shēngyi.
column7: He decided to quit and run his own business.
column9: To resign from a job: 辭職信 "resignation letter", 他辭職了, 主動辭職. It is a verb plus object, so something like 辭了職 and 辭去職務 can split it. 辭 "decline, say goodbye" and 職 "post". It does not mean being fired, which is 被開除.

column3: The function or role of an organization or office: 政府职能, 职能部门 "functional department", 职能转变. It is about what a body is meant to do, not about a person's job. 能 is a picture of a bear, and has been the word for "be able" for ages.
column4: 这个部门的职能是管理市场。
column5: 這個部門的職能是管理市場。
column6: Zhège bùmén de zhínéng shì guǎnlǐ shìchǎng.
column7: The function of this department is to manage the market.
column9: The function or role of an organization or office: 政府職能, 職能部門 "functional department", 職能轉變. It is about what a body is meant to do, not about a person's job. 能 is a picture of a bear, and has been the word for "be able" for ages.

column3: To enroll new students: 招生简章 "admissions brochure", 招生办 "admissions office", 今年招生. The school is the subject. It is a verb plus object, with the school as the subject and the number of students after it. 招 is "beckon", from 扌 and 召 "call".
column4: 这所学校今年招生三百人。
column5: 這所學校今年招生三百人。
column6: Zhè suǒ xuéxiào jīnnián zhāoshēng sānbǎi rén.
column7: This school enrolls three hundred students this year.
column9: To enroll new students: 招生簡章 "admissions brochure", 招生辦 "admissions office", 今年招生. The school is the subject. It is a verb plus object, with the school as the subject and the number of students after it. 招 is "beckon", from 扌 and 召 "call".

column3: To equip or fit out with something: 配备电脑 "equip with computers", 配备齐全 "fully equipped". It is also a noun, "equipment". Typical for rooms, schools, vehicles, teams. 配 "match" and 备 "prepare".
column4: 每个教室都配备了电脑。
column5: 每個教室都配備了電腦。
column6: Měi ge jiàoshì dōu pèibèi le diànnǎo.
column7: Every classroom is equipped with computers.
column9: To equip or fit out with something: 配備電腦 "equip with computers", 配備齊全 "fully equipped". It is also a noun, "equipment". Typical for rooms, schools, vehicles, teams. 配 "match" and 備 "prepare".

column3: A colloquial all-purpose verb, "do, make, get up to": 搞清楚 "get it clear", 搞错 "get wrong", 搞定 "sort out", 搞活动 "organize an event". Sometimes it hints at something not quite proper (搞破坏 "make trouble"). The 高 on the right still sounds like gāo.
column6: Zhè jiàn shì wǒ gǎo bù qīngchu.
column7: I cannot get this matter clear.
column9: A colloquial all-purpose verb, "do, make, get up to": 搞清楚 "get it clear", 搞錯 "get wrong", 搞定 "sort out", 搞活動 "organize an event". Sometimes it hints at something not quite proper (搞破壞 "make trouble"). The 高 on the right still sounds like gāo.

column3: To do something well, to get it right: 搞好关系 "build a good relationship", 搞好工作, 搞好卫生 "keep things clean". It is 搞 with the result 好, and you can put 得 or 不 in the middle: 搞得好, 搞不好. 好 is a woman with her child.
column6: Wǒmen yào gǎohǎo tuánduì hézuò.
column7: We must make teamwork go well.
column9: To do something well, to get it right: 搞好關係 "build a good relationship", 搞好工作, 搞好衛生 "keep things clean". It is 搞 with the result 好, and you can put 得 or 不 in the middle: 搞得好, 搞不好. 好 is a woman with her child.

column3: To get to work with one's hands: 动手做 "make it yourself", 自己动手 "do it yourself". Also to start hitting someone (不要动手 "no fighting"), and on signs 请勿动手 "do not touch". A verb plus an object, so 动了手 is normal.
column4: 遇到问题，我们自己动手解决。
column5: 遇到問題，我們自己動手解決。
column6: Yùdào wèntí, wǒmen zìjǐ dòngshǒu jiějué.
column7: When we meet a problem, we solve it ourselves.
column9: To get to work with one's hands: 動手做 "make it yourself", 自己動手 "do it yourself". Also to start hitting someone (不要動手 "no fighting"), and on signs 請勿動手 "do not touch". A verb plus an object, so 動了手 is normal.

column3: Trade between companies or countries: 国际贸易, 对外贸易 "foreign trade", 贸易战 "trade war". It is the large-scale word, not for buying in a shop. 贸 has 贝 "money" and 易 here means "exchange", as in 交易, not "easy" as in 容易.
column4: 两国之间的贸易越来越多。
column5: 兩國之間的貿易越來越多。
column6: Liǎng guó zhījiān de màoyì yuèláiyuè duō.
column7: Trade between the two countries keeps growing.
column9: Trade between companies or countries: 國際貿易, 對外貿易 "foreign trade", 貿易戰 "trade war". It is the large-scale word, not for buying in a shop. 貿 has 貝 "money" and 易 here means "exchange", as in 交易, not "easy" as in 容易.

column3: A patent: 申请专利 "apply for a patent", 专利权, 专利技术. It also means an exclusive right in general. 专 "special, exclusive" plus 利 "benefit": a benefit only one holder has. 利 shows a knife 刂 cutting grain 禾.
column4: 这项技术已经申请了专利。
column5: 這項技術已經申請了專利。
column6: Zhè xiàng jìshù yǐjīng shēnqǐng le zhuānlì.
column7: A patent has already been applied for on this technology.
column9: A patent: 申請專利 "apply for a patent", 專利權, 專利技術. It also means an exclusive right in general. 專 "special, exclusive" plus 利 "benefit": a benefit only one holder has. 利 shows a knife 刂 cutting grain 禾.

column3: Capital, money put into a business: 投入资本, 资本家 "capitalist", 资本主义 "capitalism". Also a figurative asset: 他有骄傲的资本 "he has reason to be proud". 本 is a tree with its root marked, the base or root of something, as in 本钱 "starting capital".
column4: 开公司需要足够的资本。
column5: 開公司需要足夠的資本。
column6: Kāi gōngsī xūyào zúgòu de zīběn.
column7: Starting a company takes enough capital.
column9: Capital, money put into a business: 投入資本, 資本家 "capitalist", 資本主義 "capitalism". Also a figurative asset: 他有驕傲的資本 "he has reason to be proud". 本 is a tree with its root marked, the base or root of something, as in 本錢 "starting capital".

column3: Assets, property worth money: 固定资产 "fixed assets", 总资产 "total assets", 个人资产. It speaks mostly of a company's or a person's whole holdings on a balance sheet. 资 "capital" plus 产 "produce".
column4: 这家公司的资产超过一亿元。
column5: 這家公司的資產超過一億元。
column6: Zhè jiā gōngsī de zīchǎn chāoguò yīyì yuán.
column7: This company has assets of over a hundred million yuan.
column9: Assets, property worth money: 固定資產 "fixed assets", 總資產 "total assets", 個人資產. It speaks mostly of a company's or a person's whole holdings on a balance sheet. 資 "capital" plus 產 "produce".

column3: A fund: an investment fund (买基金 "buy into a fund"), a foundation (基金会), or a sum set aside (教育基金). 基 "foundation" has 土 "earth" and 金 is "gold, metal, money", so it is money laid as a base.
column4: 他把一部分钱买了基金。
column5: 他把一部分錢買了基金。
column6: Tā bǎ yī bùfen qián mǎi le jījīn.
column7: He put part of his money into a fund.
column9: A fund: an investment fund (買基金 "buy into a fund"), a foundation (基金會), or a sum set aside (教育基金). 基 "foundation" has 土 "earth" and 金 is "gold, metal, money", so it is money laid as a base.

column3: Profit: 利润率 "profit margin", 赚取利润, 利润增长. The money left over after costs, as in 成本. 润 usually means to moisten, which is why it has 氵 "water", so profit is what "moistens" a business. Not for personal earnings, which are 收入.
column4: 公司今年的利润增长了两成。
column5: 公司今年的利潤增長了兩成。
column6: Gōngsī jīnnián de lìrùn zēngzhǎng le liǎng chéng.
column7: The company's profit grew by twenty percent this year.
column9: Profit: 利潤率 "profit margin", 賺取利潤, 利潤增長. The money left over after costs, as in 成本. 潤 usually means to moisten, which is why it has 氵 "water", so profit is what "moistens" a business. Not for personal earnings, which are 收入.

column3: Cost, what it takes to make or do something: 生产成本, 降低成本 "cut costs", 成本高. It is the seller's cost; the price a buyer pays is 价格. 本 is a tree with its root marked, the "root" money. It is used about effort too: 时间成本 "cost in time".
column4: 原料涨价，生产成本也高了。
column5: 原料漲價，生產成本也高了。
column6: Yuánliào zhǎngjià, shēngchǎn chéngběn yě gāo le.
column7: Raw materials went up in price, so production costs rose too.
column9: Cost, what it takes to make or do something: 生產成本, 降低成本 "cut costs", 成本高. It is the seller's cost; the price a buyer pays is 價格. 本 is a tree with its root marked, the "root" money. It is used about effort too: 時間成本 "cost in time".

column3: The effect or result of an effort: 成效显著 "clear results", 取得成效 "achieve results", 见成效 "show results". It is a formal word for the result of measures, policies or work, and is nearly always good. A bad result is 后果.
column4: 这项政策已经取得了明显的成效。
column5: 這項政策已經取得了明顯的成效。
column6: Zhè xiàng zhèngcè yǐjīng qǔdé le míngxiǎn de chéngxiào.
column7: This policy has already achieved clear results.
column9: The effect or result of an effort: 成效顯著 "clear results", 取得成效 "achieve results", 見成效 "show results". It is a formal word for the result of measures, policies or work, and is nearly always good. A bad result is 後果.

column3: Business or professional work, what a company or an employee deals with: 业务能力 "professional skill", 业务员 "salesperson", 熟悉业务, 开展业务 "start a line of business". It is about the work of a firm or a trade, not about business as in "company", which is 公司.
column4: 他对公司的业务很熟悉。
column5: 他對公司的業務很熟悉。
column6: Tā duì gōngsī de yèwù hěn shúxī.
column7: He knows the company's business well.
column9: Business or professional work, what a company or an employee deals with: 業務能力 "professional skill", 業務員 "salesperson", 熟悉業務, 開展業務 "start a line of business". It is about the work of a firm or a trade, not about business as in "company", which is 公司.

column3: An industry or sector of the economy: 第三产业 "the service sector", 旅游产业, 产业链 "industrial chain". Less often it means property that one owns, such as family property. It is broader than 工业 "manufacturing". 产 "produce" and 业 "trade".
column4: 旅游是这个城市的主要产业。
column5: 旅遊是這個城市的主要產業。
column6: Lǚyóu shì zhège chéngshì de zhǔyào chǎnyè.
column7: Tourism is this city's main industry.
column9: An industry or sector of the economy: 第三產業 "the service sector", 旅遊產業, 產業鏈 "industrial chain". Less often it means property that one owns, such as family property. It is broader than 工業 "manufacturing". 產 "produce" and 業 "trade".

column3: In everyday China, the management company of a housing estate, and also real estate: 物业费 "management fee", 联系物业 "contact the management", 物业公司. Residents deal with 物业 for repairs, cleaning and security. 物 "things" plus 业 "estate, trade".
column6: Shuǐguǎn huài le, qǐng liánxì wùyè.
column7: The water pipe is broken, please contact the property management.
column9: In everyday China, the management company of a housing estate, and also real estate: 物業費 "management fee", 聯繫物業 "contact the management", 物業公司. Residents deal with 物業 for repairs, cleaning and security. 物 "things" plus 業 "estate, trade".

column3: A corporate group of many companies, and sometimes a bloc: 企业集团, 集团公司, 军事集团. It sits in a company's name for the parent firm. 集 is birds 隹 gathering on a tree 木 and 团 is a crowd inside an enclosure, so both characters mean "gather".
column4: 这个集团在很多国家都有工厂。
column5: 這個集團在很多國家都有工廠。
column6: Zhège jítuán zài hěn duō guójiā dōu yǒu gōngchǎng.
column7: This group has factories in many countries.
column9: A corporate group of many companies, and sometimes a bloc: 企業集團, 集團公司, 軍事集團. It sits in a company's name for the parent firm. 集 is birds 隹 gathering on a tree 木 and 團 is a crowd inside an enclosure, so both characters mean "gather".

column3: To act on someone's behalf: 代理人 "agent", 代理商 "distributor", 代理经理 "acting manager". In computing it is a proxy. It also means to deal in a brand for its maker: 代理这个品牌. 代 "replace" and 理 "manage", the same 理 as in 经理 and 助理.
column4: 经理出差了，由副经理代理。
column5: 經理出差了，由副經理代理。
column6: Jīnglǐ chūchāi le, yóu fùjīnglǐ dàilǐ.
column7: The manager is away, so the deputy manager is acting for him.
column9: To act on someone's behalf: 代理人 "agent", 代理商 "distributor", 代理經理 "acting manager". In computing it is a proxy. It also means to deal in a brand for its maker: 代理這個品牌. 代 "replace" and 理 "manage", the same 理 as in 經理 and 助理.

column3: To write back, and a reply letter: 给我回信 "write back to me", 收到回信, 回信了. As a verb it takes its object before it: 给他回信, not 回信他. 回 comes from a spiral and means "return", and 信 is a letter.
column6: Tā hěn kuài jiù huíxìn le.
column7: He wrote back very quickly.
column9: To write back, and a reply letter: 給我回信 "write back to me", 收到回信, 回信了. As a verb it takes its object before it: 給他回信, not 回信他. 回 comes from a spiral and means "return", and 信 is a letter.

column3: A letter that has come to you, and to write to the speaker: 读者来信 "readers' letters", 收到你的来信, 欢迎来信 "letters welcome". The 来 is from the receiver's point of view. The 来 is a wheat plant, and today also has the meaning "come".
column4: 我今天收到了他的来信。
column5: 我今天收到了他的來信。
column6: Wǒ jīntiān shōudào le tā de láixìn.
column7: I received a letter from him today.
column9: A letter that has come to you, and to write to the speaker: 讀者來信 "readers' letters", 收到你的來信, 歡迎來信 "letters welcome". The 來 is from the receiver's point of view. The 來 is a wheat plant, and today also has the meaning "come".

column3: A short informal note: 留便条 "leave a note", 写便条, 一张便条. It is a slip of paper for a message, for example to a roommate, or for a request. 便 means casual and convenient here, read biàn, and 条 is a strip or slip.
column4: 他在桌上留了一张便条。
column5: 他在桌上留了一張便條。
column6: Tā zài zhuō shàng liú le yī zhāng biàntiáo.
column7: He left a note on the table.
column9: A short informal note: 留便條 "leave a note", 寫便條, 一張便條. It is a slip of paper for a message, for example to a roommate, or for a request. 便 means casual and convenient here, read biàn, and 條 is a strip or slip.

column3: A notice posted publicly or placed in a paper: 招聘启事 "job notice", 寻人启事 "missing-person notice", 贴启事. It is an announcement about one particular matter. 启 is a door 户 being opened by a mouth 口, which gives "begin, announce".
column6: Ménkǒu tiēzhe yī zhāng qǐshì.
column7: A notice is posted at the door.
column9: A notice posted publicly or placed in a paper: 招聘啟事 "job notice", 尋人啟事 "missing-person notice", 貼啟事. It is an announcement about one particular matter. 啟 is a door 戶 being opened by a mouth 口, which gives "begin, announce".

column3: An attachment to an email, or an appendix to a document: 添加附件, 打开附件, 见附件 "see attached". It can also mean an accessory for a machine. 附 "attach" has 阝 and 付 for the sound, and 件 is a countable item.
column6: Qǐng kàn yóujiàn lǐ de fùjiàn.
column7: Please look at the attachment in the email.
column9: An attachment to an email, or an appendix to a document: 添加附件, 打開附件, 見附件 "see attached". It can also mean an accessory for a machine. 附 "attach" has 阝 and 付 for the sound, and 件 is a countable item.

column3: To hint or remind, and a hint or prompt: 提示信息, 温馨提示 "friendly reminder" on signs, 屏幕提示 "on-screen prompt". It gives a pointer without saying everything. 提 "raise" has 扌 "hand", and 示 is a picture of an altar, with the meaning "show".
column4: 屏幕上出现了一条提示。
column5: 屏幕上出現了一條提示。
column6: Píngmù shàng chūxiàn le yī tiáo tíshì.
column7: A prompt appeared on the screen.
column9: To hint or remind, and a hint or prompt: 提示信息, 溫馨提示 "friendly reminder" on signs, 屏幕提示 "on-screen prompt". It gives a pointer without saying everything. 提 "raise" has 扌 "hand", and 示 is a picture of an altar, with the meaning "show".

column3: To warn, in a stronger and more official sense than 提醒: 警告他不要… "warn him not to…", 受到警告 "receive a warning", 严重警告. The warning comes from an authority and has consequences if ignored. 警 has 言 "speech" below 敬 and 告 means to tell.
column4: 老师警告他不要再迟到。
column5: 老師警告他不要再遲到。
column6: Lǎoshī jǐnggào tā bùyào zài chídào.
column7: The teacher warned him not to be late again.
column9: To warn, in a stronger and more official sense than 提醒: 警告他不要… "warn him not to…", 受到警告 "receive a warning", 嚴重警告. The warning comes from an authority and has consequences if ignored. 警 has 言 "speech" below 敬 and 告 means to tell.

column3: To instruct, as a superior: 上级指示 "instructions from above", 按照指示, 作出指示. As a noun it is an order or directive. It can also mean to indicate or point out, as with a signal or a gauge. 指 combines 扌 "hand" and 旨, which also gives the sound.
column4: 我们要按照领导的指示办事。
column5: 我們要按照領導的指示辦事。
column6: Wǒmen yào ànzhào lǐngdǎo de zhǐshì bànshì.
column7: We must act according to the leader's instructions.
column9: To instruct, as a superior: 上級指示 "instructions from above", 按照指示, 作出指示. As a noun it is an order or directive. It can also mean to indicate or point out, as with a signal or a gauge. 指 combines 扌 "hand" and 旨, which also gives the sound.

column3: To pass something along from one to another: 传递信息 "pass on information", 传递给下一个人, 传递热量 "transfer heat". It is for things and also for feelings and messages. Both characters mean "pass" and carry the 辶 or 亻 of movement and people. 传 is read zhuàn in 传记 "biography".
column4: 这个消息很快传递到各地。
column5: 這個消息很快傳遞到各地。
column6: Zhège xiāoxi hěn kuài chuándì dào gèdì.
column7: The news spread quickly to all places.
column9: To pass something along from one to another: 傳遞信息 "pass on information", 傳遞給下一個人, 傳遞熱量 "transfer heat". It is for things and also for feelings and messages. Both characters mean "pass" and carry the 辶 or 亻 of movement and people. 傳 is read zhuàn in 傳記 "biography".

column3: A mailbox or post office box: 邮政信箱, 电子信箱 "email box". In speech 邮箱 is more usual for email. 箱 is a box: ⺮ "bamboo" on top as the material, and 相 below for the sound.
column6: Xìnxiāng lǐ yǒu yī fēng xìn.
column7: There is a letter in the mailbox.
column9: A mailbox or post office box: 郵政信箱, 電子信箱 "email box". In speech 郵箱 is more usual for email. 箱 is a box: ⺮ "bamboo" on top as the material, and 相 below for the sound.

column3: A fax, to fax: 发传真, 传真机 "fax machine", 传真号码. It is "transmit a true copy": 传 "transmit" and 真 "true". In older documents also "a lifelike portrait". Used for the thing and the action, and now rarer than email.
column6: Qǐng bǎ wénjiàn chuánzhēn gěi wǒ.
column7: Please fax the document to me.
column9: A fax, to fax: 發傳真, 傳真機 "fax machine", 傳真號碼. It is "transmit a true copy": 傳 "transmit" and 真 "true". In older documents also "a lifelike portrait". Used for the thing and the action, and now rarer than email.

column3: To send money, especially to another city or country: 银行汇款, 汇款单 "money order", 给家里汇款. Also the money sent. 汇 is water 氵 gathering in a container 匚, hence "gather, remit", and 款 means a sum of money.
column6: Wǒ jīntiān gěi jiālǐ huìkuǎn le.
column7: I sent money home today.
column9: To send money, especially to another city or country: 銀行匯款, 匯款單 "money order", 給家裡匯款. Also the money sent. 匯 is water 氵 gathering in a container 匚, hence "gather, remit", and 款 means a sum of money.

column3: To sign, to write one's name: 签个名, 签字, 签合同 "sign a contract". It is also a thin stick or slip: 抽签 "draw lots", 牙签 "toothpick", which is why it has ⺮ "bamboo" on top. 佥 below gives the sound.
column6: Qǐng zài zhèlǐ qiān yīxià.
column7: Please sign here.
column9: To sign, to write one's name: 簽個名, 簽字, 簽合同 "sign a contract". It is also a thin stick or slip: 抽籤 "draw lots", 牙籤 "toothpick", which is why it has ⺮ "bamboo" on top. 僉 below gives the sound.

column3: To sign one's name, and a signature or an autograph: 请在这里签名, 明星签名. It stresses writing the name as a mark of who you are, while 签字 is signing to approve. 名 has 夕 "evening" and 口 "mouth": a name called out when it is too dark to see.
column6: Zhè wèi gēshǒu gěi fěnsī qiānmíng.
column7: This singer signs autographs for fans.
column9: To sign one's name, and a signature or an autograph: 請在這裡簽名, 明星簽名. It stresses writing the name as a mark of who you are, while 簽字 is signing to approve. 名 has 夕 "evening" and 口 "mouth": a name called out when it is too dark to see.

column3: To sign a document, to approve: 签字同意 "sign to agree", 请签字, 合同上签字. It is the act of putting your name to something official, so it is used with contracts, forms and orders. 字 is a child 子 under a roof 宀. It is a verb plus object: 签了字.
column4: 你签字以后合同就有效了。
column5: 你簽字以後合同就有效了。
column6: Nǐ qiānzì yǐhòu hétong jiù yǒuxiào le.
column7: Once you sign, the contract takes effect.
column9: To sign a document, to approve: 簽字同意 "sign to agree", 請簽字, 合同上簽字. It is the act of putting your name to something official, so it is used with contracts, forms and orders. 字 is a child 子 under a roof 宀. It is a verb plus object: 簽了字.

column3: To sign a contract or agreement, formal: 签约仪式 "signing ceremony", 正式签约, 公司签约. Often a team, company or a player signing with another party. 约 means "agreement" here (also "about" and "make an appointment"). 约 has 纟 "thread", for binding.
column4: 两家公司今天正式签约。
column5: 兩家公司今天正式簽約。
column6: Liǎng jiā gōngsī jīntiān zhèngshì qiānyuē.
column7: The two companies formally signed a contract today.
column9: To sign a contract or agreement, formal: 簽約儀式 "signing ceremony", 正式簽約, 公司簽約. Often a team, company or a player signing with another party. 約 means "agreement" here (also "about" and "make an appointment"). 約 has 糹 "thread", for binding.

column3: To sign and conclude a treaty, contract or agreement: 签订合同, 签订协议, 签订条约. Both sides sign it and it is official. The object is always a document or deal, never a person. 订 has 讠 "speech" and 丁, and also means to book or order, as in 订票.
column6: Shuāngfāng qiāndìng le yī fèn hétong.
column7: Both sides signed a contract.
column9: To sign and conclude a treaty, contract or agreement: 簽訂合同, 簽訂協議, 簽訂條約. Both sides sign it and it is official. The object is always a document or deal, never a person. 訂 has 言 "speech" and 丁, and also means to book or order, as in 訂票.

column3: An agreement, in writing or not: 达成协议 "reach an agreement", 签订协议, 和平协议. Also the verb "to agree upon". 协议 stresses that both sides agree; a 合同 "contract" stresses legal rights and duties.
column6: Shuāngfāng zhōngyú dáchéng le xiéyì.
column7: The two sides finally reached an agreement.
column9: An agreement, in writing or not: 達成協議 "reach an agreement", 簽訂協議, 和平協議. Also the verb "to agree upon". 協議 stresses that both sides agree; a 合同 "contract" stresses legal rights and duties.

column3: The written document of an agreement: 签协议书, 一份协议书. 协议 is the agreement itself and 书 makes it the paper, as in 证书, 说明书 and 保证书 "written guarantee". It is a plain contract between parties.
column6: Tāmen qiān le yī fèn xiéyìshū.
column7: They signed a written agreement.
column9: The written document of an agreement: 簽協議書, 一份協議書. 協議 is the agreement itself and 書 makes it the paper, as in 證書, 說明書 and 保證書 "written guarantee". It is a plain contract between parties.

column3: A certificate: 毕业证书, 获得证书, 荣誉证书 "certificate of honor", 资格证书 "qualification". The paper that proves something. 证 is speech 讠 plus 正 "right", which also gives the sound, and it means to prove or testify.
column4: 她拿到了英语考试的证书。
column5: 她拿到了英語考試的證書。
column6: Tā ná dào le Yīngyǔ kǎoshì de zhèngshū.
column7: She received the certificate for her English exam.
column9: A certificate: 畢業證書, 獲得證書, 榮譽證書 "certificate of honor", 資格證書 "qualification". The paper that proves something. 證 is speech 言 plus 登, which gives the sound, and it means to prove or testify.

column3: To permit, and permission: 得到许可, 未经许可 "without permission", 许可证 "permit, license". It is formal and often has an official ring, with an authority doing the permitting. In everyday speech, people say 允许 or 让. Both characters mean "may".
column4: 没有许可，不能进入这里。
column5: 沒有許可，不能進入這裡。
column6: Méiyǒu xǔkě, bù néng jìnrù zhèlǐ.
column7: You cannot enter here without permission.
column9: To permit, and permission: 得到許可, 未經許可 "without permission", 許可證 "permit, license". It is formal and often has an official ring, with an authority doing the permitting. In everyday speech, people say 允許 or 讓. Both characters mean "may".

column3: To register: 注册账号 "create an account", 注册公司, 注册商标, 注册会员. 注 here means "to enter, to record" and 册 is a register or volume, a picture of bamboo strips tied together. The same 册 is a measure for books in 第一册. Used for sites, schools and companies.
column4: 你需要先注册一个账号。
column5: 你需要先註冊一個帳號。
column6: Nǐ xūyào xiān zhùcè yī ge zhànghào.
column7: You need to register an account first.
column9: To register: 註冊帳號 "create an account", 註冊公司, 註冊商標, 註冊會員. 註 here means "to enter, to record" and 冊 is a register or volume, a picture of bamboo strips tied together. The same 冊 is a measure for books in 第一冊. Used for sites, schools and companies.

column3: To reach, in the sense of coming to an agreement: 达成协议, 达成共识 "reach a consensus", 达成目标 "reach a goal". The object is an abstract result, never a place; for a place use 到达. 达 "reach" and 成 "complete".
column4: 经过讨论，大家达成了共识。
column5: 經過討論，大家達成了共識。
column6: Jīngguò tǎolùn, dàjiā dáchéng le gòngshí.
column7: After discussion, everyone reached a consensus.
column9: To reach, in the sense of coming to an agreement: 達成協議, 達成共識 "reach a consensus", 達成目標 "reach a goal". The object is an abstract result, never a place; for a place use 到達. 達 "reach" and 成 "complete".

column3: A visa: 申请签证, 办签证 "get a visa", 旅游签证, 签证过期 "visa expired". It is a mark of permission signed 签 and stamped in a passport, as proof 证.
column6: Qù Měiguó xūyào bàn qiānzhèng.
column7: You need to get a visa to go to America.
column9: A visa: 申請簽證, 辦簽證 "get a visa", 旅遊簽證, 簽證過期 "visa expired". It is a mark of permission signed 簽 and stamped in a passport, as proof 證.

column3: To entrust a task to someone, or to commission: 委托律师 "hire a lawyer", 委托书 "power of attorney", 受人委托 "on someone's behalf". Pattern: 委托 + person + verb: 委托他办理. 托 has 扌 "hand" and supports something, which fits "put into someone's hands".
column4: 他委托律师处理这件事。
column5: 他委託律師處理這件事。
column6: Tā wěituō lǜshī chǔlǐ zhè jiàn shì.
column7: He entrusted the matter to a lawyer.
column9: To entrust a task to someone, or to commission: 委託律師 "hire a lawyer", 委託書 "power of attorney", 受人委託 "on someone's behalf". Pattern: 委託 + person + verb: 委託他辦理. 託 has 言 "speech" and 乇 for the sound.

column3: Formal talks between two sides: 举行会谈 "hold talks", 双边会谈 "bilateral talks", 会谈结束. Used for governments, companies and leaders, not for a chat, which is 聊天. 会 is people 人 speaking 云, and the 炎 in 谈 still sounds nearly alike (yán, tán).
column4: 两国领导人举行了会谈。
column5: 兩國領導人舉行了會談。
column6: Liǎng guó lǐngdǎorén jǔxíng le huìtán.
