column3: To build or construct something such as a road, railway, dam or building, usually public works: 修建铁路 "build a railway", 修建水库. It is a little more formal than 建 and suits large projects. 修 is to repair or build and 建 is to set up.
column4: 政府打算在这里修建一条高速公路。
column5: 政府打算在這裡修建一條高速公路。
column6: Zhèngfǔ dǎsuàn zài zhèlǐ xiūjiàn yī tiáo gāosùgōnglù.
column7: The government plans to build an expressway here.
column9: To build or construct something such as a road, railway, dam or building, usually public works: 修建鐵路 "build a railway", 修建水庫. It is a little more formal than 建 and suits large projects. 修 is to repair or build and 建 is to set up.

column3: To make something out of a material: 用木头制成 "made of wood", 制成品 "finished product". The pattern is 用/由 + material + 制成 + product, or product + 由 + material + 制成. 制 "make, manufacture" + 成 "become", the result.
column4: 这张桌子是用竹子制成的。
column5: 這張桌子是用竹子製成的。
column6: Zhè zhāng zhuōzi shì yòng zhúzi zhìchéng de.
column7: This table is made of bamboo.
column9: To make something out of a material: 用木頭製成 "made of wood", 製成品 "finished product". The pattern is 用/由 + material + 製成 + product, or product + 由 + material + 製成. 製 "make, manufacture" + 成 "become", the result.

column3: To come into being or to produce something as a result of a process, a term that is common in science and computing: 生成新的文件 "generate a new file", 水和二氧化碳生成. 生 is "produce" and 成 "become", so something is born and takes shape.
column4: 这个程序会自动生成报告。
column5: 這個程式會自動生成報告。
column6: Zhège chéngxù huì zìdòng shēngchéng bàogào.
column7: This program generates a report automatically.
column9: To come into being or to produce something as a result of a process, a term that is common in science and computing: 生成新的文件 "generate a new file", 水和二氧化碳生成. 生 is "produce" and 成 "become", so something is born and takes shape.

column3: To combine parts into one whole, especially in chemistry, sound and images, and also a noun for something synthetic: 合成材料 "synthetic material", 合成图片 "composite picture". 合 "join" + 成 "become". It is the opposite of 分解.
column4: 这种布料是用化学纤维合成的。
column5: 這種布料是用化學纖維合成的。
column6: Zhè zhǒng bùliào shì yòng huàxué xiānwéi héchéng de.
column7: This fabric is synthesized from chemical fibers.
column9: To combine parts into one whole, especially in chemistry, sound and images, and also a noun for something synthetic: 合成材料 "synthetic material", 合成圖片 "composite picture". 合 "join" + 成 "become". It is the opposite of 分解.

column3: To break something down into parts or into simpler substances: 分解成小部分 "break into small parts", 水被分解, 分解动作 "break an action down". It is used for chemical decomposition and for taking a task apart. 解 is "untie, separate" and carries the sense of taking things apart.
column6: Xìjūn kěyǐ fēnjiě lājī.
column7: Bacteria can break down garbage.
column9: To break something down into parts or into simpler substances: 分解成小部分 "break into small parts", 水被分解, 分解動作 "break an action down". It is used for chemical decomposition and for taking a task apart. 解 is "untie, separate" and carries the sense of taking things apart.

column3: To sort things into categories: 垃圾分类 "garbage sorting", 按颜色分类 "classify by color". It is also a noun for a classification. The verb comes before the thing sorted when it is a modifier, and 把 can bring the thing before the verb: 把书分类. 类 means "kind".
column4: 我们把图书按内容分类。
column5: 我們把圖書按內容分類。
column6: Wǒmen bǎ túshū àn nèiróng fēnlèi.
column7: We sort the books by subject.
column9: To sort things into categories: 垃圾分類 "garbage sorting", 按顏色分類 "classify by color". It is also a noun for a classification. The verb comes before the thing sorted when it is a modifier, and 把 can bring the thing before the verb: 把書分類. 類 means "kind".

column3: To divide up an area, a period or responsibilities according to some standard: 划分地区 "divide into regions", 划分责任. It is more about setting boundaries than cutting. 划 is read hua4 here, but it is hua2 in "row a boat".
column4: 这个国家被划分为二十个省。
column5: 這個國家被劃分為二十個省。
column6: Zhège guójiā bèi huàfēn wéi èrshí ge shěng.
column7: This country is divided into twenty provinces.
column9: To divide up an area, a period or responsibilities according to some standard: 劃分地區 "divide into regions", 劃分責任. It is more about setting boundaries than cutting. 劃 is read hua4 here, but it is hua2 in "row a boat".

column3: To pack goods for sale or shipping, and the packaging itself: 包装纸 "wrapping paper", 精美的包装. Figuratively it is to present someone or something attractively, often a little falsely: 包装明星. 包 "wrap" + 装 "load, dress up".
column4: 这份礼物的包装非常漂亮。
column5: 這份禮物的包裝非常漂亮。
column6: Zhè fèn lǐwù de bāozhuāng fēicháng piàoliang.
column7: The wrapping of this gift is very beautiful.
column9: To pack goods for sale or shipping, and the packaging itself: 包裝紙 "wrapping paper", 精美的包裝. Figuratively it is to present someone or something attractively, often a little falsely: 包裝明星. 包 "wrap" + 裝 "load, dress up".

column3: To repair something damaged until it works or looks as it did before: 修复文物 "restore cultural relics", 修复系统漏洞 "fix a system bug", 修复关系 "mend a relationship". It is a bigger and more careful repair than 修理. 复 means "return, restore".
column4: 工人们正在修复被雨水冲坏的路。
column5: 工人們正在修復被雨水沖壞的路。
column6: Gōngrénmen zhèngzài xiūfù bèi yǔshuǐ chōnghuài de lù.
column7: Workers are repairing the road that the rain washed out.
column9: To repair something damaged until it works or looks as it did before: 修復文物 "restore cultural relics", 修復系統漏洞 "fix a system bug", 修復關係 "mend a relationship". It is a bigger and more careful repair than 修理. 復 means "return, restore".

column3: To decorate a room, a building or an object to make it look nicer, and the decoration itself: 装饰房间 "decorate a room", 装饰品 "ornament". 装 is "dress up" and 饰 "adorn", so the word is about making a place or thing look dressed up.
column6: Tā yòng xiānhuā zhuāngshì le kètīng.
column7: She decorated the living room with fresh flowers.
column9: To decorate a room, a building or an object to make it look nicer, and the decoration itself: 裝飾房間 "decorate a room", 裝飾品 "ornament". 裝 is "dress up" and 飾 "adorn", so the word is about making a place or thing look dressed up.

column3: A change or shift, as a noun, and to change as a verb, usually of things that are expected to stay steady, such as plans, prices, personnel: 人事变动 "personnel changes", 价格变动, 没有变动. 变 "change" + 动 "move". It describes adjustments rather than a full transformation.
column4: 公司最近有一些人事变动。
column5: 公司最近有一些人事變動。
column6: Gōngsī zuìjìn yǒu yīxiē rénshì biàndòng.
column7: The company has had some personnel changes recently.
column9: A change or shift, as a noun, and to change as a verb, usually of things that are expected to stay steady, such as plans, prices, personnel: 人事變動 "personnel changes", 價格變動, 沒有變動. 變 "change" + 動 "move". It describes adjustments rather than a full transformation.

column3: To update or renew, now used above all for software and information: 更新系统 "update the system", 软件更新, 知识更新 "refresh one's knowledge". Read geng1 here, "change", not gèng "even more". 更 "change" + 新 "new".
column6: Shǒujī xūyào gēngxīn xìtǒng le.
column7: The phone needs a system update.
column9: To update or renew, now used above all for software and information: 更新系統 "update the system", 軟件更新, 知識更新 "refresh one's knowledge". Read geng1 here, "change", not gèng "even more". 更 "change" + 新 "new".

column3: To replace something, usually a worn or old part, by another of the same kind: 更换轮胎 "change a tire", 更换密码 "change a password", 更换地址. It is for swapping one item for another. Read geng1 here, as in 更新, not gèng. 换 means "exchange".
column4: 你该更换这个旧电池了。
column5: 你該更換這個舊電池了。
column6: Nǐ gāi gēnghuàn zhège jiù diànchí le.
column7: You should replace this old battery.
column9: To replace something, usually a worn or old part, by another of the same kind: 更換輪胎 "change a tire", 更換密碼 "change a password", 更換地址. It is for swapping one item for another. Read geng1 here, as in 更新, not gèng. 換 means "exchange".

column3: To turn into something different, often of one kind of thing into another: 转化为能量 "convert into energy", 矛盾转化. The pattern is A 转化为 B or A 转化成 B. It suggests a change of nature, not just form. 转 "turn" + 化 "change".
column4: 这种机器把热能转化为电能。
column5: 這種機器把熱能轉化為電能。
column6: Zhè zhǒng jīqì bǎ rènéng zhuǎnhuà wéi diànnéng.
column7: This machine turns heat energy into electricity.
column9: To turn into something different, often of one kind of thing into another: 轉化為能量 "convert into energy", 矛盾轉化. The pattern is A 轉化為 B or A 轉化成 B. It suggests a change of nature, not just form. 轉 "turn" + 化 "change".

column3: To switch from one state, form or mode to another: 转换角色 "switch roles", 转换思路 "change one's way of thinking", 转换成 "convert into". It stresses an act of switching and is common with formats and modes. 转 "turn" + 换 "exchange".
column6: Qǐng bǎ wénjiàn zhuǎnhuàn chéng PDF géshì.
column7: Please convert the file to PDF format.
column9: To switch from one state, form or mode to another: 轉換角色 "switch roles", 轉換思路 "change one's way of thinking", 轉換成 "convert into". It stresses an act of switching and is common with formats and modes. 轉 "turn" + 換 "exchange".

column3: To change direction, literally for a vehicle or a person, and figuratively to change one's attitude or approach: 向左转向 "turn left", 转向新能源 "turn to new energy". 转 "turn" + 向 "direction". Here 转 is read zhuan3.
column6: Qìchē tūrán xiàng yòu zhuǎnxiàng.
column7: The car suddenly turned right.
column9: To change direction, literally for a vehicle or a person, and figuratively to change one's attitude or approach: 向左轉向 "turn left", 轉向新能源 "turn to new energy". 轉 "turn" + 向 "direction". Here 轉 is read zhuan3.

column3: To transfer ownership or a right to someone else, for a price or free: 转让房子 "transfer a house", 转让股份 "transfer shares", and the shop sign 店面转让 "shop for transfer". 转 "turn over" + 让 "let, give up". It is a formal, legal and business word.
column6: Tā bǎ diàn zhuǎnràng gěi le péngyou.
column7: He transferred the shop to a friend.
column9: To transfer ownership or a right to someone else, for a price or free: 轉讓房子 "transfer a house", 轉讓股份 "transfer shares", and the shop sign 店面轉讓 "shop for transfer". 轉 "turn over" + 讓 "let, give up". It is a formal, legal and business word.

column3: To transfer someone to another post or to move forces, and to mobilize or stir up: 工作调动 "job transfer", 调动积极性 "get people motivated". Read diao4 here, not tiao2: it is the 调 of "transfer", as in 调查 and 调整. 动 adds the idea of moving.
column4: 公司把他调动到上海分公司。
column5: 公司把他調動到上海分公司。
column6: Gōngsī bǎ tā diàodòng dào Shànghǎi fēngōngsī.
column7: The company transferred him to the Shanghai branch.
column9: To transfer someone to another post or to move forces, and to mobilize or stir up: 工作調動 "job transfer", 調動積極性 "get people motivated". Read diao4 here, not tiao2: it is the 調 of "transfer", as in 調查 and 調整. 動 adds the idea of moving.

column3: To adjust something so that it fits or stays in balance: 调节温度 "adjust the temperature", 调节心情 "regulate one's mood", 调节器 "regulator". It suggests fine control of a degree or level. 调 is read tiao2 here, "adjust, blend", and 节 is "regulate".
column4: 你可以自己调节空调的温度。
column5: 你可以自己調節空調的溫度。
column6: Nǐ kěyǐ zìjǐ tiáojié kōngtiáo de wēndù.
column7: You can adjust the air conditioner's temperature yourself.
column9: To adjust something so that it fits or stays in balance: 調節溫度 "adjust the temperature", 調節心情 "regulate one's mood", 調節器 "regulator". It suggests fine control of a degree or level. 調 is read tiao2 here, "adjust, blend", and 節 is "regulate".

column3: To mediate in a dispute and bring the two sides to an agreement: 调解纠纷 "settle a dispute", 调解员 "mediator", 法院调解. It is what a third party does, not the sides themselves. Read the second syllable jie3, as in 解决; the 调 is tiao2 as in 调节.
column4: 社区工作人员帮他们调解了矛盾。
column5: 社區工作人員幫他們調解了矛盾。
column6: Shèqū gōngzuò rényuán bāng tāmen tiáojiě le máodùn.
column7: A community worker helped mediate their quarrel.
column9: To mediate in a dispute and bring the two sides to an agreement: 調解糾紛 "settle a dispute", 調解員 "mediator", 法院調解. It is what a third party does, not the sides themselves. Read the second syllable jie3, as in 解決; the 調 is tiao2 as in 調節.

column3: To flow or move around, for liquids, air, people and money: 空气流动 "air circulates", 流动人口 "migrant population", 流动资金 "working capital". It can also be an adjective, "mobile": 流动图书馆. 流 "flow" + 动 "move".
column4: 河水在山谷里慢慢流动。
column5: 河水在山谷裡慢慢流動。
column6: Héshuǐ zài shāngǔ lǐ mànmàn liúdòng.
column7: The river flows slowly through the valley.
column9: To flow or move around, for liquids, air, people and money: 空氣流動 "air circulates", 流動人口 "migrant population", 流動資金 "working capital". It can also be an adjective, "mobile": 流動圖書館. 流 "flow" + 動 "move".

column3: To circulate freely, of money, goods, information or air: 商品流通 "the circulation of goods", 货币流通, 空气流通 "ventilation". It is about passing through without blockage. 流 "flow" + 通 "go through".
column4: 这种新钞已经开始在市场上流通。
column5: 這種新鈔已經開始在市場上流通。
column6: Zhè zhǒng xīn chāo yǐjīng kāishǐ zài shìchǎng shàng liútōng.
column7: This new banknote has started to circulate in the market.
column9: To circulate freely, of money, goods, information or air: 商品流通 "the circulation of goods", 貨幣流通, 空氣流通 "ventilation". It is about passing through without blockage. 流 "flow" + 通 "go through".

column3: Developments, a trend, or a state of movement, as against 静态: 最新动态 "the latest developments", 市场动态, 关注动态. Social-media users also call a post a 动态 ("update"). It also means dynamic as an adjective. 动 "move" + 态 "state".
column4: 我们要随时关注市场的动态。
column5: 我們要隨時關注市場的動態。
column6: Wǒmen yào suíshí guānzhù shìchǎng de dòngtài.
column7: We must keep following developments in the market at all times.
column9: Developments, a trend, or a state of movement, as against 靜態: 最新動態 "the latest developments", 市場動態, 關注動態. Social-media users also call a post a 動態 ("update"). It also means dynamic as an adjective. 動 "move" + 態 "state".

column3: To increase or add: it is mostly found in compounds, such as 增加, 增长, 增强, 增多, and in the phrase 增产 "increase output". On its own it is a written, bound form. Learn it as the first character of 增加 and the other 增- words, all meaning that something becomes more.
column4: 他的体重一个月增了三公斤。
column5: 他的體重一個月增了三公斤。
column6: Tā de tǐzhòng yī ge yuè zēng le sān gōngjīn.
column7: His weight went up three kilograms in a month.
column9: To increase or add: it is mostly found in compounds, such as 增加, 增長, 增強, 增多, and in the phrase 增產 "increase output". On its own it is a written, bound form. Learn it as the first character of 增加 and the other 增- words, all meaning that something becomes more.

column3: To increase output, usually of crops, factories or oil: 粮食增产 "grain output rises", 增产增收 "more output and more income". The opposite is 减产. 增 "increase" + 产 "produce".
column6: Jīnnián xiǎomài dàfú zēngchǎn.
column7: Wheat output has risen sharply this year.
column9: To increase output, usually of crops, factories or oil: 糧食增產 "grain output rises", 增產增收 "more output and more income". The opposite is 減產. 增 "increase" + 產 "produce".

column3: To become bigger or to make something bigger in size, force or degree: 压力增大 "pressure grows", 增大面积 "enlarge the area". It suits measurable things such as pressure, risk, distance and area, and the result needs no 了 if it is general. 增 "increase" + 大 "big".
column6: Zhèyàng zuò huì zēngdà fēngxiǎn.
column7: Doing it this way will increase the risk.
column9: To become bigger or to make something bigger in size, force or degree: 壓力增大 "pressure grows", 增大面積 "enlarge the area". It suits measurable things such as pressure, risk, distance and area, and the result needs no 了 if it is general. 增 "increase" + 大 "big".

column3: To grow in number or quantity: 游客增多 "more tourists", 人数增多, 雨水增多. It is about counting things becoming more, and it describes a state rather than something done to an object. 增 "increase" + 多 "many".
column4: 夏天来了，游客明显增多。
column5: 夏天來了，遊客明顯增多。
column6: Xiàtiān lái le, yóukè míngxiǎn zēngduō.
column7: Summer has come, and the number of tourists has clearly increased.
column9: To grow in number or quantity: 遊客增多 "more tourists", 人數增多, 雨水增多. It is about counting things becoming more, and it describes a state rather than something done to an object. 增 "increase" + 多 "many".

column3: To strengthen something that already exists, such as strength, confidence, awareness or ability: 增强体质 "build up the body", 增强信心 "boost confidence". The object is an abstract or bodily quality. 增 "increase" + 强 "strong".
column6: Duō yùndòng kěyǐ zēngqiáng tǐzhì.
column7: More exercise can strengthen the body.
column9: To strengthen something that already exists, such as strength, confidence, awareness or ability: 增強體質 "build up the body", 增強信心 "boost confidence". The object is an abstract or bodily quality. 增 "increase" + 強 "strong".

column3: To speed up, as a verb: 加速前进 "speed up", 加速发展 "speed up development", 加速度 "acceleration". Unlike 加快, which is common in speech, 加速 is a bit more technical and fits machines and processes. 加 "add" + 速 "speed".
column4: 车子慢慢加速，开上了高速公路。
column5: 車子慢慢加速，開上了高速公路。
column6: Chēzi mànmàn jiāsù, kāishàng le gāosùgōnglù.
column7: The car slowly sped up and drove onto the expressway.
column9: To speed up, as a verb: 加速前進 "speed up", 加速發展 "speed up development", 加速度 "acceleration". Unlike 加快, which is common in speech, 加速 is a bit more technical and fits machines and processes. 加 "add" + 速 "speed".

column3: To rise or to raise something in height, level or degree: 气温升高 "the temperature rises", 升高了两米, 血压升高. It is for things that climb along a scale. 升 "rise" + 高 "high".
column4: 天气转暖，气温慢慢升高。
column5: 天氣轉暖，氣溫慢慢升高。
column6: Tiānqì zhuǎn nuǎn, qìwēn mànmàn shēnggāo.
column7: As the weather warms, the temperature rises slowly.
column9: To rise or to raise something in height, level or degree: 氣溫升高 "the temperature rises", 升高了兩米, 血壓升高. It is for things that climb along a scale. 升 "rise" + 高 "high".

column3: To enlarge or magnify: 放大照片 "enlarge a photo", 放大镜 "magnifying glass", 把声音放大 "turn the sound up". It also means to exaggerate: 放大问题. 放 "put, let go" + 大 "big".
column4: 请把这张照片放大一点儿。
column5: 請把這張照片放大一點兒。
column6: Qǐng bǎ zhè zhāng zhàopiàn fàngdà yīdiǎnr.
column7: Please enlarge this photo a little.
column9: To enlarge or magnify: 放大照片 "enlarge a photo", 放大鏡 "magnifying glass", 把聲音放大 "turn the sound up". It also means to exaggerate: 放大問題. 放 "put, let go" + 大 "big".

column3: To add something to something else: 一加上二 "one plus two", 加上盐 "add salt". It is also a conjunction, "on top of that, plus", at the start of a clause: 加上天气不好，我们没去. 加 "add" + 上 "on top".
column4: 他很聪明，加上努力，成绩一直很好。
column5: 他很聰明，加上努力，成績一直很好。
column6: Tā hěn cōngming, jiāshang nǔlì, chéngjì yīzhí hěn hǎo.
column7: He is smart, and on top of that he works hard, so his grades have always been good.
column9: To add something to something else: 一加上二 "one plus two", 加上鹽 "add salt". It is also a conjunction, "on top of that, plus", at the start of a clause: 加上天氣不好，我們沒去. 加 "add" + 上 "on top".

column3: To heat something up: 加热食物 "heat food", 加热到一百度 "heat to 100 degrees", 加热器 "heater". The object is the thing being warmed. It is the technical word and the word on microwave and cooking instructions. 加 "add" + 热 "heat".
column6: Bǎ niúnǎi jiārè hòu zài hē.
column7: Heat the milk before you drink it.
column9: To heat something up: 加熱食物 "heat food", 加熱到一百度 "heat to 100 degrees", 加熱器 "heater". The object is the thing being warmed. It is the technical word and the word on microwave and cooking instructions. 加 "add" + 熱 "heat".

column3: Prosperous and thriving, of an economy, a market, a culture or a city: 经济繁荣 "a prosperous economy", 繁荣昌盛 "prosperous and flourishing". It can also be a verb, "to make prosper": 繁荣市场. 繁 is "numerous" and 荣 is "flourishing", a written, positive word.
column4: 这个城市的经济非常繁荣。
column5: 這個城市的經濟非常繁榮。
column6: Zhège chéngshì de jīngjì fēicháng fánróng.
column7: This city's economy is very prosperous.
column9: Prosperous and thriving, of an economy, a market, a culture or a city: 經濟繁榮 "a prosperous economy", 繁榮昌盛 "prosperous and flourishing". It can also be a verb, "to make prosper": 繁榮市場. 繁 is "numerous" and 榮 is "flourishing", a written, positive word.

column3: To restore or to return to a former state: 恢复健康 "recover one's health", 恢复正常 "return to normal", 恢复联系 "reestablish contact". The thing restored is the object, and it can also be intransitive. 恢 is "restore" and 复 is "return", both reversing a loss.
column4: 经过休息，他的体力慢慢恢复了。
column5: 經過休息，他的體力慢慢恢復了。
column6: Jīngguò xiūxi, tā de tǐlì mànmàn huīfù le.
column7: After rest, his strength slowly came back.
column9: To restore or to return to a former state: 恢復健康 "recover one's health", 恢復正常 "return to normal", 恢復聯繫 "reestablish contact". The thing restored is the object, and it can also be intransitive. 恢 is "restore" and 復 is "return", both reversing a loss.

column3: To get rid of something unwanted, mostly something abstract: 消除误会 "clear up a misunderstanding", 消除疲劳 "relieve fatigue", 消除疑虑 "dispel doubts". 消 "disappear" + 除 "remove". With the object after it, the result is that the thing no longer exists.
column4: 这次谈话消除了我们之间的误会。
column5: 這次談話消除了我們之間的誤會。
column6: Zhè cì tánhuà xiāochú le wǒmen zhījiān de wùhuì.
column7: This talk cleared up the misunderstanding between us.
column9: To get rid of something unwanted, mostly something abstract: 消除誤會 "clear up a misunderstanding", 消除疲勞 "relieve fatigue", 消除疑慮 "dispel doubts". 消 "disappear" + 除 "remove". With the object after it, the result is that the thing no longer exists.

column3: To lift, cancel or end something that restricts, such as a contract, a ban, an alert or a relationship: 解除合同 "terminate a contract", 解除警报 "sound the all-clear", 解除误会. It is formal. 解 "untie" + 除 "remove".
column4: 公司解除了和他的合同。
column5: 公司解除了和他的合同。
column6: Gōngsī jiěchú le hé tā de hétong.
column7: The company terminated its contract with him.
column9: To lift, cancel or end something that restricts, such as a contract, a ban, an alert or a relationship: 解除合同 "terminate a contract", 解除警報 "sound the all-clear", 解除誤會. It is formal. 解 "untie" + 除 "remove".

column3: To rule out or remove something that stands in the way: 排除困难 "overcome difficulties", 排除可能性 "rule out the possibility", 排除障碍 "clear obstacles". The object is a difficulty or a possibility rather than a person. 排 "push away" + 除 "remove".
column4: 警方没有排除任何可能。
column5: 警方沒有排除任何可能。
column6: Jǐngfāng méiyǒu páichú rènhé kěnéng.
column7: The police have not ruled out any possibility.
column9: To rule out or remove something that stands in the way: 排除困難 "overcome difficulties", 排除可能性 "rule out the possibility", 排除障礙 "clear obstacles". The object is a difficulty or a possibility rather than a person. 排 "push away" + 除 "remove".

column3: To tear down a building or a structure, or to remove a device: 拆除旧楼 "demolish an old building", 拆除炸弹 "defuse a bomb". It is about taking apart something that was built or installed. 拆 "take apart" + 除 "remove".
column4: 这座旧楼下个月就要拆除了。
column5: 這座舊樓下個月就要拆除了。
column6: Zhè zuò jiù lóu xià ge yuè jiù yào chāichú le.
column7: This old building will be torn down next month.
column9: To tear down a building or a structure, or to remove a device: 拆除舊樓 "demolish an old building", 拆除炸彈 "defuse a bomb". It is about taking apart something that was built or installed. 拆 "take apart" + 除 "remove".

column3: To break off something that was going on, so that it stops, at least for a while: 通话中断 "the call was cut off", 中断学业 "interrupt one's studies", 供电中断 "a power outage". 中 "in the middle" + 断 "break", so the stop happens partway through.
column6: Diànhuà tūrán zhōngduàn le.
column7: The call was suddenly cut off.
column9: To break off something that was going on, so that it stops, at least for a while: 通話中斷 "the call was cut off", 中斷學業 "interrupt one's studies", 供電中斷 "a power outage". 中 "in the middle" + 斷 "break", so the stop happens partway through.

column3: To bring to an end, formally, often for contracts, talks, a project or a procedure: 终止合同 "terminate a contract", 终止比赛, 终止谈判. It is the formal word for stopping that is final, unlike 暂停. 终 "end" + 止 "stop".
column6: Shuāngfāng tóngyì zhōngzhǐ hézuò.
column7: Both sides agreed to end the cooperation.
column9: To bring to an end, formally, often for contracts, talks, a project or a procedure: 終止合同 "terminate a contract", 終止比賽, 終止談判. It is the formal word for stopping that is final, unlike 暫停. 終 "end" + 止 "stop".

column3: To give up something, such as a plan, a right, a chance or an attempt: 放弃机会 "pass up a chance", 不要放弃 "don't give up", 放弃治疗. The object is what is given up. 放 "let go" + 弃 "abandon".
column4: 不管多难，我都不会放弃。
column5: 不管多難，我都不會放棄。
column6: Bùguǎn duō nán, wǒ dōu bù huì fàngqì.
column7: No matter how hard it is, I will not give up.
column9: To give up something, such as a plan, a right, a chance or an attempt: 放棄機會 "pass up a chance", 不要放棄 "don't give up", 放棄治療. The object is what is given up. 放 "let go" + 棄 "abandon".

column3: To avoid something or someone on purpose, not to face it: 回避问题 "dodge a question", 回避矛盾 "avoid conflict", 不要回避. It also means to step aside for a conflict of interest (a judge who recuses himself). 回 "turn back" + 避 "avoid".
column6: Tā zǒngshì huíbì zhège wèntí.
column7: He always avoids this question.
column9: To avoid something or someone on purpose, not to face it: 回避問題 "dodge a question", 回避矛盾 "avoid conflict", 不要回避. It also means to step aside for a conflict of interest (a judge who recuses himself). 回 "turn back" + 避 "avoid".

column3: To collect something back for reuse or return: 回收垃圾 "collect waste for recycling", 回收旧手机, 资源回收 "recycling". It can also mean to recover a cost or a product: 回收成本. 回 "back" + 收 "collect".
column4: 这些旧衣服可以回收再利用。
column5: 這些舊衣服可以回收再利用。
column6: Zhèxiē jiù yīfu kěyǐ huíshōu zài lìyòng.
column7: These old clothes can be collected and reused.
column9: To collect something back for reuse or return: 回收垃圾 "collect waste for recycling", 回收舊手機, 資源回收 "recycling". It can also mean to recover a cost or a product: 回收成本. 回 "back" + 收 "collect".

column3: To clear out or sort through something to get rid of what is not needed: 清理房间 "clean up a room", 清理垃圾, 清理账目 "settle accounts". It stresses a thorough sort and removal. 清 "clear" + 理 "put in order".
column4: 周末我要清理一下书房。
column5: 週末我要清理一下書房。
column6: Zhōumò wǒ yào qīnglǐ yīxià shūfáng.
column7: I will tidy up the study this weekend.
column9: To clear out or sort through something to get rid of what is not needed: 清理房間 "clean up a room", 清理垃圾, 清理帳目 "settle accounts". It stresses a thorough sort and removal. 清 "clear" + 理 "put in order".

column3: To tidy or put things in order, to pack, and also to fix or punish someone: 收拾房间 "tidy the room", 收拾行李 "pack luggage", 看我怎么收拾你 "just watch how I'll deal with you". The second syllable is neutral. 收 "gather" + 拾 "pick up".
column4: 吃完饭后，我帮妈妈收拾桌子。
column5: 吃完飯後，我幫媽媽收拾桌子。
column6: Chī wán fàn hòu, wǒ bāng māma shōushi zhuōzi.
column7: After the meal, I helped Mom clear the table.
column9: To tidy or put things in order, to pack, and also to fix or punish someone: 收拾房間 "tidy the room", 收拾行李 "pack luggage", 看我怎麼收拾你 "just watch how I'll deal with you". The second syllable is neutral. 收 "gather" + 拾 "pick up".

column3: To pause or suspend something for the time being: 暂停营业 "closed for the time being", 暂停比赛 "pause the match", and the pause button on a player. 暂 means "temporary", which marks the stop as one that will end. The opposite idea of a final stop is 终止.
column6: Yīnwèi xià yǔ, bǐsài zàntíng le.
column7: The match was suspended because of the rain.
column9: To pause or suspend something for the time being: 暫停營業 "closed for the time being", 暫停比賽 "pause the match", and the pause button on a player. 暫 means "temporary", which marks the stop as one that will end. The opposite idea of a final stop is 終止.

column3: The end of a route or a race, where one finishes: 到达终点 "reach the finish line", 终点站 "terminal station", 终点线. The opposite is 起点. It is also used for the end of a process or journey in a general sense. 终 "end" + 点 "point".
column4: 他第一个冲过了终点线。
column5: 他第一個衝過了終點線。
column6: Tā dì-yī ge chōngguò le zhōngdiǎn xiàn.
column7: He was the first to dash across the finish line.
column9: The end of a route or a race, where one finishes: 到達終點 "reach the finish line", 終點站 "terminal station", 終點線. The opposite is 起點. It is also used for the end of a process or journey in a general sense. 終 "end" + 點 "point".

column3: To lighten or reduce a burden, pain, pressure or punishment: 减轻负担 "lighten the burden", 减轻压力, 减轻痛苦. It is for things felt as heavy, and the object is that weight. 减 "reduce" + 轻 "light".
column6: Zhè zhǒng yào kěyǐ jiǎnqīng téngtòng.
column7: This medicine can ease the pain.
column9: To lighten or reduce a burden, pain, pressure or punishment: 減輕負擔 "lighten the burden", 減輕壓力, 減輕痛苦. It is for things felt as heavy, and the object is that weight. 減 "reduce" + 輕 "light".

column3: To wait for someone or something, more formal and polite than 等: 等候通知 "wait for notice", 在门口等候, 恭候 is higher still. It is common on signs and in service talk, as in 请在这里等候. 等 "wait" + 候 "await".
column4: 请在大厅等候，医生马上就来。
column5: 請在大廳等候，醫生馬上就來。
column6: Qǐng zài dàtīng děnghòu, yīshēng mǎshàng jiù lái.
column7: Please wait in the hall; the doctor will be right here.
column9: To wait for someone or something, more formal and polite than 等: 等候通知 "wait for notice", 在門口等候, 恭候 is higher still. It is common on signs and in service talk, as in 請在這裡等候. 等 "wait" + 候 "await".

column3: To stay or remain in a place, a spoken sense: 待在家里 "stay at home", 待一会儿 "stay for a while", 待不下去 "can't stand staying". It is pronounced dai1 in this sense, and dai4 in 对待 "treat" and 招待 "entertain". It is a spoken word and takes a place word afterwards.
column4: 周末我想待在家里休息。
column5: 週末我想待在家裡休息。
column6: Zhōumò wǒ xiǎng dāi zài jiālǐ xiūxi.
column7: I want to stay at home and rest this weekend.
column9: To stay or remain in a place, a spoken sense: 待在家裡 "stay at home", 待一會兒 "stay for a while", 待不下去 "can't stand staying". It is pronounced dai1 in this sense, and dai4 in 對待 "treat" and 招待 "entertain". It is a spoken word and takes a place word afterwards.

column3: Blank, stunned or slow: 发呆 "stare blankly", 吓呆了 "stunned with fear", 呆呆地 "in a daze". It describes a face or person without reaction, and in speech it is also a variant of 待 "to stay" (呆在家里). The character is 口 over 木, a plain shape that is a good one to learn as a unit.
column4: 听到这个消息，他整个人都呆了。
column5: 聽到這個消息，他整個人都呆了。
column6: Tīngdào zhège xiāoxi, tā zhěng ge rén dōu dāi le.
column7: On hearing the news, he was struck dumb.
column9: Blank, stunned or slow: 發呆 "stare blankly", 嚇呆了 "stunned with fear", 呆呆地 "in a daze". It describes a face or person without reaction, and in speech it is also a variant of 待 "to stay" (呆在家裡). The character is 口 over 木, a plain shape that is a good one to learn as a unit.

column3: To stay in a place for a time, not long and not permanently, as on a trip or in transit: 停留三天 "stay three days", 在北京停留. It can also mean to remain at a stage: 停留在原地. 停 "stop" + 留 "stay".
column4: 我们在上海停留了三天。
column5: 我們在上海停留了三天。
column6: Wǒmen zài Shànghǎi tíngliú le sān tiān.
column7: We stayed in Shanghai for three days.
column9: To stay in a place for a time, not long and not permanently, as on a trip or in transit: 停留三天 "stay three days", 在北京停留. It can also mean to remain at a stage: 停留在原地. 停 "stop" + 留 "stay".

column3: Late, delayed, or slow: 迟到 "arrive late", 迟早 "sooner or later", 不迟 "not late", 推迟 "postpone". On its own it is mostly in compounds, but 来迟了 "came late" is possible. The 辶 shows movement, fitting something that is slow to arrive.
column6: Duìbuqǐ, wǒ lái chí le.
column7: Sorry, I'm late.
column9: Late, delayed, or slow: 遲到 "arrive late", 遲早 "sooner or later", 不遲 "not late", 推遲 "postpone". On its own it is mostly in compounds, but 來遲了 "came late" is possible. The 辶 shows movement, fitting something that is slow to arrive.

column3: The arrival of something, often a season, a time or an event, in a written style: 春天的到来 "the arrival of spring", 迎接新年的到来, and also a verb: 假期即将到来. It is not used for people arriving. 到 "arrive" + 来 "come".
column4: 春天的到来让大家心情很好。
column5: 春天的到來讓大家心情很好。
column6: Chūntiān de dàolái ràng dàjiā xīnqíng hěn hǎo.
column7: The arrival of spring puts everyone in a good mood.
column9: The arrival of something, often a season, a time or an event, in a written style: 春天的到來 "the arrival of spring", 迎接新年的到來, and also a verb: 假期即將到來. It is not used for people arriving. 到 "arrive" + 來 "come".

column3: The right moment for an action, an opportunity as a matter of timing: 把握时机 "seize the moment", 时机成熟 "the time is ripe", 等待时机. It is not just "time"; it implies the point at which something will work. 时 "time" + 机 "chance".
column4: 现在还不是出手的时机。
column5: 現在還不是出手的時機。
column6: Xiànzài hái bù shì chūshǒu de shíjī.
column7: Now is not yet the time to act.
column9: The right moment for an action, an opportunity as a matter of timing: 把握時機 "seize the moment", 時機成熟 "the time is ripe", 等待時機. It is not just "time"; it implies the point at which something will work. 時 "time" + 機 "chance".

column3: Current affairs, the news of the day: 关心时事 "follow current affairs", 时事新闻, 时事评论 "commentary on current events". It is the topic of newspapers and talk shows. 时 "time" + 事 "matter".
column4: 他每天看报纸，很关心时事。
column5: 他每天看報紙，很關心時事。
column6: Tā měi tiān kàn bàozhǐ, hěn guānxīn shíshì.
column7: He reads the paper every day and follows current affairs closely.
column9: Current affairs, the news of the day: 關心時事 "follow current affairs", 時事新聞, 時事評論 "commentary on current events". It is the topic of newspapers and talk shows. 時 "time" + 事 "matter".

column3: A major matter, an important event: 国家大事 "affairs of state", 终身大事 "the big event of a lifetime, marriage", 大事不好 "something terrible has happened". The opposite is 小事. 大事 is also used with 化小 in the saying 大事化小，小事化了. Treat it as two words in the sentence, as 大 modifies 事.
column4: 结婚是人生中的一件大事。
column5: 結婚是人生中的一件大事。
column6: Jiéhūn shì rénshēng zhōng de yī jiàn dàshì.
column7: Getting married is a major event in life.
column9: A major matter, an important event: 國家大事 "affairs of state", 終身大事 "the big event of a lifetime, marriage", 大事不好 "something terrible has happened". The opposite is 小事. 大事 is also used with 化小 in the saying 大事化小，小事化了. Treat it as two words in the sentence, as 大 modifies 事.

column3: To prepare or get ready, either as a verb or as a modifier: 预备好了吗 "are you ready", 预备考试, 预备班. It is a bit more formal than 准备 and often for preparing in advance. The command 预备，开始！ is "ready, begin!". 预 "in advance" + 备 "prepare".
column4: 孩子们正在预备明天的考试。
column5: 孩子們正在預備明天的考試。
column6: Háizimen zhèngzài yùbèi míngtiān de kǎoshì.
column7: The children are getting ready for tomorrow's exam.
column9: To prepare or get ready, either as a verb or as a modifier: 預備好了嗎 "are you ready", 預備考試, 預備班. It is a bit more formal than 準備 and often for preparing in advance. The command 預備，開始！ is "ready, begin!". 預 "in advance" + 備 "prepare".

column3: In a row, one after another: 接连几天 "for several days in a row", 接连三次, 接连发生. It comes before the verb as an adverb and is used for events of the same kind that follow each other quickly. 接 "join" + 连 "link".
column4: 这个月接连下了好几场大雨。
column5: 這個月接連下了好幾場大雨。
column6: Zhège yuè jiēlián xià le hǎo jǐ chǎng dàyǔ.
column7: It has rained heavily several times in a row this month.
column9: In a row, one after another: 接連幾天 "for several days in a row", 接連三次, 接連發生. It comes before the verb as an adverb and is used for events of the same kind that follow each other quickly. 接 "join" + 連 "link".

column3: Frequent, often, and used as an adjective or adverb: 频繁出现 "appear frequently", 联系频繁, 频繁地使用. It sounds written and suits formal writing and reports. For daily speech 经常 is more common. 频 means "frequent" and 繁 "numerous".
column6: Zuìjìn tā chūchāi hěn pínfán.
column7: He has been on business trips very often lately.
column9: Frequent, often, and used as an adjective or adverb: 頻繁出現 "appear frequently", 聯繫頻繁, 頻繁地使用. It sounds written and suits formal writing and reports. For daily speech 經常 is more common. 頻 means "frequent" and 繁 "numerous".

column3: To mention or bring up a topic: 提起这件事 "mention this matter", 别提起 "don't bring it up". It also means to lift up or arouse: 提起精神 "pick up one's spirits", and to start a lawsuit: 提起诉讼. 提 "carry, raise" + 起 "up".
column4: 她从来不愿提起过去的事。
column5: 她從來不願提起過去的事。
column6: Tā cónglái bù yuàn tíqǐ guòqù de shì.
column7: She has never been willing to talk about the past.
column9: To mention or bring up a topic: 提起這件事 "mention this matter", 別提起 "don't bring it up". It also means to lift up or arouse: 提起精神 "pick up one's spirits", and to start a lawsuit: 提起訴訟. 提 "carry, raise" + 起 "up".

column3: To encourage someone: 鼓励孩子 "encourage a child", 受到鼓励 "feel encouraged", and also a noun, "encouragement". The pattern is 鼓励 + person + verb: 鼓励他继续努力. 鼓 is a drum, so the word is like beating the drum to spur someone on, and 励 means "urge".
column4: 老师鼓励我们多说汉语。
column5: 老師鼓勵我們多說漢語。
column6: Lǎoshī gǔlì wǒmen duō shuō Hànyǔ.
column7: The teacher encourages us to speak more Chinese.
column9: To encourage someone: 鼓勵孩子 "encourage a child", 受到鼓勵 "feel encouraged", and also a noun, "encouragement". The pattern is 鼓勵 + person + verb: 鼓勵他繼續努力. 鼓 is a drum, so the word is like beating the drum to spur someone on, and 勵 means "urge".

column3: To mobilize people for a task or a campaign: 动员群众 "rally the masses", 总动员 "full mobilization", 动员大会. It also means to persuade someone to do something: 动员他参加. It has a political and organizational flavor. 动 "move" + 员 "member".
column4: 学校动员大家参加植树活动。
column5: 學校動員大家參加植樹活動。
column6: Xuéxiào dòngyuán dàjiā cānjiā zhíshù huódòng.
column7: The school mobilized everyone to take part in the tree planting.
column9: To mobilize people for a task or a campaign: 動員群眾 "rally the masses", 總動員 "full mobilization", 動員大會. It also means to persuade someone to do something: 動員他參加. It has a political and organizational flavor. 動 "move" + 員 "member".

column3: To refuse a request, invitation, offer or demand: 拒绝邀请 "decline an invitation", 被拒绝 "be rejected", 拒绝回答. It is clear and firm, stronger than the soft 谢绝 and less formal than 驳回. 拒 "resist" + 绝 "cut off".
column4: 他礼貌地拒绝了我们的邀请。
column5: 他禮貌地拒絕了我們的邀請。
column6: Tā lǐmào de jùjué le wǒmen de yāoqǐng.
column7: He politely declined our invitation.
column9: To refuse a request, invitation, offer or demand: 拒絕邀請 "decline an invitation", 被拒絕 "be rejected", 拒絕回答. It is clear and firm, stronger than the soft 謝絕 and less formal than 駁回. 拒 "resist" + 絕 "cut off".

column3: To blame or criticize someone openly for a fault: 指责别人 "criticize others", 受到指责 "come under criticism", 互相指责 "blame each other". It is stronger than 批评 and implies accusing. 指 "point at" + 责 "blame".
column4: 他不应该指责朋友的错误。
column5: 他不應該指責朋友的錯誤。
column6: Tā bù yīnggāi zhǐzé péngyou de cuòwù.
column7: He should not blame his friend for the mistake.
column9: To blame or criticize someone openly for a fault: 指責別人 "criticize others", 受到指責 "come under criticism", 互相指責 "blame each other". It is stronger than 批評 and implies accusing. 指 "point at" + 責 "blame".

column3: To force or compel someone to do something: 强迫他做 "force him to do it", 强迫症 "obsessive-compulsive disorder", 被强迫. It is read qiang3 here, not qiang2 "strong". 强 "force" + 迫 "press".
column4: 没有人可以强迫你做不喜欢的事。
column5: 沒有人可以強迫你做不喜歡的事。
column6: Méiyǒu rén kěyǐ qiǎngpò nǐ zuò bù xǐhuan de shì.
column7: No one can force you to do something you don't like.
column9: To force or compel someone to do something: 強迫他做 "force him to do it", 強迫症 "obsessive-compulsive disorder", 被強迫. It is read qiang3 here, not qiang2 "strong". 強 "force" + 迫 "press".

column3: To make things hard for someone, or to feel awkward: 别为难他 "don't make it hard for him", 感到为难 "feel in a bind", 很为难. Read wei2 here, not wei4. It can be a transitive verb with a person after it or a state of embarrassment. 为 "make, act" + 难 "hard".
column4: 你别为难他，他也是照规定办事。
column5: 你別為難他，他也是照規定辦事。
column6: Nǐ bié wéinán tā, tā yě shì zhào guīdìng bànshì.
column7: Don't make things hard for him; he is just following the rules.
column9: To make things hard for someone, or to feel awkward: 別為難他 "don't make it hard for him", 感到為難 "feel in a bind", 很為難. Read wei2 here, not wei4. It can be a transitive verb with a person after it or a state of embarrassment. 為 "make, act" + 難 "hard".

column3: To disturb or bother someone: 打扰一下 "excuse me for a moment", 不好意思打扰了 "sorry to bother you", 请勿打扰 "do not disturb". It is the polite formula for interrupting. 打 "do" + 扰 "disturb".
column6: Bù hǎoyìsi, dǎrǎo nǐ yīxià.
column7: Sorry, may I bother you for a moment?
column9: To disturb or bother someone: 打擾一下 "excuse me for a moment", 不好意思打擾了 "sorry to bother you", 請勿打擾 "do not disturb". It is the polite formula for interrupting. 打 "do" + 擾 "disturb".

column3: To control or dominate, or to allocate and arrange: 支配时间 "manage one's time", 自由支配 "free to dispose of", 被支配. The word suggests that someone has the right to decide how something is used. 支 "branch out, pay out" + 配 "match, allot".
column4: 他可以自由支配自己的时间。
column5: 他可以自由支配自己的時間。
column6: Tā kěyǐ zìyóu zhīpèi zìjǐ de shíjiān.
column7: He can manage his own time freely.
column9: To control or dominate, or to allocate and arrange: 支配時間 "manage one's time", 自由支配 "free to dispose of", 被支配. The word suggests that someone has the right to decide how something is used. 支 "branch out, pay out" + 配 "match, allot".

column3: To urge someone to do or stop doing something, by talking: 劝他别去 "advise him not to go", 劝架 "try to stop a quarrel", 劝告 "advice". It is gentler than 强迫 and often means talking someone out of something. The 力 on the right is effort.
column6: Péngyou quàn wǒ zǎodiǎn xiūxi.
column7: My friend urged me to get to bed early.
column9: To urge someone to do or stop doing something, by talking: 勸他別去 "advise him not to go", 勸架 "try to stop a quarrel", 勸告 "advice". It is gentler than 強迫 and often means talking someone out of something. The 力 on the right is effort.

column3: To call on people to act, with the authority of a leader or an organization: 号召大家 "call on everyone", 响应号召 "answer the call", 发出号召. It is formal and used in public speech. 号 "call" + 召 "summon".
column4: 学校号召同学们节约用水。
column5: 學校號召同學們節約用水。
column6: Xuéxiào hàozhào tóngxuémen jiéyuē yòngshuǐ.
column7: The school called on the students to save water.
column9: To call on people to act, with the authority of a leader or an organization: 號召大家 "call on everyone", 響應號召 "answer the call", 發出號召. It is formal and used in public speech. 號 "call" + 召 "summon".

column3: To order someone to do something, and the order itself: 下命令 "give an order", 服从命令 "obey an order", 命令他离开 "order him to leave". It comes from a superior to a subordinate. 命 "command" + 令 "order".
column4: 长官命令士兵立刻出发。
column5: 長官命令士兵立刻出發。
column6: Zhǎngguān mìnglìng shìbīng lìkè chūfā.
column7: The officer ordered the soldiers to set out at once.
column9: To order someone to do something, and the order itself: 下命令 "give an order", 服從命令 "obey an order", 命令他離開 "order him to leave". It comes from a superior to a subordinate. 命 "command" + 令 "order".

column3: To scold, swear at or curse someone: 骂人 "swear at people", 挨骂 "get scolded", 被老板骂了. The two 口 on top are mouths, a good picture for noisy scolding. 骂 is also found in 骂街 and 谩骂, though 骂人 is the usual use.
column4: 他因为迟到被老师骂了。
column5: 他因為遲到被老師罵了。
column6: Tā yīnwèi chídào bèi lǎoshī mà le.
column7: He was scolded by the teacher for being late.
column9: To scold, swear at or curse someone: 罵人 "swear at people", 挨罵 "get scolded", 被老板罵了. The two 口 on top are mouths, a good picture for noisy scolding. 罵 is also found in 罵街 and 謾罵, though 罵人 is the usual use.

column3: To possess or own, a formal word usually about big or valuable things: 拥有土地 "own land", 拥有财富, 拥有丰富的经验 "have rich experience". It is not used for small things such as a pen. 拥 "hold" + 有 "have".
column4: 这家公司拥有三千名员工。
column5: 這家公司擁有三千名員工。
column6: Zhè jiā gōngsī yōngyǒu sānqiān míng yuángōng.
column7: This company has three thousand employees.
column9: To possess or own, a formal word usually about big or valuable things: 擁有土地 "own land", 擁有財富, 擁有豐富的經驗 "have rich experience". It is not used for small things such as a pen. 擁 "hold" + 有 "have".

column3: To have or possess, used with an abstract noun and a written feel: 有着悠久的历史 "have a long history", 有着重要的意义, 有着不同的看法. 着 is the verbal particle, neutral, and it makes the phrase sound slightly literary. It is rarely used with ordinary concrete things.
column4: 这座城市有着两千年的历史。
column5: 這座城市有著兩千年的歷史。
column6: Zhè zuò chéngshì yǒuzhe liǎng qiān nián de lìshǐ.
column7: This city has a history of two thousand years.
column9: To have or possess, used with an abstract noun and a written feel: 有著悠久的歷史 "have a long history", 有著重要的意義, 有著不同的看法. 著 is the verbal particle, neutral, and it makes the phrase sound slightly literary. It is rarely used with ordinary concrete things.

column3: To carry or have a certain quality, feeling or element: 带有感情 "carry feeling", 带有地方色彩 "have a local flavor", 带有危险性. The thing it has is a trait or an element, not an object. 带 "bring, carry" + 有 "have".
column4: 他的话带有明显的讽刺意味。
column5: 他的話帶有明顯的諷刺意味。
column6: Tā de huà dàiyǒu míngxiǎn de fěngcì yìwèi.
column7: His words carry an obvious note of sarcasm.
column9: To carry or have a certain quality, feeling or element: 帶有感情 "carry feeling", 帶有地方色彩 "have a local flavor", 帶有危險性. The thing it has is a trait or an element, not an object. 帶 "bring, carry" + 有 "have".

column3: To be in a certain situation or stage: 处在困难时期 "be in a difficult period", 处在发展阶段 "be at the stage of development". It is followed by an abstract place, such as a state or period. 处 is read chu3 here, "be located", and 在 "at".
column4: 这个行业正处在快速发展的阶段。
column5: 這個行業正處在快速發展的階段。
column6: Zhège hángyè zhèng chǔzài kuàisù fāzhǎn de jiēduàn.
column7: This industry is in a stage of rapid development.
column9: To be in a certain situation or stage: 處在困難時期 "be in a difficult period", 處在發展階段 "be at the stage of development". It is followed by an abstract place, such as a state or period. 處 is read chu3 here, "be located", and 在 "at".

column3: From within it, from among them: 从中学到 "learn from it", 从中选择 "choose from among them", 从中获得. 中 refers back to something just mentioned. It comes before a verb, and the thing it points to has to be clear from before.
column4: 我们可以从中学到很多经验。
column5: 我們可以從中學到很多經驗。
column6: Wǒmen kěyǐ cóngzhōng xuédào hěn duō jīngyàn.
column7: We can learn a lot of lessons from it.
column9: From within it, from among them: 從中學到 "learn from it", 從中選擇 "choose from among them", 從中獲得. 中 refers back to something just mentioned. It comes before a verb, and the thing it points to has to be clear from before.

column3: To mean or to imply, of a result or consequence, not of a word's meaning: 这意味着… "this means…", 意味着成功 "mean success". It links a fact to what follows from it, which makes it good for explanations. 意味 "meaning, flavor" + 着.
column4: 学习外语意味着打开一个新世界。
column5: 學習外語意味著打開一個新世界。
column6: Xuéxí wàiyǔ yìwèizhe dǎkāi yī ge xīn shìjiè.
column7: Learning a foreign language means opening up a new world.
column9: To mean or to imply, of a result or consequence, not of a word's meaning: 這意味著… "this means…", 意味著成功 "mean success". It links a fact to what follows from it, which makes it good for explanations. 意味 "meaning, flavor" + 著.

column3: An exception, and "to be an exception": 没有例外 "without exception", 也不例外 "is no exception", 例外情况. The usual pattern is 也不例外 after a statement that applies to others as well. 例 "example, rule" + 外 "outside".
column4: 每个人都要遵守规定，我也不例外。
column5: 每個人都要遵守規定，我也不例外。
column6: Měi ge rén dōu yào zūnshǒu guīdìng, wǒ yě bù lìwài.
column7: Everyone has to follow the rules, and I am no exception.
column9: An exception, and "to be an exception": 沒有例外 "without exception", 也不例外 "is no exception", 例外情況. The usual pattern is 也不例外 after a statement that applies to others as well. 例 "example, rule" + 外 "outside".

column3: An analogy or example, and "for instance": 打个比方 "to take an analogy", 比方说 "let's say, for example". The second syllable is neutral. In speech 比方说 is the way to introduce an example, and 打比方 means to give an illustration.
column4: 你打个比方，我就明白了。
column5: 你打個比方，我就明白了。
column6: Nǐ dǎ ge bǐfang, wǒ jiù míngbai le.
column7: Give me an analogy and I will understand.
column9: An analogy or example, and "for instance": 打個比方 "to take an analogy", 比方說 "let's say, for example". The second syllable is neutral. In speech 比方說 is the way to introduce an example, and 打比方 means to give an illustration.

column3: To be left over, or what remains: 剩下的钱 "the remaining money", 只剩下三个 "only three are left", 剩下的时间. 剩 alone does the same, but 剩下 is the natural form with 的 in front of a noun. It is a verb, and also takes an object.
column6: Zhège yuè zhǐ shèngxià jǐ tiān le.
column7: Only a few days are left in this month.
column9: To be left over, or what remains: 剩下的錢 "the remaining money", 只剩下三個 "only three are left", 剩下的時間. 剩 alone does the same, but 剩下 is the natural form with 的 in front of a noun. It is a verb, and also takes an object.

column3: To own or hold, and to account for a share: 占有市场 "hold a share of the market", 占有率 "market share", 占有一席之地 "have a place". It is more formal than 有, and for resources, land or a percentage. Read zhan4. 占 and 有 both indicate holding.
column4: 这家公司占有百分之三十的市场。
column5: 這家公司佔有百分之三十的市場。
column6: Zhè jiā gōngsī zhànyǒu bǎi fēn zhī sānshí de shìchǎng.
column7: This company holds thirty percent of the market.
column9: To own or hold, and to account for a share: 佔有市場 "hold a share of the market", 佔有率 "market share", 佔有一席之地 "have a place". It is more formal than 有, and for resources, land or a percentage. Read zhan4. 佔 and 有 both indicate holding.

column3: To correspond to, or corresponding: 一一对应 "one-to-one correspondence", 对应的字 "the corresponding character". It is used when two things match in a system, such as a word and its translation. 对 "face, pair" + 应 "answer"; here 应 is read ying4.
column4: 每个汉字都有对应的拼音。
column5: 每個漢字都有對應的拼音。
column6: Měi ge Hànzì dōu yǒu duìyìng de pīnyīn.
column7: Every Chinese character has a corresponding pinyin.
column9: To correspond to, or corresponding: 一一對應 "one-to-one correspondence", 對應的字 "the corresponding character". It is used when two things match in a system, such as a word and its translation. 對 "face, pair" + 應 "answer"; here 應 is read ying4.

column3: Corresponding or appropriate, before a noun or a verb: 采取相应措施 "take appropriate measures", 相应的变化 "a corresponding change". It does not stand as a main verb in everyday talk. 相 "mutually" + 应 "respond", read ying4.
column4: 价格上涨，销量也相应下降。
column5: 價格上漲，銷量也相應下降。
column6: Jiàgé shàngzhǎng, xiāoliàng yě xiāngyìng xiàjiàng.
column7: Prices went up, and sales fell accordingly.
column9: Corresponding or appropriate, before a noun or a verb: 採取相應措施 "take appropriate measures", 相應的變化 "a corresponding change". It does not stand as a main verb in everyday talk. 相 "mutually" + 應 "respond", read ying4.

column3: Equal, in number, size or value: 两边相等 "both sides are equal", 数量相等, 大小相等. It is a stative adjective and does not take a degree word. 相 "mutually" + 等 "equal", so it describes two things matching each other.
column6: Zhè liǎng ge shù xiāngděng.
column7: These two numbers are equal.
column9: Equal, in number, size or value: 兩邊相等 "both sides are equal", 數量相等, 大小相等. It is a stative adjective and does not take a degree word. 相 "mutually" + 等 "equal", so it describes two things matching each other.

column3: Each other, both sides: 彼此了解 "understand each other", 彼此彼此 "the same to you", 彼此之间 "between each other". It works as a pronoun like 互相 but sits as the subject or object. 彼 is "that" and 此 "this", so the word means "that and this".
column6: Wǒmen bǐcǐ dōu hěn liǎojiě.
column7: We understand each other well.
column9: Each other, both sides: 彼此了解 "understand each other", 彼此彼此 "the same to you", 彼此之間 "between each other". It works as a pronoun like 互相 but sits as the subject or object. 彼 is "that" and 此 "this", so the word means "that and this".

column3: To be left over: 剩饭 "leftover food", 剩下 "remain", 只剩一个 "only one left". Written alone it is common with a number: 还剩两天. The leftover is the subject or the object: 菜剩了很多 "a lot of food is left".
column6: Pánzi lǐ hái shèng yī kuài dàngāo.
column7: One piece of cake is left on the plate.
column9: To be left over: 剩飯 "leftover food", 剩下 "remain", 只剩一個 "only one left". Written alone it is common with a number: 還剩兩天. The leftover is the subject or the object: 菜剩了很多 "a lot of food is left".

column3: Must, certainly, necessarily: 必须 "must", 必然 "inevitable", 必要 "necessary", and in the written 必定 "certainly". On its own it appears in formal and set phrases such as 事必躬亲, 未必 "not necessarily", and 不必 "need not". Learn it as the first character of those words.
column6: Zhè jiàn shì nǐ bùbì dānxīn.
column7: You don't need to worry about this.
column9: Must, certainly, necessarily: 必須 "must", 必然 "inevitable", 必要 "necessary", and in the written 必定 "certainly". On its own it appears in formal and set phrases such as 事必躬親, 未必 "not necessarily", and 不必 "need not". Learn it as the first character of those words.

column3: Essential, indispensable, something that cannot be done without: 生活必需品 "daily necessities", 必需的条件. It is often confused with 必须 "must"; 必需 is about need and is used before a noun, while 必须 is an adverb before a verb. 需 means "need".
column6: Shuǐ shì shēnghuó bìxū de.
column7: Water is essential for life.
column9: Essential, indispensable, something that cannot be done without: 生活必需品 "daily necessities", 必需的條件. It is often confused with 必須 "must"; 必需 is about need and is used before a noun, while 必須 is an adverb before a verb. 需 means "need".

column3: Cannot not, which means must: 不能不去 "must go", 不能不承认 "have to admit". The double negative is a bit stronger than 必须 and implies that there is no choice, because of circumstance. 不能 "cannot" + 不 "not".
column4: 这次会议我们不能不去。
column5: 這次會議我們不能不去。
column6: Zhè cì huìyì wǒmen bùnéngbù qù.
column7: We have to go to this meeting.
column9: Cannot not, which means must: 不能不去 "must go", 不能不承認 "have to admit". The double negative is a bit stronger than 必須 and implies that there is no choice, because of circumstance. 不能 "cannot" + 不 "not".

column3: Not to need, or there is no need: 用不着担心 "no need to worry", 用不着你管 "it's none of your business". The 不 in the middle is a neutral 不, and the pattern V + 不着 means "not able to". In 用不着 the 着 is zhao2, not the particle zhe5. The opposite is 用得着.
column4: 这点小事用不着麻烦别人。
column5: 這點小事用不著麻煩別人。
column6: Zhè diǎn xiǎo shì yòngbuzháo máfan biéren.
column7: There is no need to trouble others for such a small matter.
column9: Not to need, or there is no need: 用不著擔心 "no need to worry", 用不著你管 "it's none of your business". The 不 in the middle is a neutral 不, and the pattern V + 不著 means "not able to". In 用不著 the 著 is zhao2, not the particle zhe5. The opposite is 用得著.

column3: Cannot help doing something, cannot hold back: 忍不住笑了 "couldn't help laughing", 忍不住哭 "can't help crying". It comes before the verb and means the action happens against one's will. The pattern V + 不住 means "cannot hold". The opposite is 忍得住.
column4: 听到这个笑话，大家都忍不住笑了。
column5: 聽到這個笑話，大家都忍不住笑了。
column6: Tīngdào zhège xiàohua, dàjiā dōu rěnbuzhù xiào le.
column7: Hearing the joke, everyone could not help laughing.
column9: Cannot help doing something, cannot hold back: 忍不住笑了 "couldn't help laughing", 忍不住哭 "can't help crying". It comes before the verb and means the action happens against one's will. The pattern V + 不住 means "cannot hold". The opposite is 忍得住.

column3: To be unwilling to part with or to use up, out of attachment: 舍不得你 "I hate to leave you", 舍不得花钱 "hate to spend money", 舍不得扔. Read the first syllable she3, "let go". The pattern V + 不得 here is "cannot bear to". The positive form is 舍得.
column4: 我舍不得扔掉这件旧毛衣。
column5: 我捨不得扔掉這件舊毛衣。
column6: Wǒ shěbude rēngdiào zhè jiàn jiù máoyī.
column7: I can't bear to throw away this old sweater.
column9: To be unwilling to part with or to use up, out of attachment: 捨不得你 "I hate to leave you", 捨不得花錢 "hate to spend money", 捨不得扔. Read the first syllable she3, "let go". The pattern V + 不得 here is "cannot bear to". The positive form is 捨得.

column3: To be willing to part with or spend something valuable: 舍得花钱 "willing to spend money", 舍得吃 "not stingy about food". It is usually used in questions and negatives, or in the sentence 你舍得吗？. It is the positive of 舍不得, and the 得 is neutral.
column4: 他舍得为孩子的教育花钱。
column5: 他捨得為孩子的教育花錢。
column6: Tā shěde wèi háizi de jiàoyù huā qián.
column7: He is willing to spend money on his child's education.
column9: To be willing to part with or spend something valuable: 捨得花錢 "willing to spend money", 捨得吃 "not stingy about food". It is usually used in questions and negatives, or in the sentence 你捨得嗎？. It is the positive of 捨不得, and the 得 is neutral.

column3: A polite reply to praise or kindness: "I don't deserve it, you flatter me". It literally means "I dare not accept". It is said in modest, polished talk, usually after a compliment, and is somewhat old-fashioned. 当 here is read dang1, "accept".
column4: 您过奖了，我真是不敢当。
column5: 您過獎了，我真是不敢當。
column6: Nín guòjiǎng le, wǒ zhēn shì bùgǎndāng.
column7: You flatter me, I really don't deserve it.
column9: A polite reply to praise or kindness: "I don't deserve it, you flatter me". It literally means "I dare not accept". It is said in modest, polished talk, usually after a compliment, and is somewhat old-fashioned. 當 here is read dang1, "accept".

column3: Terrible, serious, and as a complement "extremely": 不得了了 "it's a disaster", 高兴得不得了 "extremely happy", 疼得不得了. The pattern is adjective + 得 + 不得了, and it is spoken. 得了 is read de2liao3 in it.
column4: 他高兴得不得了，一直在笑。
column5: 他高興得不得了，一直在笑。
column6: Tā gāoxìng de bùdéliǎo, yīzhí zài xiào.
column7: He is so happy that he keeps laughing.
column9: Terrible, serious, and as a complement "extremely": 不得了了 "it's a disaster", 高興得不得了 "extremely happy", 疼得不得了. The pattern is adjective + 得 + 不得了, and it is spoken. 得了 is read de2liao3 in it.

column3: Enough! or "all right!", a spoken way to cut someone short or to agree to leave something: 得了，别说了 "that's enough, stop talking". Spoken, with a slightly annoyed or resigned tone. It is read de2le5, and 得了 as a verb phrase "can be done" is de2liao3.
column4: 得了，别说了，我已经知道了。
column5: 得了，別說了，我已經知道了。
column6: Déle, bié shuō le, wǒ yǐjīng zhīdào le.
column7: All right, stop talking, I already know.
column9: Enough! or "all right!", a spoken way to cut someone short or to agree to leave something: 得了，別說了 "that's enough, stop talking". Spoken, with a slightly annoyed or resigned tone. It is read de2le5, and 得了 as a verb phrase "can be done" is de2liao3.

column3: Finished, or "it's all over": 完了完了 "oh no, I'm doomed", 这下完了 "now we're in trouble". It is a spoken exclamation for bad news. Without a bad meaning, 完了 means "it is finished", as in 说完了. Note that the 了 is neutral.
column4: 糟了，我把钥匙忘在家里了，完了！
column5: 糟了，我把鑰匙忘在家裡了，完了！
column6: Zāo le, wǒ bǎ yàoshi wàng zài jiālǐ le, wánle!
column7: Oh no, I forgot my keys at home, I'm done for!
column9: Finished, or "it's all over": 完了完了 "oh no, I'm doomed", 這下完了 "now we're in trouble". It is a spoken exclamation for bad news. Without a bad meaning, 完了 means "it is finished", as in 說完了. Note that the 了 is neutral.

column3: To disregard or ignore, usually a danger or a cost: 不顾危险 "regardless of danger", 不顾一切 "at all costs", 不顾家人反对. It describes a bold or reckless choice. 顾 means "care about, look after", so the word is "not care about".
column4: 他不顾危险，跳进水里救人。
column5: 他不顧危險，跳進水裡救人。
column6: Tā bùgù wēixiǎn, tiàojìn shuǐ lǐ jiù rén.
column7: Disregarding the danger, he jumped into the water to save someone.
column9: To disregard or ignore, usually a danger or a cost: 不顧危險 "regardless of danger", 不顧一切 "at all costs", 不顧家人反對. It describes a bold or reckless choice. 顧 means "care about, look after", so the word is "not care about".

column3: Thus, thereby, as a result: it joins a second action to the first as its result or purpose, with the same subject. 采取措施，从而提高效率 "take measures and thereby raise efficiency". It is a written conjunction, rarely spoken.
column4: 他每天锻炼，从而保持了健康。
column5: 他每天鍛鍊，從而保持了健康。
column6: Tā měi tiān duànliàn, cóng'ér bǎochí le jiànkāng.
column7: He exercises every day and so stays healthy.
column9: Thus, thereby, as a result: it joins a second action to the first as its result or purpose, with the same subject. 採取措施，從而提高效率 "take measures and thereby raise efficiency". It is a written conjunction, rarely spoken.

column3: Therefore, and as a result: it states a result after a cause that has already been given. 他很努力，因而成绩很好. It is written, and the cause comes first, unlike 所以, which is spoken and often paired with 因为.
column4: 天气很冷，因而路上的人很少。
column5: 天氣很冷，因而路上的人很少。
column6: Tiānqì hěn lěng, yīn'ér lùshàng de rén hěn shǎo.
column7: It was very cold, so there were few people on the road.
column9: Therefore, and as a result: it states a result after a cause that has already been given. 他很努力，因而成績很好. It is written, and the cause comes first, unlike 所以, which is spoken and often paired with 因為.

column3: So that or in order to, introducing the purpose of the earlier clause: 早点出发，以便赶上火车 "set off early so as to catch the train". It starts a second clause and has a more formal ring than 为了. The purpose is stated after it.
column4: 请留下电话号码，以便我们联系你。
column5: 請留下電話號碼，以便我們聯繫你。
column6: Qǐng liúxià diànhuà hàomǎ, yǐbiàn wǒmen liánxì nǐ.
column7: Please leave a phone number so that we can contact you.
column9: So that or in order to, introducing the purpose of the earlier clause: 早點出發，以便趕上火車 "set off early so as to catch the train". It starts a second clause and has a more formal ring than 為了. The purpose is stated after it.

column3: From this, hence: it takes what was just said as the starting point for a conclusion. 由此可见 "from this it can be seen", 由此看来 "judging from this". It is formal and normally used at the start of a clause, in a text.
column4: 他每天练习，由此可见他很努力。
column5: 他每天練習，由此可見他很努力。
column6: Tā měi tiān liànxí, yóucǐ kějiàn tā hěn nǔlì.
column7: He practices every day, which shows he works hard.
column9: From this, hence: it takes what was just said as the starting point for a conclusion. 由此可見 "from this it can be seen", 由此看來 "judging from this". It is formal and normally used at the start of a clause, in a text.

column3: Like this, so, in this way: 如此重要 "so important", 如此而已 "that's all", 事实如此 "that's how it is". It is the written counterpart of 这样 and stands in for something just described. It can be a predicate on its own: 情况如此. 如 "like" + 此 "this".
column4: 他如此努力，一定会成功。
column5: 他如此努力，一定會成功。
column6: Tā rúcǐ nǔlì, yīdìng huì chénggōng.
column7: He works so hard that he is sure to succeed.
column9: Like this, so, in this way: 如此重要 "so important", 如此而已 "that's all", 事實如此 "that's how it is". It is the written counterpart of 這樣 and stands in for something just described. It can be a predicate on its own: 情況如此. 如 "like" + 此 "this".

column3: Like or just as, in a comparison: 如同朋友一样 "just like a friend", 如同做梦 "as if in a dream". It is a written equivalent of 像 and often has 一样 or 一般 at the end. 如 and 同 both mean "like".
column4: 她对我如同亲姐姐一样。
column5: 她對我如同親姐姐一樣。
column6: Tā duì wǒ rútóng qīn jiějie yīyàng.
column7: She treats me just like a real older sister.
column9: Like or just as, in a comparison: 如同朋友一樣 "just like a friend", 如同做夢 "as if in a dream". It is a written equivalent of 像 and often has 一樣 or 一般 at the end. 如 and 同 both mean "like".

column3: As follows, introducing a list or the text that comes next: 内容如下 "the contents are as follows", 具体如下, 办法如下. It sits at the end of a clause and a colon follows. It is a written, formal word for notices and reports.
column4: 会议时间和地点如下：周五下午三点，二楼会议室。
column5: 會議時間和地點如下：週五下午三點，二樓會議室。
column6: Huìyì shíjiān hé dìdiǎn rúxià: zhōuwǔ xiàwǔ sān diǎn, èr lóu huìyìshì.
column7: The time and place of the meeting are as follows: Friday at three p.m., conference room on the second floor.
column9: As follows, introducing a list or the text that comes next: 內容如下 "the contents are as follows", 具體如下, 辦法如下. It sits at the end of a clause and a colon follows. It is a written, formal word for notices and reports.

column3: Just as, introducing a comparison with something known or said before: 正如你所说 "just as you said", 正如大家所知. It begins a clause that is a comparison and is followed by a clause saying that the same holds here. 正 "just" + 如 "like".
column4: 正如你所说，学习需要耐心。
column5: 正如你所說，學習需要耐心。
column6: Zhèngrú nǐ suǒ shuō, xuéxí xūyào nàixīn.
column7: Just as you said, learning takes patience.
column9: Just as, introducing a comparison with something known or said before: 正如你所說 "just as you said", 正如大家所知. It begins a clause that is a comparison and is followed by a clause saying that the same holds here. 正 "just" + 如 "like".

column3: Along with, as, in step with a change: 随着时间的推移 "as time goes by", 随着经济的发展 "with economic development". It introduces a change that happens together with another, and the second clause says what follows. It cannot take a person to follow, unlike 跟着.
column4: 随着生活水平的提高，人们越来越注意健康。
column5: 隨著生活水平的提高，人們越來越注意健康。
column6: Suízhe shēnghuó shuǐpíng de tígāo, rénmen yuè lái yuè zhùyì jiànkāng.
column7: As living standards rise, people pay more and more attention to health.
column9: Along with, as, in step with a change: 隨著時間的推移 "as time goes by", 隨著經濟的發展 "with economic development". It introduces a change that happens together with another, and the second clause says what follows. It cannot take a person to follow, unlike 跟著.

column3: Out of, from a motive: 出于好心 "out of good intentions", 出于礼貌 "out of politeness", 出于安全考虑. The motive follows 出于 and the action follows. It names the reason behind a deed, in a written style. 出 "come out" + 于 "from".
column6: Tā chūyú lǐmào, méiyǒu jùjué.
column7: Out of politeness, he did not refuse.
column9: Out of, from a motive: 出於好心 "out of good intentions", 出於禮貌 "out of politeness", 出於安全考慮. The motive follows 出於 and the action follows. It names the reason behind a deed, in a written style. 出 "come out" + 於 "from".

column3: To base on, and the basis itself: 依据法律 "according to the law", 没有依据 "without grounds", 科学依据 "scientific basis". As a verb it takes an object, like 根据; as a noun it is "evidence". 依 "rely on" + 据 "according to".
column4: 法官依据法律作出了判决。
column5: 法官依據法律作出了判決。
column6: Fǎguān yījù fǎlǜ zuòchū le pànjué.
column7: The judge made the ruling on the basis of the law.
column9: To base on, and the basis itself: 依據法律 "according to the law", 沒有依據 "without grounds", 科學依據 "scientific basis". As a verb it takes an object, like 根據; as a noun it is "evidence". 依 "rely on" + 據 "according to".

column3: According to, in line with a rule, plan or standard: 依照规定 "according to the regulations", 依照程序 "following the procedure". It is stricter than 按照, since the standard must be followed. 照 means "follow, match".
column6: Qǐng yīzhào shuōmíngshū ānzhuāng.
column7: Please install it in accordance with the instructions.
column9: According to, in line with a rule, plan or standard: 依照規定 "according to the regulations", 依照程序 "following the procedure". It is stricter than 按照, since the standard must be followed. 照 means "follow, match".

column3: To rely on, to go by, or "on the basis of": 凭票入场 "enter with a ticket", 凭什么 "on what grounds?", 凭本事吃饭 "live by one's skill". 凭什么 is also the spoken way to protest. It is also a verb meaning to lean on: 凭窗远望. Learn the pattern 凭 + the thing relied on + verb.
column4: 进入景区需要凭票入场。
column5: 進入景區需要憑票入場。
column6: Jìnrù jǐngqū xūyào píng piào rù chǎng.
column7: You need a ticket to get into the scenic area.
column9: To rely on, to go by, or "on the basis of": 憑票入場 "enter with a ticket", 憑什麼 "on what grounds?", 憑本事吃飯 "live by one's skill". 憑什麼 is also the spoken way to protest. It is also a verb meaning to lean on: 憑窗遠望. Learn the pattern 憑 + the thing relied on + verb.

column3: To take as the main thing, to be mainly: 以…为主 "be mainly…", 以学习为主 "study is the main thing", 以中餐为主. It is always in the pattern 以 A 为主, with A as the main part. 为 is read wei2 here.
column4: 我们公司的客户以年轻人为主。
column5: 我們公司的客戶以年輕人為主。
column6: Wǒmen gōngsī de kèhù yǐ niánqīngrén wéizhǔ.
column7: Our company's customers are mainly young people.
column9: To take as the main thing, to be mainly: 以…為主 "be mainly…", 以學習為主 "study is the main thing", 以中餐為主. It is always in the pattern 以 A 為主, with A as the main part. 為 is read wei2 here.

column3: Up to, until, the limit of a time or stage: 到今天为止 "up to today", 到目前为止 "so far", 今天就到这里为止 "that's all for today". It always follows a time phrase starting with 到 or 至, and says that a state lasts up to that point.
column4: 到目前为止，我已经学了五百个汉字。
column5: 到目前為止，我已經學了五百個漢字。
column6: Dào mùqián wéizhǐ, wǒ yǐjīng xué le wǔbǎi ge Hànzì.
column7: Up to now, I have learned five hundred characters.
column9: Up to, until, the limit of a time or stage: 到今天為止 "up to today", 到目前為止 "so far", 今天就到這裡為止 "that's all for today". It always follows a time phrase starting with 到 or 至, and says that a state lasts up to that point.

column3: Lasting for, with a set time limit: 为期三天 "lasting three days", 为期一年的课程. It is followed by the length of time and works as a predicate before a noun or at the beginning of a clause. It is for events with a fixed duration, and is written.
column6: Zhè cì péixùn wéiqī yī zhōu.
column7: This training lasts one week.
column9: Lasting for, with a set time limit: 為期三天 "lasting three days", 為期一年的課程. It is followed by the length of time and works as a predicate before a noun or at the beginning of a clause. It is for events with a fixed duration, and is written.

column3: To be used for or applied to: 用于教学 "used for teaching", 用于治疗 "used in treatment", 这种技术用于… The use or the field follows. It is a passive-like, written pattern, and 用在 is the spoken one. 用 "use" + 于 "for".
column4: 这种材料主要用于建筑。
column5: 這種材料主要用於建築。
column6: Zhè zhǒng cáiliào zhǔyào yòngyú jiànzhù.
column7: This material is mainly used in construction.
column9: To be used for or applied to: 用於教學 "used for teaching", 用於治療 "used in treatment", 這種技術用於… The use or the field follows. It is a passive-like, written pattern, and 用在 is the spoken one. 用 "use" + 於 "for".

column3: To be used for, followed by a verb for the purpose: 用来写字 "used for writing", 用来做饭 "used for cooking". The object being used comes first, as a topic: 这把刀用来切肉. After 用来 comes a verb, not a noun, which is the difference from 用于.
column4: 这把刀是用来切水果的。
column5: 這把刀是用來切水果的。
column6: Zhè bǎ dāo shì yònglái qiē shuǐguǒ de.
column7: This knife is used for cutting fruit.
column9: To be used for, followed by a verb for the purpose: 用來寫字 "used for writing", 用來做飯 "used for cooking". The object being used comes first, as a topic: 這把刀用來切肉. After 用來 comes a verb, not a noun, which is the difference from 用於.

column3: Easy to, convenient for doing: 便于携带 "easy to carry", 便于管理 "easy to manage", 便于使用. A verb follows it, and the pattern states the advantage of the thing. It is formal and common in descriptions of products. 便 "convenient" + 于 "for".
column6: Zhè zhǒng bāo hěn qīng, biànyú xiédài.
column7: This kind of bag is light and easy to carry.
column9: Easy to, convenient for doing: 便於攜帶 "easy to carry", 便於管理 "easy to manage", 便於使用. A verb follows it, and the pattern states the advantage of the thing. It is formal and common in descriptions of products. 便 "convenient" + 於 "for".

column3: To be beneficial for: 有利于健康 "good for health", 有利于发展, 不利于 as the opposite. The thing helped comes after it, and it can be a noun or a verb phrase. 有利 "advantageous" + 于 "for". It is more formal than 对…有好处.
column4: 多喝水有利于身体健康。
column5: 多喝水有利於身體健康。
column6: Duō hē shuǐ yǒulìyú shēntǐ jiànkāng.
column7: Drinking more water is good for your health.
column9: To be beneficial for: 有利於健康 "good for health", 有利於發展, 不利於 as the opposite. The thing helped comes after it, and it can be a noun or a verb phrase. 有利 "advantageous" + 於 "for". It is more formal than 對…有好處.

column3: A motive or the reason behind an action: 学习动机 "motivation to study", 犯罪动机 "motive for a crime", 动机不纯 "impure motive". 动 "move, act" + 机 "opportunity, mechanism". It sounds more serious than 目的 and often shows up in talk of behavior.
column4: 他的动机是想帮助别人。
column5: 他的動機是想幫助別人。
column6: Tā de dòngjī shì xiǎng bāngzhù biéren.
column7: His motive was to help others.
column9: A motive or the reason behind an action: 學習動機 "motivation to study", 犯罪動機 "motive for a crime", 動機不純 "impure motive". 動 "move, act" + 機 "opportunity, mechanism". It sounds more serious than 目的 and often shows up in talk of behavior.

column3: To try or attempt, often without success, in a written style: 试图逃跑 "try to escape", 试图解释 "attempt to explain". It is followed by a verb and suggests a plan whose result is uncertain. 试 "try" + 图 "plan, aim". It is more formal than 想 or 试着.
column4: 他试图说服父母，但没有成功。
column5: 他試圖說服父母，但沒有成功。
column6: Tā shìtú shuōfú fùmǔ, dàn méiyǒu chénggōng.
column7: He tried to persuade his parents but did not succeed.
column9: To try or attempt, often without success, in a written style: 試圖逃跑 "try to escape", 試圖解釋 "attempt to explain". It is followed by a verb and suggests a plan whose result is uncertain. 試 "try" + 圖 "plan, aim". It is more formal than 想 or 試著.

column3: A plan on a large scale, and to plan: 城市规划 "urban planning", 职业规划 "career planning", 规划未来. It is longer-range and more systematic than 计划. 规 "rule, regulate" + 划 "mark out", read hua4 here.
column4: 他正在认真规划自己的未来。
column5: 他正在認真規劃自己的未來。
column6: Tā zhèngzài rènzhēn guīhuà zìjǐ de wèilái.
column7: He is carefully planning his future.
column9: A plan on a large scale, and to plan: 城市規劃 "urban planning", 職業規劃 "career planning", 規劃未來. It is longer-range and more systematic than 計劃. 規 "rule, regulate" + 劃 "mark out", read hua4 here.

column3: To seek something such as help, a solution or a way out, in a formal manner: 寻求帮助 "seek help", 寻求答案 "look for an answer", 寻求支持. It is for something abstract; for objects use 寻找. 寻 "look for" + 求 "seek".
column4: 遇到困难时，要学会寻求帮助。
column5: 遇到困難時，要學會尋求幫助。
column6: Yùdào kùnnan shí, yào xuéhuì xúnqiú bāngzhù.
column7: When you run into difficulty, you should learn to ask for help.
column9: To seek something such as help, a solution or a way out, in a formal manner: 尋求幫助 "seek help", 尋求答案 "look for an answer", 尋求支持. It is for something abstract; for objects use 尋找. 尋 "look for" + 求 "seek".

column3: A means or a method of reaching a goal, often with a hint of tricks: 采取手段 "adopt measures", 不择手段 "by any means", 技术手段 "technical means". The context decides whether it is neutral or negative. 手 "hand" + 段 "section".
column4: 他想用别的手段解决问题。
column5: 他想用別的手段解決問題。
column6: Tā xiǎng yòng bié de shǒuduàn jiějué wèntí.
column7: He wants to solve the problem by other means.
column9: A means or a method of reaching a goal, often with a hint of tricks: 採取手段 "adopt measures", 不擇手段 "by any means", 技術手段 "technical means". The context decides whether it is neutral or negative. 手 "hand" + 段 "section".

column3: A technique or a way of working, especially in art, writing and crime: 艺术手法 "artistic technique", 写作手法 "writing technique", 作案手法 "method of committing a crime". It is about style and manner more than about the result. 手 "hand" + 法 "way".
column4: 这位作家的写作手法很特别。
column5: 這位作家的寫作手法很特別。
column6: Zhè wèi zuòjiā de xiězuò shǒufǎ hěn tèbié.
column7: This writer's way of writing is very distinctive.
column9: A technique or a way of working, especially in art, writing and crime: 藝術手法 "artistic technique", 寫作手法 "writing technique", 作案手法 "method of committing a crime". It is about style and manner more than about the result. 手 "hand" + 法 "way".

column3: To break through a barrier or limit, literally or figuratively, and a breakthrough: 突破记录 "break a record", 突破难关 "get past a difficulty", 取得突破. It suits records, bottlenecks and defenses. 突 "burst" + 破 "break".
column4: 这位运动员突破了世界纪录。
column5: 這位運動員突破了世界紀錄。
column6: Zhè wèi yùndòngyuán tūpò le shìjiè jìlù.
column7: This athlete broke the world record.
column9: To break through a barrier or limit, literally or figuratively, and a breakthrough: 突破記錄 "break a record", 突破難關 "get past a difficulty", 取得突破. It suits records, bottlenecks and defenses. 突 "burst" + 破 "break".

column3: To surpass or go beyond a limit, a rival or one's former self: 超越自我 "surpass oneself", 超越极限 "go beyond limits", 超越时代. It is more figurative and positive than 超过, and the object is often abstract. 超 "exceed" + 越 "cross over".
column4: 他每天都在努力超越昨天的自己。
column5: 他每天都在努力超越昨天的自己。
column6: Tā měi tiān dōu zài nǔlì chāoyuè zuótiān de zìjǐ.
column7: Every day he works hard to surpass his self of yesterday.
column9: To surpass or go beyond a limit, a rival or one's former self: 超越自我 "surpass oneself", 超越極限 "go beyond limits", 超越時代. It is more figurative and positive than 超過, and the object is often abstract. 超 "exceed" + 越 "cross over".

column3: To start up a machine or a program, and figuratively to launch a plan: 启动电脑 "start the computer", 启动项目 "launch a project", 启动仪式 "launching ceremony". 启 "open" + 动 "move". It is the word for the start of something that then keeps going.
column4: 我按了一下按钮，机器就启动了。
column5: 我按了一下按鈕，機器就啟動了。
column6: Wǒ àn le yīxià ànniǔ, jīqì jiù qǐdòng le.
column7: I pressed the button and the machine started up.
column9: To start up a machine or a program, and figuratively to launch a plan: 啟動電腦 "start the computer", 啟動項目 "launch a project", 啟動儀式 "launching ceremony". 啟 "open" + 動 "move". It is the word for the start of something that then keeps going.

column3: To carry out a plan or policy in practice, and to make sure of details: 落实政策 "implement a policy", 落实责任 "pin down responsibility", 还没落实 "not yet settled". It means turning words into action, so it goes with plans, policies and tasks. 落 "fall, land" + 实 "real".
column4: 这个计划还需要具体落实。
column5: 這個計畫還需要具體落實。
column6: Zhège jìhuà hái xūyào jùtǐ luòshí.
column7: This plan still needs to be carried out in concrete terms.
column9: To carry out a plan or policy in practice, and to make sure of details: 落實政策 "implement a policy", 落實責任 "pin down responsibility", 還沒落實 "not yet settled". It means turning words into action, so it goes with plans, policies and tasks. 落 "fall, land" + 實 "real".

column3: To establish firmly something such as a system, a goal or a position: 确立目标 "set a goal", 确立地位 "establish one's position", 确立关系. The object is abstract, and the word suggests it is settled for good. 确 "firm" + 立 "set up".
column4: 我们已经确立了今年的目标。
column5: 我們已經確立了今年的目標。
column6: Wǒmen yǐjīng quèlì le jīnnián de mùbiāo.
column7: We have already established this year's goals.
column9: To establish firmly something such as a system, a goal or a position: 確立目標 "set a goal", 確立地位 "establish one's position", 確立關係. The object is abstract, and the word suggests it is settled for good. 確 "firm" + 立 "set up".

column3: To control or keep within bounds: 控制情绪 "control one's emotions", 控制体重 "keep one's weight in check", 失去控制 "lose control". It is used for feelings, spread, size and machines. 控 "control" + 制 "restrain".
column4: 他努力控制自己的情绪。
column5: 他努力控制自己的情緒。
column6: Tā nǔlì kòngzhì zìjǐ de qíngxù.
column7: He tries hard to control his emotions.
column9: To control or keep within bounds: 控制情緒 "control one's emotions", 控制體重 "keep one's weight in check", 失去控制 "lose control". It is used for feelings, spread, size and machines. 控 "control" + 制 "restrain".
